News.title: Natalie Harp: Backstory and trigger for executive assistant's devotion to Donald Trump
News.content:
Among the fascinating details in Donald Trump's weird Turkey plane swap caper was who he took with him on the secret jet out of Ankara.

You could pretty much understand Pete Hegseth being on Trump's plane during the sneaky escape - although the concept of being in an enclosed metal tube with him for several hours doesn't bear thinking about.

But also in this select entourage was a 35-year-old blonde woman named Natalie.

Also known as "the human printer", Natalie Harp is Donald Trump's executive assistant. She gained that nickname because of her tendency to print out papers for Trump - often flattering news stories - at any time of the day or night.

‌



View 3 Images Natalie is pictured at a bill signing in the Oval Office (Image: Getty Images)

During a rally in Atlanta over the weekend, Democrat Senator Jon Ossoff - whom many (including me) have tipped as a future presidential candidate - accused Trump of wanting to "travel with Natalie" rather than of of perform his Presidential duties. The rather pointed remark has ignited a flurry of interest in Harp, and what exactly her relationship with Trump is.

She's an exceptionally visible member of the administration despite not having a public-facing role - simply because she is almost always where Trump is. She's always somewhere in the background, often with an armful of A4 printouts, neatly paper clipped together and ready to deploy.

‌



She was previously a presenter for One America News Network, a right-wing propaganda outlet, where she would often end her show either with a bible verse ...or a quote from Trump, introducing his outbursts as if he were some kind of divine prophet: "Remember what Trump said..."

After coming on Trump's radar by praising him over legislation he championed that she said had allowed her to get experimental treatment for bone cancer, she joined his 2024 campaign as an aide. And from there she was hired by the administration as an executive assistant to the President.

The New York Times' Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan included fascinating nuggets about her character in their book Regime Change, which came out in June, and in an earlier article for the Times. They report that she left "intimate letters" to Trump during the campaign. "You are all that matters to me," she's said to have written.

"I don't ever want to let you down...I want to bring you joy."

‌



The Secret Service were, by all accounts, perturbed by the letters, left for him in his "personal spaces".

But beyond her obvious proximity to Trump, a lot of the most fascinating tales of her closeness with the President are the stuff of legend - and are mostly recounted second-hand or through unnamed sources.

There's the tale of her being so eager to be close to Trump that when his campaign team moved from Palm Beach to his golf club at Bedminster, New Jersey in 2023, and she was not given a room - she set up a bed in the the women's locker room and spent several months sleeping there.

There are varying claims about how much access she has to his social media accounts - and which of his more contentious posts she has been involved in.

‌



Moreover, there are claims that she has access to other of his communications - texts and emails.

And Trump, early in his second term, is said to have told his team Natalie was "the only one who loved him as much as his wife and his kids."

To get more stories, gossip and analysis like this in your inbox every week, 

View 3 Images

‌



Click here to sign up

Kim Jong chill

North Korea has 57 nukes, Trump declared on Wednesday, as he led journalists on a tour of the construction site that is the White House South Lawn.

Trump is having a helipad installed on the lawn because the new Marine Ones keep scorching the grass. When the installation was first underway, it followed the camber of the hill atop which is the White House. Trump didn't like that, it was reported at the time, because he wanted it level with the horizon. And during his tour of the site yesterday, he let slip that another reason he wanted it flat was so he could host cocktail parties on the landing pad.

He later proudly declared that the new grass to be laid on the lawn had been supplied for free by the Scotts Miracle Gro company, a donor to his campaign and Super PAC. Scotts also distributes Roundup, and has benefited from a Trump-signed executive order that declared such herbicides "critical to US national and economic security".

‌



Anyway, somewhere between admitting to a huge conflict of interest and declaring himself "really good at flagpoles", Trump put a number on Kim Jong-un's nuclear arsenal. Which he's almost certainly not supposed to say out loud in front of a bunch of contractors and journalists, and definitely when he's being beamed live to TVs and computers around the world.

Trump has been back on his "little Rocket Man" love-in this week. He posted a picture of him and Kim taken during his first term - back when a President alienating America's natural allies while cosying up to its enemies was a novel event.

Then on Sunday night he had a direct pop at South Korea, announcing he would be scaling back American involvement in a series of military drills alongside Seoul, and branding the plans "inappropriate and hostile". Trump later explained that his was partly out of revenge for South Korea refusing to help with the war on Iran. Which is not an unreasonable position for South Korea to take, given they get 60% of their oil through the Strait of Hormuz.

But there we have it - we have a President proudly, or at least absent-mindedly admitting to huge conflicts of interest, cosying up to one of the world's most reviled dictators and wanting to host cocktail parties on the White House helipad all on the same day. Now, what else has been going on...

‌



High steaks

Susie Wiles, Donald Trump's chief of staff, has been spotted meeting with a potential candidate to replace Karoline Leavitt as mouthpiece of the administration.

She reportedly sat down for a spot of dinner with Scott Jennings - which does not surprise me. He's a MAGA blowhard who mostly appears on CNN panel shows, and has an apparently limitless appetite for saying whatever the President might want him to say, no matter how preposterous or offensive it is.

No surprise he's being sounded out for the Press Secretary vacancy, then. What did surprise me was their choice of dinner venue.

Morton's is a longtime staple of Washington's steakhouse scene, but its main differentiator is the long outdoor terrace where people go to smoke cigars.

‌



Point is, there are many classier restaurants in the Capital, and eateries that are more MAGA friendly than catering to cigar-chomping lobbyists and congressmen.

Not to mention there are many more private places to eat. In fact, I'd argue Morton's is probably one of the more surveilled rooms in Washington DC - both by nosey senators, and in the 2019 case of Democrat Senator Bob Menendez, the FBI. (He'd taken to meeting Egyptian officials there, from whom he accepted bribes, a court later heard).

An odd choice of venue for a quiet chat.

News.title: Under-15s have been banned from travelling on buses alone at night across Stoke-on-Trent
News.content:
Under-15s have been banned from travelling on buses alone at night across Stoke-on-Trent

A total of 32 bus services in Stoke-on-Trent, Staffordshire, are affected by the new evening restriction, introduced following growing concerns over anti-social behaviour involving youngsters

View 2 Images Teenagers are pictured on a bus (file image) (Image: Getty Images)

Under-15s have been banned from travelling alone on some buses in Stoke-on-Trent after 6pm.

‌



The evening restriction was introduced following a rise in anti-social behaviour, meaning children under 15 can only travel on services to and from Hanley Bus Station if accompanied by an adult.

‌



The ban came into force on Friday and was approved by the Department for Transport following discussions with Staffordshire Police and Stoke-on-Trent City Council.

‌



Rebecca Arrowsmith, general manager of First Bus in the area, said there had been increased incidents of anti-social behaviour at the bus station and on board services.

A total of 32 services across the Potteries are affected, although drivers have been told to “exercise their discretion” if there are concerns about an unaccompanied child’s safety.

A66 Middlesbrough crash: Andy Burnham leads tributes to police officers killed on active duty READ MORE :

View 2 Images Buses in Stoke, including those to Kidsgrove, are going to change (Image: Supplied)

‌



Rebecca said: “The safety of our staff and customers is always our number one priority and we will always take steps to ensure everyone on board can travel in comfort and without nuisance.

"This measure has the full support of the council and will be kept under daily review. We hope to be able to end the restriction as soon as possible.”

The temporary measure comes while children aged five to 15 can travel on most bus services in England for free as part of a government scheme due to run until the end of August.

Article continues below

Simon Mathieson, the firm’s regional director for the East and Midlands, said the decision had been made “regrettably” and the company hoped to lift the restriction once the free bus travel offer ends.

He told BBC Radio Stoke: “We have seen a large uptake in the area for children using this scheme, which is great. Buses are important, buses matter. We know people like to travel by bus. Obviously, the weather has been fantastic, with people getting out and about.

“We’ve seen good use of this scheme, but we just need people to act sensibly when they’re on the bus and in the bus station.”

News.title: Young children shown hunted deer corpse in disturbing drone footage
News.content:
Young children shown hunted deer corpse in disturbing drone footage

WARNING: GRAPHIC CONTENT. EXCLUSIVE: The Mirror has seen drone footage from a deer hunt in Somerset earlier this year, which was being monitored by animal rights group the League Against Cruel Sports

Andy Burnham urged to crack down on 'barbaric' deer hunts

Campaigners have renewed calls for a crackdown on hunting after drone footage showed ­children – including a baby – being encouraged to look at a stag’s bloody corpse.

‌



The clip shows a group examining the body of a young stag in the back of a vehicle after a hunt in Somerset earlier this year. The League Against Cruel Sports and North Dorset Hunt Saboteurs monitored the hunt.

‌



The League is now calling on Andy Burnham to strengthen laws on hunting – League chief executive Emma Slawinski explained: “It’s shocking to see adults trying to normalise this cruel and sickening activity with kids, showing them the victims of a hunt.

‌



View Image Andy Burnham has been urged to crack down on deer hunts (Image: Getty Images)

“This harrowing footage shows why we are calling on the Prime Minister to strengthen hunting laws to prevent this barbaric blood sport from still taking place. We are calling for the removal of the exemptions in the Hunting Act.

“[They] are being exploited by the deer hunts to chase stags and hinds for many miles before shooting them.

‌



“The ‘research and observation’ and ‘rescue of a wild mammal’ exemptions are enabling deer hunts in Somerset and Devon to kill wildlife and get away with barbaric behaviour.”

There is no suggestion the hunters in the video acted illegally. Deer hunting is legal within seasonal rules, i.e mature stags may be hunted from early August to October’s end, young stags in March and April and hinds November to early March.

A Countryside Alliance spokesman said: “The Devon and Somerset staghounds are integral to the management of the deer on Exmoor. Hundreds of thousands of deer are culled in the UK every year and go into the food chain to provide healthy wild meat.”

Article continues below

Defra said: “Causing unnecessary suffering to an animal is an offence, and we are committed to upholding the UK’s high standards of animal welfare.”

But it added that sustainable shooting had an important role in rural communities, and that it would work with them to preserve the countryside, wildlife and rural ways of life.

Earlier this year, the government ran a consultation on banning trail hunting, amid fears it was used as a cover to genuinely chase and kill foxes. Defra is still analysing the responses.

News.title: Teenage girl dies after being struck by vehicles near footbridge on M20 in Kent
News.content:
Teenage girl dies after being struck by vehicles near footbridge on M20 in Kent

A teenage girl has died after being struck by vehicles on the M20 near Aylesford in Kent in the early hours of Saturday

View Image A teenage girl died on the M20 in Kent in the early hours of Saturday (Image: Google Maps)

A teenage girl has died after being struck by vehicles on the M20 in Kent.

Kent Police said officers were called at 3.19am on Saturday following a collision on the coastbound carriageway between Junction 4 (West Malling) and Junction 5 (Aylesford).

The girl, who was on the carriageway near a footbridge close to Teapot Lane in Aylesford, had been "struck by vehicles including a Ford Transit van and a Vauxhall Corsa", the force said.

Officers attended the scene and the girl was sadly pronounced dead. Her next of kin have been informed.

Investigators are appealing for witnesses and dashcam footage, particularly from anyone who travelled through the area between 3.15am and 3.28am and saw a pedestrian in the carriageway.

Article continues below

Motorists with dashcams are also being asked to check their footage for anything that could assist the investigation.

Anyone with relevant information is asked to call 01622 798538 or email sciu.td@kent.police.uk, quoting reference 46/138541/26. Dashcam footage can be uploaded to the force's public portal here.

News.title: A66 Middlesbrough crash: Andy Burnham leads tributes to police officers killed on active duty
News.content:
A66 Middlesbrough crash: Andy Burnham leads tributes to police officers killed on active duty

Andy Burnham has paid tribute after seven people - including serving police officers PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough - were killed when a wrong-way car collided with a marked police vehicle

Cleveland Police issue statement following tragic A66 crash

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has led tributes after seven people - including two serving police officers - were killed in a horror crash.

‌



The officers were on active duty when their marked police vehicle collided with a Volkswagen Passat travelling the wrong way along the A66 in the early hours of Saturday morning. The officers have since been named as PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough.

‌



The Prime Minister said: “Devastated to hear that two police officers have lost their lives while on duty in Cleveland this morning, as well as five members of the public.

‌



“My thoughts are with the families and loved ones of everyone involved, and with everyone at Cleveland Police. Thank you to the emergency services responding in incredibly difficult circumstances.

“I would urge people to avoid speculation at this time.”

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood also paid tribute, she said: “A devastating incident in Teesside this morning in which seven people have died, including two police officers. Cleveland police have my support as they work to identify all those involved. Police officers put their own safety on the line to protect their communities every single day. The two officers were on active duty, serving the people of Cleveland.

‌



“My thoughts are with all those affected, their families, friends, the emergency services who attended the scene and the wider police family.”

View 3 Images A large police presence remains at the scene (Image: Iain Buist/Newcastle Chronicle)

The tragedy unfolded in South Bank, near Middlesbrough, at around 3.39am. Five members of the public travelling in the Passat were also killed and everyone in both vehicles was pronounced dead at the scene.

‌



A major emergency response was launched following the collision, with the North East Ambulance Service sending 14 resources to the scene, including ambulance crews, a specialist paramedic and its Hazardous Area Response Team.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the crash. The watchdog said it understands Cleveland Police had sighted a suspicious vehicle and a pursuit began before the Passat travelled onto the A66 and collided with the police car.

The pursuit had been abandoned before the crash and the police vehicle involved in the collision was not part of the pursuit and was just travelling in the area, according to the BBC

‌



View 3 Images The road has remained closed

Work is reportedly still ongoing to formally identify everyone who was inside the Passat. Families of those who have been identified have been informed and are receiving specialist support.

The ambulance service said: “Sadly despite the best efforts of everyone attending, a number of patients died at the scene. We send condolences to all of those affected by such a tragic event and thank everyone for all they did to help.”

‌



View 3 Images Cleveland Police Chief Constable Victoria Fuller spoke to reporters (Image: Iain Buist/Newcastle Chronicle)

The deaths of the two officers have left colleagues at Cleveland Police devastated. Lauren Somerville, Chair of Cleveland Police Federation, said: “Words cannot describe the pain the Cleveland Police Family are feeling today. Our colleagues who should have been going home to their loved ones at the end of their shifts are not. And that is just unfathomable.

“Cleveland Police Federation will be offering full support to our fallen colleagues families and they have all of our love and care at this time. When the time is right we will pay full tribute to our brave colleagues. But we can assure that their sacrifice will never be forgotten.”

‌



Chief Constable Victoria Fuller said: “First and foremost, our thoughts are with the families of everyone involved in today’s incident. No one should leave their home and not return safely, including police officers serving their communities and protecting the people of Cleveland.

“This tragic incident will be felt across Cleveland, within our communities and throughout the entire policing family. We are providing specialist support to all families involved at this extremely difficult time.

“The investigation has been referred to the IOPC, which is the standard approach when a death occurs following police contact. We will cooperate fully with their investigation. While this investigation takes place, we strongly urge people to avoid speculation.”

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Police and Crime Commissioner Matt Storey said there were few words that could bring comfort to the families, friends and colleagues of the seven people who died. He added: “Our thoughts are with everyone affected and with those who are continuing to come to terms with this unimaginable loss, including colleagues at Cleveland Police, who will feel the profound loss of two of their serving officers.

“On behalf of everyone at the Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner and the people of Cleveland, I extend our deepest condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of all seven people who lost their lives.

Article continues below

“I also give my sincere thanks to the staff from all our emergency services who responded to, and are continuing to manage, this devastating incident.”

News.title: TikTok in $400m settlement with US after being accused of violating children's privacy law
News.content:
TikTok in $400m settlement with US after being accused of violating children's privacy law

TikTok will pay sum to the US Department of Justice to end the 2024 lawsuit, which focused on allegations TikTok and China-based parent firm ByteDance broke federal law

View 3 Images US Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward Jr said: 'This settlement is a major victory for American children and parents.' (Image: Getty Images)

Social media giant TikTok has reached a settlement worth nearly £300million with the US after being accused of violating children’s privacy laws.

‌



TikTok will pay $400m (£293m) to the US Department of Justice [DOJ] to end the 2024 lawsuit. The legal action focused on allegations TikTok and China-based parent firm ByteDance broke a federal law requiring child-oriented apps and websites to get parental consent before collecting personal information of kids under 13. It also says the companies failed to honour requests from parents who wanted their children's accounts deleted, and chose not to delete accounts even when the firms knew they belonged to kids under 13.

‌



View 3 Images TikTok will fork out $300m immediately and another $100m after an order vacates an earlier consent decree against its predecessor company, Musical.ly, the DOJ said on Friday (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Meta trial begins as company accused of preying on vulnerability of young brains READ MORE :

Meta child safety trial could have 'astronomical' global impact for Facebook and Instagram READ MORE :

TikTok will fork out $300m (£220m) immediately and another $100m (£73m) after an order vacates an earlier consent decree against its predecessor company, Musical.ly, the DOJ said on Friday. US Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward Jr said: "This settlement is a major victory for American children and parents.”

He added: "The Department's priority is ensuring that children are protected online and that companies entrusted with their personal information meet their legal obligations. This resolution secures a substantial recovery while reinforcing the protections that families expect and deserve."

Article continues below

View 3 Images The US government said TikTok had 'implemented extensive measures designed to strengthen safeguards for younger users, improve age-related controls, and enhance parental oversight' (Image: PA)

TikTok has undergone big changes since the DOJ’s lawsuit in 2024, most notably in the ownership structure of its US arm. The US government said TikTok had “implemented extensive measures designed to strengthen safeguards for younger users, improve age-related controls, and enhance parental oversight”. TikTok did not immediately comment.

The settlement comes as social media companies face an avalanche of lawsuits over children's safety and privacy and a growing number of countries are banning young kids and teens from social media apps.

News.title: Tracker shows Reform loses newly-elected councillor every three days as Farage troubles mount
News.content:
Tracker shows Reform loses newly-elected councillor every three days as Farage troubles mount

EXCLUSIVE: A new online tracker by campaign group Best For Britain shows 35 newly-elected Reform councillors have quit or been suspended since May as the group's chief say it would 'struggle to run a bath'

View 4 Images A new online tracker shows how many new councillors Reform has lost since May (Image: James Manning/PA Wire)

Reform UK is losing a councillor every three days on average as critics claim Nigel Farage ’s party would “struggle to run a bath”.

‌



A new resignation and defection tracker reveals 35 newly-elected representatives have resigned or been suspended since local elections in May. It comes as a public rupture in the national party raises fresh questions about Mr Farage's ability to lead a team that could run the country.

‌



The online tool has been released days after a leaked training video said the biggest threat the party faces is "people in it and itself".

‌



Launching the tracker, which will be updated with each new resignation or suspension, Best For Britain’s chief executive Naomi Smith told The Mirror: “Whether they've resigned, been suspended, or were simply never up to the job, Reform UK have been shedding councillors ever since May.

"So much for the tidal wave about to break over British politics, this is a party that would struggle to run a bath. They're now losing a councillor every three days.

Reform civil war erupts as top supporter suspended after scathing Farage and Yusuf criticism READ MORE :

View 4 Images Reform councillor Dave Rowan was suspended over allegations his social media account called for John Bercow to be hanged (Image: Kirklees Council)

‌



"Little wonder Reform UK themselves have warned activists their own officials are the 'biggest threat' the party faces. On this evidence, it's hard to disagree.”

Names on Best For Britain's tracker include Alex Clarke, who stepped down from South Tyneside Council in June, saying he was mis-sold the role and thought he would only need to attend six meetings a year.

He said: "I wanted to resign because I was sold [the councillor position] under false pretences. It was only after the election that the reality of what the position entailed made itself apparent, to which I was immediately overwhelmed and felt trapped."

‌



And earlier this month, Plymouth councillor Carol Ney, who only joined Reform UK in April, returned to being an independent, saying she was “unable to support the direction of the party”.

Rhys Carr, who quit as a Reform UK councillor in Wakefield to sit as an independent in June. He wrote on social media: "It has become clear that local issues are not prioritised, and that is simply not what I stood for when I was elected."

The tracker, based on information in the public domain, shows five councillors are currently suspended having first been elected in May. These include Billy Burke, of Trafford Council, who was charged with possession of an offensive weapon in June.

‌



View 4 Images Tim Montgomerie, centre, was suspended this week after criticising Nigel Farage and Zia Yusuf (Image: reformparty_uk/x)

Also suspended is Sunderland City councillor Glenn Gibbins, 66, who has been charged with posting a grossly offensive comment about Nigerians on social media. And the list includes Robin Perry of Walsall Council, who was suspended over claims he made unfounded allegations against a fellow Reform councillor. He said he would appeal, and told the BBC: "Nationally, I agree with the policies. Locally, it's like Mussolini's government."

This was a reference to Italian far-right leader Benito Mussolini, who aligned his country with Nazi Germany in World War Two. Earlier this month councillor Dave Rowan was suspended in Kirklees after historic social media posts appeared to show him calling for ex-Commons Speaker John Bercow to be hanged.

‌



And Birmingham's Rebecca Waters was kicked out after voting for a Lib Dem rather than a member of her own party in a leadership contest in July.

Best For Britain's online tracker states: "Reform UK wants power. But the party is haemorrhaging the people it recruits, with representatives resigning, being suspended or quitting Nigel Farage's outfit.

"Reform UK then mops up failed Conservatives to fill the gaps in its ranks. Much of this goes unreported - even though the pattern is the story."

‌



The site also lists 180 elected politicians and former MPs who have defected from the Tories to Reform - including the party's chief whip, Lee Anderson, who was Conservative deputy chairman under Rishi Sunak.

Tensions at the top of the party were thrown into the spotlight this week when commentator Tim Montgomerie was suspended over a string of critical comments about Mr Farage and home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf.

View 4 Images Best For Britain chief Naomi Smith said Reform is a party 'which would struggle to run a bath' (Image: Best for Britain)

‌



It boiled over when he told a Spectator podcast: "There are a lot of people who are not on speaking terms with Zia, and it's nearly always Zia who initiates this. And it has to end. You cannot behave like a child in politics."

And he questioned Mr Farage's ability to manage the party, posting on social media: "One of the biggest question marks over Nigel Farage's leadership is whether he brings Zia under control."

Mr Montgomerie had previously questioned Mr Farage's response to questions about his undeclared £5million 'gift' from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne. The Reform leader is being investigated by Parliament's standards commissioner over whether it broke rules for MPs.

‌



In July Mr Montgomerie told the BBC: “People do not normally get a £5 million gift, we get a box of chocolates or a bottle of champagne, that’s the sort of gift most people get." And he went on: “I think he has to find better answers to these questions so far, and he will do, because the parliamentary process is now underway and he will have to be open”.

On Thursday Mr Farage's number two, Richard Tice, denied on Thursday that Reform risked being seen as thin-skinned, saying: "We're a fast-growing political party. There'll be a range of views, and sometimes we'll agree, and sometimes we'll have a debate and discussion.

"That's what you do in business. That's what you do in a boardroom. That's what you do when you're brainstorming. But what we've always said is that actually ... when you're having your discussions about those things, in the nicest possible way, as you would in a boardroom or in a brainstorming session in a company, you keep it behind closed doors, and then you go out and sell a great message.

‌



"That's what we're doing."

It comes after a training video leaked to the Byline Times told activists: "The fact is, the biggest threat to Reform is people in it and itself. It’s not the Tories, it’s not Labour, the establishment is going to throw everything at us.

"The biggest chance of things going wrong is stuff like infighting, stuff like people just saying and doing stupid stuff. That’s our biggest risk." It went on to tell them: "Don’t drink and tweet. If there is any doubt, just don’t post it."

Article continues below

The Mirror has approached Reform UK for comment about Best For Britain's tracker.

News.title: Edgware Road incident: Station closed as police close off huge area in London
News.content:
Police officers seen outside Edgware Road Tube station in London

Edgware Road Tube station was closed on Friday night following a police incident, with officers seen swarming the busy north-west London street

Edgware Road incident: Station closed as police close off huge area in London

A huge police cordon was in place outside the Tube station on Edgware Road, north-west London, on Friday night, with part of the street also closed off.

Videos shared on social media showed multiple police vehicles and other emergency crews outside the underground station.

Transport for London (TfL) said on its website: "This station is closed while police respond to an incident. Tickets are being accepted on London Buses." The station has since reopened.

The Mirror has contacted the Metropolitan Police for further information.

News.title: Two police officers among seven killed in wrong-way car crash
News.content:
Seven people including two police officers have been killed in a crash with a car driving the wrong way down a dual-carriageway following a pursuit.

A Volkswagen Passat with five occupants said to be in their late teens struck an oncoming marked Cleveland Police vehicle on the A66 near Middlesbrough at about 03:39 BST.

The BBC understands a pursuit of the car had been called off before the crash, with the police vehicle just happening to be in the South Bank area. The occupants of both cars were pronounced dead at the scene.

The officers have been named as PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38. Chief Constable Victoria Fuller said they were "brave officers protecting our communities".

She said it was an "incredibly sad day for Cleveland", adding: "No one should leave their home and not return safely.

"These were brave officers protecting our communities and serving our residents who didn't return home to their families at the end of their shift."

News.title: Video appears to show police chase minutes before fatal A66 crash
News.content:
Security camera footage appears to show several police vehicles chasing a car just minutes before a fatal crash that killed seven people, including two police officers, near Middlesbrough.

The clip is thought to have been filmed on Lime Road at 03:36 BST on Saturday morning, around three minutes before a Volkswagen Passat travelling the wrong way on the A66 nearby collided into a marked police vehicle.

The police car involved in the crash was not part of the pursuit, the BBC understands

A police source said the chase had been abandoned before the collision.

News.title: How this 1960s ex-council house is managing to stay cool without air con
News.content:
After five heatwaves and plenty of advice on how to stay safe in what is set to become the UK's hottest summer on record, many people continue to find it a challenge to stay cool - particularly in their homes.

This is perhaps no surprise. More than half of homes, external in the UK are already at risk of overheating and at current rates of climate change this will rise to 92% by 2050 if we do not adapt.

But in south London, on a 35C day, one 1960s ex-council house with no air-conditioning is managing to beat the heat.

Marion Baeli's home is one of many across the UK being adapted for warmer - maybe even 40C - British summers.

News.title: Watch: Moment humanoid robot beats Usain Bolt's 100m record
News.content:
A robot has outperformed humans by running faster than Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record at the World Humanoid Robot Games in China.

The humanoid robot, developed by the Beijing Innovation Centre of Humanoid Robotics, ran the distance in 9.39 seconds at the event.

Eight-time Olympic gold medallist Bolt set the world record for humans in 2009, running 100m in 9.58 seconds.

The robot beat two others including one made by Chinese smartphone maker Honor - which the manufacturer says ran the distance in 9.32 seconds in a test run.

Other events at the robot games, which started on Saturday, include boxing and football, but also household tasks such as folding laundry.

The BBC's China correspondent Laura Bicker reports from Beijing.

News.title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs
News.content:
More new students are choosing to live at home for university this year than in the last nine years, new data shows.

Over 81,000 UK 18-year-olds said in their accepted university application that they intended to live at home this year, according to the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (Ucas) - just over one in three students in that category.

In 2017, it was closer to one in five.

The figures vary across the UK - with 48% of applicants in Scotland intending to live at home, compared with 20% in Wales - but the trend is rising across the board.

Students told the BBC the rising cost of living was a major influence in deciding what to do after school or college.

For friends Beatrice and Amelia, who are from St Helens, Merseyside, the cost of accommodation was a big factor in their decision to live at home while studying.

Both are heading to university in September, but neither will be moving into student accommodation.

News.title: As they return to the UK, Harry and Meghan search for a brand that sticks
News.content:
In late July, the Duchess of Sussex's lifestyle range, called As ever, launched a "rich, vibrant" blackberry spread alongside a softly lit video of her picking the fruit.

A month later, Meghan and her husband Prince Harry are returning to live in the UK just as blackberry season ends. Perhaps we can expect another video soon, shot on these shores.

Or perhaps not, because experts say the Harry and Meghan brand is at a crossroads.

After the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's acrimonious exit from the Royal Family in 2020, the projects marking their fresh start in California - from streaming to signature scents - have mostly failed to find large audiences, and experts say it's unclear where the couple goes from here.

Their return to the UK has surprised many and we don't know their reasons for the switch, but what's clear is that they will not be working royals when they return. So what could they be doing instead?

News.title: GTA 6 leaks - a nightmare or a blip for the biggest video game of the year?
News.content:
Video game journalist Wesley Yin-Poole, director of news at IGN, says the apparent leaks will be tough for the game's developers.

"GTA 6 is an enormous endeavour," says Yin-Poole. "It's being built over the course a decade, essentially, with thousands of people involved.

"To have the game exposed in this way will have been devastating to many people who worked on it."

The group behind the apparent leaks claims to be acting in the interests of players, accusing Rockstar of engaging in anti-consumer practices, such as its decision not to release a disc version of GTA 6 at launch.

Not everyone is convinced about the group's intentions, as each release of new material has invited viewers to send cryptocurrency "donations" to the user uploading them.

Stop Killing Games, which campaigns against all-digital distribution models, criticised the alleged leaks as "destructive" and urged people not to send money to those claiming responsibility.

Yin-Poole says there's "a huge amount of scepticism" about the stated motivation.

"Most people believe this is about money," he says, "it feels like, honestly, the whole 'we're doing this for the gamers' angle is nonsense, and I suspect most people have dismissed it."

So far, two official trailers for GTA 6 have been released, the most recent in May 2025. Since then, ardent fans have leapt on any rumours or apparent clues in official Rockstar posts.

Some famously came up with an elaborate theory, external suggesting an image of the moon included in a promotional post for GTA Online held clues to the release date of GTA 6's first trailer.

"To a certain extent, Rockstar has themselves to blame," says Vermeij. "That's their strategy - and I think it's a good strategy, it's exciting. But the consequence is that every little bit of information, every little event, gets sort of blown out of proportion."

Yin-Poole says while people will likely understand this isn't the way Rockstar had intended GTA6 to be revealed and doesn't show the game in the best light, he believes most will "reserve judgement" about it until they have seen official footage in action, or played it for themselves.

Ultimately, he believes there's little chance the leaks will "derail the potential success of the game".

"GTA 6 will be an unprecedented moment in pop culture history," he says. "So ultimately, this will become a footnote in the history of GTA 6's development."

Vermeij, who has not watched any of the latest leaks, agrees.

"I think it will have no impact at all whatsoever," he says. "People will have forgotten about it by the time the game comes out."

Grand Theft Auto 6 is due to be released on 19 November for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, with a PC release expected at a later date.

News.title: Drugs at their fingertips, intense pressure: Why child stars fall into addiction
News.content:
Hayden Panettiere was 16 when drugs first arrived in her life in Hollywood.

Ahead of a red carpet event for the hit series Heroes, she has said someone on her team handed her a pill to help amp up her energy. The hit sci-fi NBC series had catapulted the teen into a household name - and that brought with it intense pressure and exhaustion she says felt overwhelming.

"Within minutes, a wave of energy washed over me, like I'd just woken up from the most refreshing night's sleep of my life," Panettiere wrote about that pill in her memoir, which was released just months before her death.

She called it "the gateway drug that ushered me toward the good of pharmaceuticals and the downfall of addiction".

The star's sudden death at the age of 36 has placed a renewed focus on her struggles with mental health and substance abuse, and re-ignited a discussion about the pressures of Hollywood on child stars.

The coroner's office in Greenville, South Carolina said crews treated a woman in "cardiac arrest" and her autopsy showed "no signs of trauma".

No cause of death has been released, though additional tests are yet to be completed.

Audio from police dispatchers and crews who responded to the address said they were responding to a "cardiac arrest" and detailed their efforts to resuscitate the woman after a possible "overdose". Panettiere's ex boyfriend, Brian Hickerson - who has admitted to abusing her - and his brother Zack, were with Panettiere when emergency services came, according to a police report.

There is no suggestion of wrongdoing on their part, according to police.

It is not known if drugs or alcohol played a factor in her death, but the US Drug Enforcement Agency is joining an investigation into her death, according to US media reports.

Panettiere is one of many actors who has openly struggled with addiction after exposure to fame at an early age, which addiction experts told the BBC can put people at risk for mental health and substance abuse issues.

It can sometimes seem to the rest of the world that child actors have "everything" at their fingertips - like fame and money, said Lucas Trautman, the medical director of Oxford Treatment Center, an addiction treatment centre in Mississippi.

"But it's important to remember that they were also exposed during a developmental time to many adult aspects of life that the rest of us weren't - including traumatic experiences - and so that gives them unique risk factors for addiction," Trautman said.

Panettiere's death comes after she published a memoir where she discussed at length her issues with addiction, her postpartum depression and the loss of her 28-year-old brother.

Panettiere's decision to publicly share her struggles is worthy of respect, said William Moyers, the vice-president of public affairs for Hazelden Betty Ford, the largest nonprofit addiction treatment provider in the US. But he said the constant public scrutiny she faced may not have allowed her room to address her mental health in private.

"Her entire life from the beginning was centred in the intense public spotlight, and this didn't give Hayden much in the way of a respite," said Moyers, who has been in recovery from an addiction since 1989.

News.title: Vigil held for family who died in sea off Shoreham
News.content:
Alden added: "The way everybody has come together and marked today with this minute's silence, and there were people who met with paddleboards and kayaks over at Kingston Beach as well this morning, it's been a really lovely way to pay to the very sad loss of these lives."

Wesley Horscroft attended on behalf of paddlers in the Kingston beach community.

He said he had originally planned to go out alone and "put some flowers on the water" to honour the family, before he decided to invite others.

"It's kind of grown and a lot of people wanted to turn up to do the same," he said.

He said Saja's death had added an "another layer" to the grief felt in the town.

News.title: Economic adviser O'Neill rules out government job but backs PM's devolution plans
News.content:
Economist Lord Jim O'Neill, who has been advising the prime minister, has said he will not be taking a job in Andy Burnham's government.

As first reported by, external the Financial Times, Lord O'Neill, a crossbench peer who was once a treasury minister under the Conservatives, said he did not want the constraints involved in taking on a formal role.

The former chief economist at Goldman Sachs had been tipped to become Burnham's chief economic adviser.

He said he was enjoying what he was currently doing too much and did not want to have to give up control of his business interests to comply with official rules.

He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that he had "lots of other things that are going on that I very much enjoy" and, having been a minister before, he knew the job included "all the constraints that understandably go with it, like a blind trust and to abandon everything else you do, never mind the fact that it's 24/7".

In placing shares in blind trusts, ministers have no knowledge of how their investment is being handled, to avoid any potential conflict of interest.

He said he concluded he would rather be a voice to talk to and "get on with the rest of the things in my life".

He earlier told the Financial Times it was "not because of any policy disagreements", adding "I'm a massive fan of the focus on devolution and I hope Andy and his team will be bold on this and everything else."

He pointed to Greater Manchester as an example of economic growth and said if you could repeat that around populated areas, "then national economic performance will improve".

Asked by the BBC whether the new government in the upcoming October budget would need to raise taxes, Lord O'Neill said it was a choice for the prime minister and his team "based on the things they're saying they want to do more of - defence spending is obviously the one that catches the eye", among other things.

Pressed on whether the government could turn to something such as wealth taxes, Lord O'Neill said he was "not a fan of further increases in these kind of taxes, particularly as it relates to capital gains for genuine risk taking things like venture capital".

He noted that the country has boosted government spending "dramatically" in recent years and needed a "more sensible approach to welfare spending under genuine welfare reform".

From 2015-2016, Lord O'Neill was commercial secretary to the Treasury under the then-Chancellor, George Osborne.

The peer, who grew up in Greater Manchester, was a key figure in pushing the Conservatives' Northern Powerhouse agenda, which was aimed at boosting the economy of the North of England.

Lord O'Neill is also known as the economist who coined the term Bric in 2001 to describe leading developing or newly industrialised countries with potential for fast growth and, therefore, investment returns.

The original four nations - Brazil, Russia, India and China - later became the Brics when they were joined by South Africa.

News.title: Welsh county becomes global hotspot for carbon emissions after wildfires
News.content:
A county in Wales had one of the world's highest carbon emissions per square kilometre due to wildfires in July, according to a charity.

The fire above Blaenavon, Torfaen was described as "one of the largest and most challenging" in south Wales in recent years by the fire service.

Save the Children said it was concerned about possible health consequences after data, external published by the European Union's earth observation programme, Copernicus, showed Torfaen behind Malanje in Angola, Spain's Ãvila and Annaba in Algeria in terms of wildfire emissions in July.

Torfaen council said it was unaware of the EU data but its own air quality monitoring showed "elevated particulate concentrations".

A blaze the size of about 300 football pitches broke out on Mynydd Garnclochdy, between Abersychan and Blaenavon, with people reporting smelling smoke about 30 (48km) miles away in Cardiff.

Combined with others across the region it contributed to a major incident being declared, which eventually required assistance from the military.

Blaenavon councillor Janet Jones said the smoke had been "particularly bad" on 13 August - about three weeks after the fire first ignited.

"There was great concern about air quality and the impact on elderly people and those suffering with respiratory issues such as emphysema and COPD."

Jones said she had spoken with GP practice nurses two weeks ago and was not aware of any increase in patients complaining about respiratory problems, but added this "could change in the months ahead".

News.title: Third arrest in murder probe after cyclist punched
News.content:
A third person has been arrested as part of a murder investigation following the death of a "loving and loyal" man in Leicester.

George Glover, 27, was punched as he cycled along Narborough Road, close to the junction with Noel Street, at about 06:30 BST on Monday, Leicestershire Police said. He died in hospital on Thursday.

A 24-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit murder on Friday and remains in custody.

A 31-year-old man and 39-year-old woman, who were previously arrested on suspicion of robbery and conspiracy to commit murder, also remain in custody, the force said.

In a tribute released by police on Friday, Glover's family said they were "so proud of the young man he'd become".

They said: "George was a much-loved son and big brother to his three siblings. His loss is already felt so deeply."

Officers from the East Midlands Special Operations Unit are continuing to appeal for anyone who may be able to assist with their inquiries to get in touch.

Det Insp Kevin Hames said: "If you can help but haven't yet contacted us, please be assured it's not too late and anything you're able to provide â including any footage â could be vital to our investigation."

News.title: Hidden museum gallery to reopen after 83 years
News.content:
A gallery that has remained closed to the public since World War Two is to reopen at London's Natural History Museum next month.

The gallery, which has remained hidden from view since 1943, will reopen from 16 September, featuring 50 objects which show our evolving relationship with the natural world.

The exhibition, named Nature and Us, is part of a transformation project called NHM150, which aims to open a new or revamped showcase every year until the museum's 150th anniversary in 2031.

Dr Doug Gurr, director of the NHM, said: "For the first time in over 80 years, visitors will be able to step into this beautiful historic space and explore our changing relationship with the natural world."

News.title: Two men re-arrested after death of soldier
News.content:
Two men have been re-arrested on suspicion of manslaughter after the body of a soldier was found in a river.

Northumbria Police recovered the body of Liam Potts, 22, who served with the Coldstream Guards, close to Wylam Bridge on 18 August.

Prior to his disappearance in the early hours of 15 August, the force said it received reports of a disturbance at The Boathouse pub and a subsequent collision at the bridge between a car and group of pedestrians. Police are investigating whether the incidents are linked to the soldier entering the water.

Two men, aged 22 and 23, have been re-arrested on suspicion of manslaughter and remain in custody.

A man and woman, both in their 20s, sustained serious but not life-threatening injuries in the collision.

The woman has since been discharged, while the man remains in hospital for further treatment.

Police said the soldier was on the bridge at the time of the collision, but was not in the car or hit by it, yet entered the water "within minutes" of it happening.

News.title: Police investigate car crash into house in Glasgow suburb
News.content:
Police are investigating after a car crashed into a house in a Glasgow suburb.

Officers were called to the property on Low Borland Way in Eaglesham, East Renfrewshire, at about 13:20 on Friday.

A large police presence was seen on the street on Friday, which was sealed off behind a cordon. The house was protected by temporary fencing on Saturday.

BBC Scotland News understands that Police Scotland is not ruling out links to Operation Portaledge - its investigation into gangland activity across central Scotland.

The crash happened at the end of a quiet cul-de-sac of detached homes.

The brick wall of the property was caved in near the front door, with smoke marks visible to the upper floor.

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: "There are no reports of any injuries. Officers attended and inquiries are ongoing."

News.title: Brief break from rain as sunshine returns for weekend
News.content:
After the spell of showery weather earlier this week, a strong area of high pressure is set to bring bright and sunny weather to much of the UK this weekend.

Daytime temperatures will feel pleasantly warm - though a long way off from the record heat experienced earlier this month.

Nights are expected to be mostly clear, leading to a significant temperature contrast from morning lows to afternoon highs.

While Saturday and Sunday will bring a brief break from the rain for many, unsettled weather will return early next week.

The Buffalo Bills have confirmed the death of defensive tackle Ed Oliver's two-year-old son, who reportedly drowned in a swimming pool at the family's Texas home earlier this summer.

“On behalf of the entire Buffalo Bills organization, we want to publicly express our condolences to Ed Oliver and his family on the devastating loss of his son,” the NFL team’s general manager, Brandon Beane, said Saturday in a statement posted online. “It's an unthinkable tragedy for any parent. We will continue to support Ed and his family as we all grieve this tragic loss.”

The boy drowned June 28, according to The Buffalo News, which said grainy video posted online shortly after the incident showed a man who resembled Oliver sitting on a curb while speaking with a sheriff’s deputy.

Oliver, 28, didn’t join the Bills for a trip to Cleveland for a preseason Saturday game against the Browns, Fox News reported, adding that a source said he and his family were asking the public for privacy and prayers.

The Houston Chronicle reported on the fatal incident in Huffman, Texas, at the time, without identifying the victim.

open image in gallery The young son of Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver's reportedly drowned in the family’s pool in Huffman, Texas ( Getty )

A dispatcher for the Harris County Sheriff's Office was unable to immediately provide The Independent with additional information Saturday.

In a Facebook post about the drowning, Sheriff Ed Gonzalez said deputies found the toddler unresponsive in a pool in the 500 block of Lago Trace Drive in Huffman.

The child was rushed to a local hospital and pronounced dead, Gonzalez said, calling it a “tragic incident” and saying an investigation was underway.

Property records show Oliver owns a home on the block, according to The Buffalo News, which said the sheriff’s office has declined to release records related to the case.

The sheriff’s office also recently asked the state attorney general for permission to reject the news outlet’s formal request under the Texas Public Information Act, saying that the case remained open and that releasing the records could jeopardize an ongoing investigation, The Buffalo News said

Drowning is the leading cause of death for children under five, and the No. 2 cause after vehicle crashes for children ages five to 14 who die of fatal, unintentional injuries, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

open image in gallery The boy drowned June 28, according to The Buffalo News , which said grainy video posted online shortly after the incident showed a man who resembled Oliver sitting on a curb while speaking with a sheriff’s deputy ( Getty )

Oliver, who’s six-feet, one-inch tall and weighs 287 pounds, was the Bills’ first-round draft pick in 2019, and he signed a four-year contract extension worth up to $68 million in 2023, according to ESPN and The Buffalo News.

He was sidelined for all but three games of the 2025 regular season, but bounced back to play in the Bills’ win over the Jacksonville Jaguars in the AFC wild card round, according to The Buffalo News.

His hometown of Huffman is a quickly growing unincorporated community about 30 miles northeast of Houston on the eastern shore of Lake Houston, an 11,000-acre reservoir, according to Homes.com.

Many houses sit on more than an acre of land in the wooded area, with many located in a series of subdivisions that feature custom-built, farmhouse-inspired residences, Homes.com says.

Tadej Pogacar got straight down to business as ​he opened his quest to win the Vuelta a Espana for the first time by snatching victory in the opening time trial in Monaco.

Little more than two months after the roar of Formula 1 cars echoed around the streets of the glitzy principality, the world's fastest cyclist relied purely on leg and lung power to underline his superiority.

Seven years after his only previous appearance at the Spanish race, since when he has won five Tour de France titles and a ⁠Giro d'Italia, the UAE Emirates rider laid ​down ⁠an immediate marker to break the heart of Britain's Ethan Hayter.

Hayter had looked on course to win the 9.4km time trial and take the red jersey at the 81st edition of the Vuelta. But Slovenia's Pogacar, the penultimate ​starter of ⁠the 184 riders, had other ‌ideas as he rolled down the start ramp from the marbled floors of Monte Carlo's glitzy casino.

open image in gallery Tadej Pogacar made a strong start to his bid to complete the grand tour set ( AP )

Few would wager against a rider who dominated last month's Tour de France to move alongside the greats of the past, although he was marginally down on the split times. He produced a devastating late burst through the final curves though to claim his 20th victory of the season.

Britain's Josh Tarling finished an emotional third fastest having decided to race eight days after the death of his 19-year-old brother Fin at the Volta a Portugal. "It was just great to have him here and he was really keen to ride and get back to the day job," his Netcompany-Ineos race director Geraint Thomas told TNT Sports.

"It's unimaginable what he has gone through the last week and to put in a performance like that shows his class. We will try to be normal around him and support him as best we can." Monaco became the seventh non-Spain start for ‌the Vuelta and the fourth in ⁠five years after Piemonte last year, Lisbon in 2024 and Utrecht in ⁠2022.

It proved a fitting launch pad for the last grand tour of the year and one which could see Pogacar become only the ninth rider to win all three. After a relatively gentle start, things will ​quickly toughen up on Sunday with a hilly 214km stage from Monaco to Manosque.

Reuters

Tottenham Hotspur’s expensive summer rebuild was shaken to its foundations by rampant Brentford on an alarming opening day for Roberto De Zerbi’s side.

New-look Spurs showed the same old flaws as goals from Keane Lewis-Potter, Vitaly Janelt and Michael Kayode saw them dismantled 3-0.

Spurs look set to top the £300m mark on new faces this summer once they complete deals for Savinho and Omar Marmoush in a bid to move on from last season’s scrape with relegation.

open image in gallery Roberto De Zerbi was left with questions about his side after a poor performance ( PA )

But it was Brentford’s marquee signing, the comparably reasonably-priced £41m midfielder Mamadou Sangare, who provided the early dividends in west London.

Archie Gray made Spurs history as the club’s youngest captain since Steve Perryman in the 1970s, and he was joined in the back four by three new signings in Andy Robertson, Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi.

That lack of familiarity showed in the opening seconds with Robertson almost putting through his own net before Bees skipper Nathan Collins stabbed a glorious chance wide from six yards out.

Livewire Mali international Sangare set up the opening goal after just 12 minutes, playing a one-two on the edge of the box, bursting to the byline and cutting the ball back for Lewis-Potter to convert.

open image in gallery Keane Lewis-Potter put his side ahead ( Getty )

The Bees kept piling forward and Dango Ouattara was put through by Igor Thiago only to be thwarted by Spurs keeper Antonin Kinsky.

The pressure told in the 33rd minute when Kinsky could only parry Mathias Jensen’s shot from the edge of the box and Janelt snaffled up the rebound.

Tottenham’s torrid first half was best summed up when the ball dropped 18 yards out to £100m man Sandro Tonali, who shanked his volley miles over the crossbar.

Things did not improve after the break, despite the half-time arrival of £85m midfielder Mateus Fernandes.

The third goal came when Collins headed a corner down at the far post, Sangare’s snap-shot was beaten away by Kinsky and Kayode lashed in the loose ball.

open image in gallery Michael Kayode, right, wrapped up the points ( PA Wire )

“Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you,” chimed the Brentford fans, an ode to their old boss whose disastrous spell at Spurs last season left De Zerbi picking up the pieces.

Moments later it should have been four after Rodrigo Bentancur bundled over Kevin Schade in the area, but last term’s top scorer Thiago rolled his spot-kick against a post.

Mikey Moore, the 19-year-old homegrown winger, provided the only bright spark with two efforts saved by Bees keeper Caoimhin Kelleher on an otherwise dark opening day for Spurs.

PA

News.title: Police chief gives emotional update after A66 crash kills seven, including two officers
News.content:
Cleveland Police Chief Constable Victoria Fuller gave an emotional update after seven people, including two police officers, died in a crash.

The incident happened during a police pursuit in the early hours of Saturday morning on the A66 near Middlesbrough. (22 August)

“This morning, a Volkswagen Passat that was traveling the wrong way down the A66 has collided with a marked Cleveland Police armed response vehicle, which was traveling on the correct side of the road” The Chief Constable said during a press conference on Saturday afternoon.

The Home Depot is making urgent DIY jobs easier with a new Express Delivery service across the U.S. that promises to get eligible orders to customers in three hours or less.

The service, announced earlier this week, is available to both professional contractors and small-time customers for a flat fee. Home Depot has not said how much it will cost but shoppers will not need a subscription or membership to use the service.

The chain is relying on more than 2,000 U.S. stores to fulfill the orders, giving customers access to thousands of products without having to go pick them out themselves. The selection includes plumbing and electrical supplies, paint, tools, hardware and other common project essentials.

"Whether you're a DIYer who needs one more bag of fertilizer to finish the yard or a Pro running short on adhesives and caulk for a time-sensitive job, Express Delivery makes it easier than ever for our customers to get the supplies they need, right when they need them most,” Jordan Broggi, EVP of Interconnected Retail, said in a statement.

Customers can check whether an item is eligible for Express Delivery on its product page or at checkout. Home Depot says it is also working to make the delivery window even shorter in the coming months.

open image in gallery Home Depot’s new nationwide Express Delivery gets orders to customers in three hours or less ( The Home Depot )

The express delivery launch comes after Home Depot got a boost from shoppers tackling smaller home improvement projects this summer. This helped the retailer post better-than-expected second-quarter results despite the ongoing slump in the U.S. housing market.

Revenue rose to $47.86 billion from $45.28 billion, beating the $47.24 billion analysts had expected, according to FactSet. Sales at stores open for at least a year increased 1.7 percent worldwide, while U.S. comparable sales rose 1.3 percent.

Express Delivery is just one of several delivery options Home Depot is expanding. Customers can also get free same-day delivery on orders of $25 or more placed by 4 p.m., according to the news release.

open image in gallery More than 2,000 U.S. Home Depot stores will fulfill Express Delivery orders, with eligible items including plumbing and electrical supplies, paint, tools, and hardware ( Getty Images )

The retailer is also relying on an expanding network of delivery centers to speed up orders across categories including lighting, vanities, décor and building materials.

Home Depot says more than 65 percent of its in-stock parcel products can be delivered the same day or the next day, while about 55 percent of in-stock big-and-bulky orders can arrive within two days.

For customers replacing a major appliance, Home Depot is also expanding next-day delivery. The service now reaches about 60 percent of the U.S. population for select appliances, including refrigerators, washers and dryers, according to the company. The faster service can also help contractors who need to quickly replace an appliance as part of a time-sensitive repair.
