Nigel Farage’s Reform UK has received £20m in donations from cryptocurrency investors since the general election, The Independent can reveal.

An analysis of Electoral Commission data shows that a staggering 60 per cent of the right-wing eurosceptic group’s funding comes from wealthy individuals associated with the digital currency since the beginning of 2024.

The largest donations, totalling £15m, came from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne, whose separate undeclared donation of £5m directly to Mr Farage is the subject of a parliamentary probe.

Other donors include Ben Peter Delo, the founder of cryptocurrency trading platform BitMex, who gave two £2m payments to the party this year and Maria Rost, the wife of US crypto investor John Rost, who has given nine payments worth £125,000.

Simon William Smith, a London-based bitcoin investor who founded a company which allows content creators to sell their content in exchange for Bitcoin, donated £116,000 ahead of the general election in 2024. Oscar Townsley, the founder of Bitcoin derivatives trading firm A1X, gave the party £30,000 last year.

By comparison, the Conservative Party received £82,250 in donations from Alan Eldad Howard, a hedge fund manager and crypto investor. The Independent did not identify any such donations for Labour, Lib Dems or the Green Party.

A Reform UK spokesman said: “Reform takes pride in its stringent vetting of donations and always ensures that the Electoral Commission guidelines on donations, as set out in the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000, are strictly followed, as has been the case with all donations.”

open image in gallery The majority of Reform’s funding is from individuals tied to the crypto sector ( Getty/The Independent )

The revelations will pile further pressure on Mr Farage, who was re-elected as Clacton MP earlier this month after he dramatically quit in protest at intense scrutiny over Mr Harborne’s £5m donation, which he insists was a personal gift.

Bridget Phillipson, chair of the Labour Party, told The Independent: “Nigel Farage has spent the summer battling a bin in a desperate attempt to dodge scrutiny but people have a right to know what he’s hiding.

“He secretly took a £5m ‘gift’ from a Thai-based crypto billionaire and then promised to cut taxes for the crypto industry.

“Now it seems his party is awash with crypto cash. Farage is treating the public with contempt. With donations from a convicted fraudster and police probes into Reform’s donors and finances – it’s clear they think the rules are for other people."

What are the other parties’ stance on cryptocurrency?

Labour has taken a strict stance on cryptocurrency, with Sir Keir Starmer imposing a temporary ban on cryptocurrency donations and a cap on donations from Britons living abroad to political parties as part of a wider government review into electoral interference. No other parties have promoted pro-crypto policies and the Greens have called for a ban on “unethical” crypto adverts in the London Underground.

open image in gallery Stella Creasy is seeking an amendment that would cap donations from any individual ( House of Commons )

Labour MP Stella Creasy wants the government to go further and fears its cap could only create a loophole that people with British postcodes will exploit.

She is fighting for an amendment to cap donations from any individual and prevent everyone from having “an outsized influence on British politics because of the amount of money they can give”.

“I think the public should be worried full stop,” she said. “What I fear is coming is the wholesale distortion of democracy whereby a small number of disproportionately loud voices determine outcomes because of the funding they offer.

“Even if there is no connection between Mr Farage receiving substantial sums of money and his views on cryptocurrencies, the appearance of it undermines our democracy. Just as the appearance that individual donations to my own political party might be shaping outcomes, or to the Conservatives, or to the Greens, or the Lib Dems.”

She added: “But if it walks like a duck and it talks like a duck, you can see why people are squawking.”

Labour MP Catherine West told The Independent: “The late Robin Williams once suggested that politicians should wear jackets with the names of the people who are sponsoring them. In Reform's case, it seems to be a magic cloak that disappears when difficult questions are asked.

“Ordinary people across the country need nothing less than full disclosure on who exactly is trying to buy their way into UK legislation.”

open image in gallery Nigel Farage claimed his party would make London one of the major crypto trading centres of the world ( PA Wire )

Experts have warned of the dangers of accepting such large donations from a tiny group of people, saying many will likely be seeking a “return on investment” and may be hoping to influence policy or party stance.

Tory MP Harriet Baldwin, former chair of the Treasury committee, said: “In the US, President Trump has profited personally from liberalising the rules around cryptocurrencies. It would be regrettable if the UK became a place where politicians used power over independent regulators for their own personal enrichment.”

What are Reform’s policies on cryptocurrency?

The £20m received by Reform does not include £614,000 in donations and payments from individuals and groups tied to the sector, declared by Mr Farage. He also has shares in Stack BTC, a UK bitcoin treasury.

Since the general election, he and his party have fought to liberalise the crypto market, argued against state involvement in the sector, and published draft legislation that hopes to ignite a “crypto revolution” in Britain.

It is a stance shared by Farage ally Donald Trump who has championed the digital currency and heavily profited from crypto while in office.

The US president has unveiled several crypto-friendly policies since and made more than $1.4bn (USD) from business dealings in cryptocurrency last year.

During a bitcoin conference in Las Vegas, Mr Farage promised to enact his Cryptoassets and Digital Finance Bill if Reform won at the next general election.

The draft piece of legislation promised to cut taxes on crypto profits and create a Treasury bitcoin reserve fund. It has since disappeared from Reform’s website.

Stuart Wilks-Heeg, a politics professor at the University of Liverpool, said the large proportion of Reform’s funding coming from individuals with crypto ties was “significant”. He said individuals typically donated to parties because they have a shared ideology, want influence, or expect something in return.

He told The Independent: “These are some of the biggest donations in British political history, and it's a sector that a lot of people have concerns about for good reason.

“The easiest party to influence in terms of policy is clearly Reform, because it's not internally democratic. Basically, what Nigel says goes. So if you've got Nigel's ear, you can shape policy.”

open image in gallery Donald Trump made more than $1.4bn (USD) from business dealings in cryptocurrency last year ( Instagram )

Sam Power, a leading expert in political financing at the University of Bristol, said the donations were essential for a party that has such a shallow funding base.

“We have never in British politics seen a party of that shape and size secure the kind of income that they [Reform] have.

“It’d be hard to look at Reform’s view on crypto and think that crypto donors backing them wouldn’t think they’ve spent their money wisely.”

News.title: New Zealand stun South Africa to make statement start to Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

New Zealand overcame a tough physical challenge to outscore hosts South Africa five tries to one and win the first Test 33-16 at Ellis Park on Saturday to go one-up in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

The ​All ⁠Blacks had been underdogs going into the first ⁠international of their eight-match tour, ​but ⁠took full advantage ‌of the home side’s numerous handling errors and ill-discipline ‌for a statement victory ‌that ended a 12-match winning streak for the Springboks and will ⁠rock the confidence of the world champions.

Will Jordan extended his run as New Zealand’s record try scorer with two tries that bookended scores from Josh Moorby, Fabian Holland and Luke Jacobson. Ruben Love kicked over four conversions.

South Africa’s try came from ⁠Andre Esterhuizen, with three penalties and ‌a conversion ​from Cheslin ‌Kolbe.

An attritional contest was always on the cards and it proved a slugfest at times as South Africa looked to impose their physicality, but the All Blacks took them on toe-to-toe ⁠and emerged with a deserved win. It hands them a major psychological advantage with the next three Tests to follow on successive Saturdays.

“It meant everything,” two-try Jordan beamed. “Ellis Park, what an arena. It was a serious shift and the boys dug deep. They got a taste of what it is like and I'm proud of our group, it's an awesome start to the series.

open image in gallery Will Jordan scored his 52nd and 53rd Test tries ( AP )

"Test footy is about absorbing pressure and turning yours into points. We withstood an Springbok onslaught, so we're stoked. I just love being out here. I'm so proud of our team for this effort."

The Springboks ⁠had the chance to take an early lead ‌in the second minute with an easy-looking penalty but opted for a lineout instead, looking to maul over for an early statement try, but botched it. The next penalty, three minutes later, was then booted over for the opening points of the series.

When New Zealand had their first opportunity to level in the ninth minute, ‌they also spurned easy points and opted to kick out for a lineout, from which a maul and snap pass out to the wing put Jordan over for the first try of the four-Test series.

Five minutes later, Bok replacement Esterhuizen bashed his way through a porous Kiwi defence and put South Africa back in front. But while the home side tried some extravagant passes in the backline, and were guilty of handling errors, the All Blacks probed with their own ability to run at the Springboks, and when Josh Moorby slipped two tackles and went over on the left wing, they had a second try in the 23rd minute.

open image in gallery The scrum battle proved fascinating and key in Johannesburg ( Reuters )

Kolbe’s penalty before the break, after the South Africans began to dominate the scrums, made it 13-12 at halftime to the hosts, and he kicked over another as the Boks again forced a scrum infringement early in the second half. South Africa’s forwards then held the upper hand, but errors stymied their hopes of converting dominance into ‌points, while the All Blacks refused to capitulate and were back ahead when giant lock Fabian Holland charged down ​a clearance from Grant Williams and went over in the 48th minute.

open image in gallery A bruising affair sets up the series nicely ( Reuters )

South Africa had won a series of easily kickable penalties to regain the lead but looked to scrum the resistance out of the All Blacks and were met by solid defence. The hosts were always vulnerable to ⁠the counter-attack, and when Damian McKenzie broke the line, it set up a scrum from which Luke Jacobson scored the Kiwis’ fourth try.

Jordan made sure of a 17-point difference as he went over near the end, for his 53rd international try. By that time South Africa had ‌lost their discipline, after multiple turnovers, and finished down ​to 13 players with Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach sent to the sin bin in the final 10 minutes.

"In hindsight there were two or three big moments where we let the game get away from us because New Zealand forced us into errors by being intense and sharp," said home coach Rassie Erasmus.

The second Test is in Cape Town next Saturday.

Reuters

News.title: All Blacks stun Springboks in statement win
News.content:
Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry did not begin with the year’s greatest game, but a New Zealand victory against the odds, at high altitude in Johannesburg, has poured intrigue and interest on to a series which was already brimming with them.

The All Blacks’ recent record at Ellis Park, the Springboks’ spiritual home, is by no means shabby – this was their fourth victory from the last six visits – but few fancied Dave Rennie’s galvanised Kiwis on Saturday, against the back-to-back world champions, after a week which had been dominated by chat of officials and law interpretations.

Yet, this stunning victory was almost as comfortable as it was surprising. New Zealand outscored their hosts by five tries to one and, by the end, a 13-player Springboks outfit – both Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sin-binned within a minute of each other – were left chasing shadows in an Ellis Park which had been stupefied into silence. The Springboks did not score a solitary second-half point.

It was at the beginning of that 13-player period when New Zealand put the game to bed, with Will Jordan crossing for his second try. But the damage had already been done by a cast of Kiwi conquerors. Ardie Savea, captain and No 8, could not have delivered more for the cause; Luke Jacobson and Tupou Vaa’i on the flanks were more than deputies to Savea; the locks, until Josh Lord’s unfortunate departure just before half-time, were magnificent; and, behind them, Cam Roigard continues to look every bit the equal of those phenomenal French scrum-halves. The New Zealand midfield got the upper hand on their much vaunted counterparts, too, on the day of Damian de Allende’s 100th cap for South Africa.

News.title: George Russell king of the sprint and driving with freedom after engagement
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix, the first race after F1’s summer break. Kimi Antonelli has had a tremendous first part of the season, leading Lewis Hamilton by 50 points and George Russell by 59 after the first 11 rounds. He has taken six wins to Russell’s two, with Hamilton, Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc all racking up a win apiece.

His start to the second part of the season was not the best, however. A messy sprint qualifying session meant he ended down in fifth, more than 0.2sec behind team-mate Russell, who took a much-needed pole.

Some of the damage was self-inflicted, quite literally. In the first session of sprint qualifying he ran wide at the banked turn 12 and into the gravel. The damage to the floor of his car was attempted to be repaired for the rest of the session but left him lacking downforce. A gap of 0.2sec is not enormous but the other issue was that three other cars – Norris, Leclerc and Piastri – are between him and Russell.

That said, it is not a great worry at this point. The points available in the sprint are relatively small and Antonelli has a healthy margin at this point over his rivals. In any case, there is no guarantee that Russell and Antonelli finish where they will start. Antonelli has shown on numerous occasions that he can bounce back from a difficult session and you have to expect that again here.

The race, which starts at 11am BST, is one-third of the race distance and should be run in dry conditions. There have been persistent showers and a steady breeze at Zandvoort this weekend, but it is not expected to affect the running in the sprint.

Qualifying for tomorrow’s grand prix comes later today at 3pm, which could be a more consequential session.

News.title: Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

Full team news as and when we get it.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

News.title: Congo gambles on ‘old’ vaccine as new Ebola virus spirals
News.content:
Nearly half of all those infected have gone on to die.

Dr Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine partnership, earlier this week said to beat the outbreak “we must deploy every tool at our disposal”.

She went on: “To avoid this becoming the worst recorded Ebola outbreak in history, it is critical that all effective countermeasure options are brought to bear.

“We have a tool that could help save lives while we wait for [Bundibugyo]-specific vaccines to become available.”

Previous clinical trials have shown that Ervebo is safe, but its effect on other strains is unknown.

The World Health Organisation said in a statement that while it was not known if Ervebo may protect against the Bundibugyo virus, “early laboratory and animal data suggest it may provide some protection”.

Medics told the Telegraph of anecdotal claims that health workers who had been given Ervebo to protect them during an outbreak of the Zaire strain in 2018 to 2020 had not fallen ill during the current Bundibugyo outbreak.

Health workers are at extreme risk of catching the disease because they come into contact with highly-contagious blood, vomit and diarrhoea from dying patients. When they fall sick themselves, they frequently go on to infect their own families.

Giving health workers vaccine jabs to protect them as they tend the sick is a cornerstone of Ebola responses.

The WHO said the vaccine allocation includes 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus. The remaining 50,000 doses will be used for front-line and health workers as recommended by WHO experts.

Dr Nishtar said: “Having already been licensed for the Zaire strain, we know that Ervebo is proven to be safe.

“And while the signs are that it may not stop transmission – which is essential for ending the outbreak - it could well save precious lives and reduce suffering.”

Health officials warn that the Bundibugyo outbreak centred on DRC’s Ituri province is easily outpacing relief efforts.

The virus is thought to have been spreading for months before an outbreak was finally declared in mid-May and medics have been unable to make up the head start.

An analysis by the Africa Centres for Disease Control meanwhile warned the current outbreak dwarfed all others on record

The current outbreak had almost ten times more cases than any other previous outbreak at a similar stage.

News.title: Soaring welfare bill pushes national debt to almost £3tn
News.content:
Britain’s soaring welfare bill forced John Healey to borrow more to balance the books last month.

The gap between tax receipts and spending unexpectedly resulted in a £1.8bn deficit in July, taking the national debt to within a whisker of £3tn.

Economists had predicted the Government would borrow nothing and blamed the deficit on the rising welfare bill.

Figures published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) this morning show total debt rose to £2.985tn in July.

Benefit payments also climbed by 7.2pc, or £2bn, to £30bn last month.

The Chancellor now faces another tax-raising Budget in October, even as strong receipts from self-employed workers provide some respite.

The ONS also said Mr Healey spent £7.7bn on debt interest in July alone, almost 10pc higher than a year ago.

Ashley Webb, at Capital Economics said: “The weak performance was mainly due higher social payments.”

Monthly borrowing was slightly higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility and markets expected, meaning the Government has borrowed £56.7bn this financial year to plug the gap between tax receipts and public spending.

Julian Jessop, an independent economist and IEA economics fellow, said: “The latest official data highlight the fragility of the public finances as John Healey prepares his first Budget. Government borrowing was £2.3bn above forecast in July, and £0.7bn higher than in the same month a year ago.”

July is traditionally a strong month for receipts from the self-employed, with self-assessed income tax receipts last month coming to £17.1bn, about £1.7bn more than a year earlier.

However, higher inflation triggered by the Iran war means Mr Healey will be forced to use the Budget to find billions of pounds to repair the public finances.

Mr Healey said: “Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our UK economic stability and national security which is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules, with a buffer against global uncertainties.”

The Resolution Foundation warned that the Chancellor’s headroom against his fiscal rules - self-imposed guardrails to guide public spending - has shrunk from around £24bn in the Spring Statement to less than £8bn today.

The think tank called on the Chancellor to use his first Budget on Oct 28 to put the nation’s finances on a more sustainable path.

Elliott Christensen, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The Chancellor’s margin against his fiscal rules is now razor thin.”

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola reveals ‘fight’ with Alexander Isak as Liverpool icon demands Florian Wirtz grab the bull by the horns
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL’S £100m stars Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz have been challenged to step up to the mark this season.

Andoni Iraola believes Isak can become more than just a goalscorer, while Stan Collymore has told Wirtz he must start dominating games for Liverpool.



Isak returns to Newcastle tomorrow for the first time since his controversial £130million move to Anfield, with the striker set to face a hostile reception from supporters who have not forgotten his decision to go on strike to force through the transfer window last summer.

The Sweden international endured a difficult first season on Merseyside, scoring just four goals in 22 appearances after a broken leg restricted him to only 12 starts.



But new Liverpool boss Iraola believes Isak can rediscover the form that made him a hero at Newcastle, where he scored 62 goals across three seasons.

The Basque boss said: “Alex is going to be a very important player for us this season.

“Right now, he is in a very good place. He has been training every day, has not missed a session and has been adding more and more minutes every friendly game.”

“He played a very good World Cup in terms of availability – fitness level – and I want to keep him there as much as we can.

“We know his level and, if we can keep him there, he will score goals and give us a lot of things.”

Talking about where Isak can improve, the Liverpool boss gave his verdict.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Iraola added: “Probably my fight with him, my instructions, are more in terms of without the ball.

“How he can help in his position when we have the ball, so he can open spaces for other players.”

“I am not trying to focus in terms of goals but he is a striker – he will want to score, but I try not to judge strikers if they score or if they haven’t.”

Iraola’s comments come as Liverpool continue to search for more attacking options, with the new boss admitting: “We don’t have enough wingers.”



The Reds have have been linked with PSG duo Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

However, they appear to be prioritising Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh to replace Mo Salah after the Reds legend left for Trabzonspor.

Liverpool have already had two bids rejected for the 22-year-old, with their latest £60million offer turned down and Brighton understood to want closer to £70m.

While Isak is being challenged to become more complete, Collymore has issued a similar warning to Wirtz.



The Germany international arrived from Bayer Leverkusen for around £100m last summer, but struggled to consistently produce his best football during a disappointing campaign in 2025/26.

Collymore believes there can be no excuses this time around.

Speaking on behalf of 10bet, the former Liverpool striker said: “He has to be better this season and I think that is HIS responsibility. But this time he needs to lead the attack and be the focus, and he needs to show that he can make an impact more regularly.

“When he plays for Germany, he dominates matches to the point where you walk away thinking he was head and shoulders above everyone else on the pitch. He hasn’t reached that level consistently for Liverpool yet.”

“I don’t think he’s controlling enough games for Liverpool yet. The key thing you want is to completely occupy the opposition for 15 or 20-minute spells.



“Where is he positioning himself? What is he creating? Right now, he goes in and out of matches.”

Collymore also believes Wirtz and Isak must complement each other if Liverpool are to become a more dangerous side.

Liverpool and Premier League fans will remember the partnership Steven Gerrard and Fernando Torres had during their time at the club playing under Rafa Benitez, with Gerrard playing in behind the Spaniard – something Wirtz and Isak will look to for inspiration.

Collymore added: “While someone like Isak needs to dictate where he wants the service, Wirtz needs to control games much more through his ability.



“At the moment, he operates as a bit-part player who shows flashes of brilliance, leaving people expecting something to happen that then doesn’t materialise.

“If he can dominate games with an eight-out-of-ten performance week in, week out, Liverpool become a more three-dimensional team.”

For Iraola and Liverpool, getting both of them firing could be the difference between another difficult campaign and a serious challenge at the top.

Sports.title: ‘Sack him now’ – Raging West Ham fans get ‘NUNO OUT’ trending after horror defeat leaves them 17th in Championship
Sports.content:
FUMING West Ham fans were left up in arms after their newly-relegated side lost 2-1 to Charlton.

The raging supporters rushed online as they demanded that manager Nuno Espirito Santo immediately get the sack.



The Addicks’ Lloyd Jones opened scoring in the seventh minute before Tyreece Campbell doubled the lead after half-time.

While Joel Piroe, on loan from Leeds, clawed one back in the last 20 minutes, it was not enough as the Hammers slumped to 17th in the Championship.



The Portuguese boss penned a three-year deal with the Hammers in September 2025, following the sacking of Graham Potter.

Nuno was fired from Nottingham Forest less than three weeks before walking into the London Stadium.

At the time, the 52-year-old said: “My objective is to work hard to get the very best from the team and ensure that we are as competitive as we possibly can be.

“The work has already started and I am looking forward to the challenge that is ahead.”

Nuno bowed out of last season with the Hammers missing out on safety after Tottenham beat Everton 1-0 on the final day.

But now his future has been left hanging in the balance.

Sports.title: Liverpool transfer boost as Bradley Barcola and Ibrahima Mbaye both DROPPED from PSG squad for Ligue 1 opener
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL transfer targets Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye are both out of PSG’s matchday squad again amid uncertainty surrounding their future.

Barcola, 23, has been top of the Reds’ wishlist for months but a move to Anfield is dragging on.



And team-mate Mbaye, 18, is a possible alternative for Andoni Iraola‘s men.

But the pair will not be playing for the second week in a row after being DROPPED by boss Luis Enrique.



According to Fabrizio Romano, they will not be included in Sunday’s opening Ligue 1 match away at Rennes.

The attacking duo were left out of the Trophee Des Champions final defeat to Lens last week as well.

And that came after they played no role in the Uefa Super Cup win over Aston Villa just days previously.

Barcola and Mbaye were at the World Cup with France and Senegal respectively, and have a host of competition for a spot in the line-up.

Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue, and Khvicha Kvaratskelia were already key members of Enrique’s group, and they have bolstered that with Maghnes Akliouche’s arrival from Monaco.

When asked about the bold decision to leave Mbaye and Barcola at home for the Lens clash, Enrique stormed out of his post-match interview.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He then added in a press conference:

“We are a very young, very ambitious team.

“And it’s more important to make changes and find players who enjoy playing our way and being happy to play for PSG.

“If a player doesn’t really want to come, if he’s not happy here, it’s better to find another solution.”

Barcola has also been on Arsenal’s radar but they turned attention towards Vinicius Jr before missing out.



But he is valued at £140million which has proven far too much so far for Liverpool.

Iraola and Co are set to push for a new winger in the final days of the window.

They have now had two bids rejected for INJURED Brighton man Jankuba Minteh.

Sports.title: Man Utd legend Peter Schmeichel slams two ‘sloppy’ stars for shambolic moment in humiliating Hull defeat
Sports.content:
PETER SCHMEICHEL has slammed Patrick Dorgu and Ayden Heaven for their role in Manchester United’s shambolic defending during their humiliating defeat to Hull City.

The Red Devils legend was left furious after United conceded twice in the first half of their 2-0 loss at the MKM Stadium.



Newly-promoted Hull stunned Michael Carrick‘s side as Semi Ajayi smashed home the opener from close range after United failed to properly deal with a corner.

Former United keeper Schmeichel wasted no time picking out Dorgu and Heaven for their roles in the sloppy defending.



Analysing the goal at half-time on Premier League Productions, the Dane said: “This is sloppy defending, this is all about concentrating.

“Look at Dorgu, Dorgu on the front post, he is not even looking at the guy taking the corner kick.

“At that exact moment, he loses his concentration, he does not have the ability to block the first ball.”

Dorgu’s lapse allowed the ball to reach the danger area, with United unable to clear their lines before Ajayi pounced.

Schmeichel added: “And of course, Ayden Heaven on the back post. That’s not how you defend, you have to be stronger.”

Debutant Nobel Mendy headed home the second to leave the hosts 2-0 up and United facing a mountain to climb – something they didn’t manage to do.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It was a brutal assessment from Schmeichel, who won five Premier League titles while at United during the 90s.

United also won the Champions League in 1998/99 on a night where Schmeichel captained the side in the absence of the suspended Roy Keane.

He played under the same manager throughout in Sir Alex Ferguson, who once famously said: “Attack wins you games, defence wins you titles.”

That was certainly the case in the 90s while Schmeichel was playing in net, and in front of him he regularly had a solid defence.



The likes of Gary and Phil Neville, Gary Pallister, Steve Bruce, Denis Irwin, Jaap Stam and Ronny Johnsen formed the base of consistent title winning teams.

That’s why today’s under par defensive performance from the Red Devils would have angered Schmeichel even more as it’s something he wasn’t used to during his playing days at the club.

United had never previously lost their opening league fixture of a season against a newly-promoted team, winning nine and drawing three of their previous 12 meetings.

But for Hull, today is a day that will live long in the memory on Humberside.

Sports.title: Fans cringe as Sky Sports commentators make ‘dad jokes’ after cameras pan to Jon Bon Jovi in crowd for Brentford-Spurs
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL fans were left cringing as Sky Sports commentators made dad jokes after spotting Jon Bon Jovi at Brentford vs Tottenham.

The music icon was sitting in the crowd at the Gtech when cameras panned to him in black sunnies.



Smiling away, the American, 64, was quickly the subject of some song puns.

With Bill Leslie on main duties and Alan Smith his co-comms partner, the pair immediately cracked a gag.



Leslie said: “There was a rumour doing the rounds that he’d come to watch one of Tottenham’s new signings that he heard had joined from a coastal club.

“He heard that Jonny used to work down the docks.”

Referencing the lyrics from top hit Livin’ on a Prayer, Smith picked up on it and replied: “It’s been a Bed of Roses for Spurs so far.”

That drew a laugh from Leslie but fans weren’t sure about their chat.

One wrote online: “The pre written Bon Jovi gags a new low”.

Others were happier to see the legend in attendance.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

A different user said: “Oh my god lads (Spurs) you CANNOT embarrass me Infront of THE Jon Bon Jovi!!!!”

Someone else commented: “spurs opening premier league game & my commentators are making bon jovi jokes. we are so back”.

And many were just confused.

An account questioned: “John Bon Jovi is at Brentford for the game against Tottenham. Wonder what team he supports.”

Bon Jovi is due to play three nights at Wembley on his Forever tour early next month.

Sports.title: Non-league side slam ref for refusing to call off FA Cup game with pitch ‘unplayable’ – fans say ‘genuinely disgusting’
Sports.content:
NON-LEAGUE club Beckenham Town have slammed a “disgraceful” referee after he deemed a pitch playable, despite it being in a shocking state.

The club have vowed to get in touch with the FA, after the ref gave the go ahead on an “absolutely awful” pitch.



The club posted a video of the turf, or lack of, at FA Cup opponents Camberley Town on their X account, while slamming the ref in the process.

They said: “Absolutely disgraceful decision by the referee, I don’t think he’s qualified enough to call this game on.



“The pitch is absolutely awful, you can’t see the goal areas, you can’t see the markings.”

They added that they plan to contact the FA to find out which ref gave the pitch the go-ahead the day before.



Beckenham went on to lose in dramatic fashion on the barren surface, throwing away a 2-1 lead to eventually lose 3-2.

It means their FA Cup dream is over for another season, but they will feel hard-done-by, after being forced to play on the arid pitch.

Fans also had their say on social media, as the clip went viral.

One wrote: “That is genuinely disgusting.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Another one hilariously compared it to the Star Wars sand planet Tattooine.

While a third posted: “Games will get called off for frozen pitches but they allow them to be played on these concrete dustbowls.”

Sports.title: ‘Goal of the season already’ – EFL star scores Puskas contender with outrageous backheeled volley into top bins
Sports.content:
BRISTOL CITY striker Dom Ballard scored a Puskas Award contender in the late stages of a Championship thriller against Birmingham.

The 21-year-old sent a backheeled volley flying into the top-left corner in the 85th minute of the match to put City 2-1 up at St Andrew’s.

Ballard pounced onto a cross from Rio Cardines with his back to goal and flicked his right boot at the ball, firing it past James Beadle and into the Birmingham net.



Fans were quick to react on social media, with one person writing: “DOM BALLARD THAT IS GOAL OF THE SEASON ALREADY!”



Another commented: “DOM BALLARD that is INSANE, goal of the season is already in boys and girls!”

A third wrote: “What on earth has Dom Ballard just done… Goal of the season already.”

While a fourth said: “Dom Ballard, this is magical.”

Despite the incredible finish, Bristol City went on to concede a 95th-minute equaliser from Demarai Gray.

Speaking after the match, Ballard said: “Not just me, the performance is from everyone.

“Everyone played their role today and did it really well.

“But yeah, to score that goal, I don’t think I’ll score many better.



“Really, really happy.”

Ballard’s stunning strike was his first competitive goal for Bristol City since completing his move from Leyton Orient earlier this month.

Sports.title: ‘Which numpty signed off on this?’ – Fans baffled by bizarre kit clash in Tottenham’s Premier League visit to Brentford
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM fans have been left baffled over a bizarre kit clash for their opening day trip to Brentford.

Spurs travelled to the Gtech on Saturday sporting their unusual navy away kit with purple, orange and blue diagonal stripes.



But it didn’t mesh too well with Brentford‘s home kit, which uses red and white stripes.

And supporters voiced their frustrations on X as they called the clash “annoying”.



One Spurs fan wrote: “Which numpty signed off on using this kit when today? This is one hell of clash with Brentford’s at least on tv viewing anyway.”

Another said: “What’s going on with this kit clash very annoying.”



A third added: “The kit clash is still present today… should’ve worn the home kit.”

And a fourth said: “Bit of a kit clash?”

The clash wasn’t the only thing troubling Spurs fans as they watched their side go 1-0 down in the opening 12 minutes.

Keane Lewis-Potter was left totally unmarked inside the box and calmly dispatched.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And the Bees made it 2-0 midway through the first half as Vitaly Janelt buried a rebound after Lucas Bergvall‘s error.

Brentford grabbed a third after the break through Michael Kayode.

And they could have been 4-0 up after they were awarded a penalty for Rodrigo Bentancur’s clumsy foul on Kevin Schade – but Igor Thiago hit the post.

It was shock to the system for Tottenham, who had been backed for a big season under Roberto De Zerbi after spending nearly £300million this summer.

Spurs started the game with new signings Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali.



But the north London outfit barely created any chances in the first half as Brentford frustrated them.

Tottenham were hoping to put their disaster 2025-26 campaign behind them after scraping survival on the final day with just 41 points.

Sports.title: Tottenham fall flat as Roberto De Zerbi's new-look team dealt brutal lesson by Brentford
Sports.content:
Tottenham fall flat as Roberto De Zerbi's new-look team dealt brutal lesson by Brentford

BRENTFORD 3-0 TOTTENHAM: Roberto De Zerbi has been dealt a serious reality check as his lavishly assembled side were hammered in their Premier League opener

View 2 Images Brentford made light work of Tottenham's expensively-assembled side

Roberto De Zerbi has claimed Tottenham "can't forget what happened last season" - but there was no danger of that as their losing habit continued at Brentford.

‌



The Italian kept Tottenham afloat last term, just, and after a summer that will likely see £300million spent there was a sense of a new beginning. Instead those in the away end in west London will simply have felt a sense of deja vu from last season.

‌



It felt like digesting defeat became a weekly occurrence for Tottenham and, despite boasting £100m record signing Sandro Tonali in midfield, were outclassed in every facet by the Bees, who were three goals to the good before the hour mark.

‌



Only an Igor Thiago penalty that came off the post prevented it from being 4-0 by sixty minutes. Keane Lewis-Potter had the hosts ahead inside 12 minutes with Vitaly Janelt doubling their lead by half-time.

De Zerbi threw on Mateus Fernandes and Rodrigo Bentancur to start the second-half, but they did little to turn the tide. Fernandes spent a short period as Tottenham's record buy after signing for £85m but after successive relegation he did little to prove his doubters wrong on his first run out.

‌



The Tottenham boss said on Friday: "At the end of the transfer market, I will be more accurate in my opinion. Maybe we will know now. Maybe we have to see on the pitch. To be honest everyone we are very excited but in the end the pitch speaks."

It did speak. Volumes. Tottenham's spend has dwarfed that of Brentford but Keith Andrews' side again showed that a solid system and plenty of continuity can still power over a host of multi-million signings.

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi was regularly left looking like he had no answers

‌



Jan Paul van Hecke, the £52m new centre-half in the Tottenham backline, was unable to halt the Brentford wave. Had Tottenham got the first goal of the second-half it would've been game on, instead it was game over when Michael Kayode reacted quickest from a corner to score Brentford's third.

There is talk of Savinho and Omar Marmoush both joining from Manchester City, which would add more than £100m to Tottenham's summer spend. The addition of individual quality seems to have done little to improve Tottenham's fortunes so far, so watch this space.

James Maddison appeared from the bench after spending last season out injured, which was about as positive as Tottenham's evening got.

De Zerbi has clearly added quality to his squad, but Saturday showed that moving on from last year's 17th place finish is going to be a lot harder than it may have seemed in pre-season when record signings were arriving on a weekly basis.

Sports.title: Liverpool star told he must tear up his contract to seal return to former club
Sports.content:
Liverpool star told he must tear up his contract to seal return to former club

Celta Vigo want to re-sign Liverpool midfielder Stefan Bajcetic, who has struggled with injuries and has been made available for a permanent transfer by Andoni Iraola

View 2 Images Stefan Bajcetic could leave Liverpool (Image: Nikki Dyer/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool midfielder Stefan Bajcetic has been told he needs to terminate his contract in order to secure a move back to former club Celta Vigo.

‌



Bajcetic has struggled massively with injuries over the past few years and is not part of Andoni Iraola's plans this season. The 21-year-old came through the Celta Vigo academy before joining the Reds in 2020 - and he is now wanted back in Spain.

‌



Having previously been linked with Getafe, it is Vigo who are now reportedly leading the race. Bajcetic made an impact under Jurgen Klopp's management but hasn't featured for the first team in over two years, due to injuries and loan spells.

‌



He has spent time away with Red Bull Salzburg and Las Palmas and Liverpool now want to seal a permanent deal. There is a sticking point, however, with Bajcetic being asked to walk away from his Liverpool contract, which doesn't expire until June 2027.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Spanish newspaper Faro de Vigo report that his former club want him to terminate his deal early - like Mohamed Salah did this summer before joining Trabzonspor - and re-join on a free transfer. They would then put him into their under-21s side initially as a way to nurse him back to full fitness.

Liverpool have just waved goodbye to Curtis Jones, who completed a £30million (€35m) transfer to Inter Milan on Friday. But they are still keen to find a new club for Bajcetic who hasn't delivered on his initial promise.

"If he's happy and we can reach an agreement, it would be a good situation, but I'm not thinking about that right now," Celta Vigo head coach Claudio Giráldez said. "He's a homegrown player; I don't talk about players we don't have.

‌



View 2 Images Stefan Bajcetic hasn't played for Liverpool in two years (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

"If I talk about any of them, it's those who have been here before because we understand that we always have a stronger connection, and on top of that, we have a very good relationship. I coached him. If it happens, great, but I don't talk about players we don't have.”

Offloading unwanted players is part of Liverpool's transfer plan for the remainder of the summer transfer window, which closes on September 1.

‌



"Some deals you have to wait until the end," Iraola explained in an interview with Sky Sports this week. "But the end is the important picture, the one we will have on September 1, because it is true that we are still quite thin."

Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola remains the number one transfer target, but Liverpool have also been chasing Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh. Brighton have rejected a second bid worth £60m for Minteh and want £70m for the former Newcastle player.

Sports.title: Arsenal dealt Kenan Yildiz blow as transfer hopes ended - 'They can offer whatever'
Sports.content:
Arsenal dealt Kenan Yildiz blow as transfer hopes ended - 'They can offer whatever'

Arsenal remain in the market for a new forward but, after missing out on Vinicius Jnr, Juventus have made it clear that they will not sell Kenan Yildiz

View 2 Images Juventus star Kenan Yildiz has continued to impress in Turin (Image: Filippo Alfero - Juventus FC/Juventus FC via Getty Images)

Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti insists Arsenal "can offer whatever they like" but the Italians will not be selling Kenan Yildiz.

‌



The north Londoners failed with an initial enquiry for Yildiz earlier this summer and the Old Lady have now made it clear they're not prepared to entertain the forward's sale.

‌



Juventus are ultimately in no hurry to sell and have the 21-year-old tied down on a contract until 2030, which he signed back in February. Yildiz scored 11 times in 47 outings last term and his displays saw him named the Serie A Rising Star of the Season.

‌



Yildiz has continued to blossom since heading to Juventus as a free agent from the Bayern academy in 2022 and Spalletti is now adamant that, regardless of what figure is produce, the club will not sell their young star.

Arteta's frontline is already was stocked with the Premier League champions boasting one of the best squads on the planet. Already they are having to leave out individuals who were once regulars. Gabriel Martinelli was a headline omission on Friday night.

Sports.title: Man Utd told new urgent transfer need after awful opening-day defeat to Hull City
Sports.content:
Man Utd told new urgent transfer need after awful opening-day defeat to Hull City

Manchester United have been urged to add attacking reinforcements before the summer ends after they struggled during their shock loss at Hull

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko, Man Utd's only natural striker, was named on the bench for the loss at Hull

Former Manchester United midfielder Owen Hargreaves believes a new striker is needed at Old Trafford because they "didn’t look like scoring" during their loss at Hull.

‌



United were stunned in their Premier League opener by the newly promoted side, and left without even bothering the scoresheet. Benjamin Sesko started the game on the bench, only coming on for the final quarter of the game. Marcus Rashford also appeared as a substitute.

‌



Matheus Cunha began as United's central point in attack but Hargreaves would like to see another No 9 arrive on the red side of Manchester, citing it as an area of concern.

‌



The former player referenced Michael Carrick's biggest successes, which came when they were able to play on the break, but against a Hull side that sat deep and without a genuine No 9 on the pitch, they were stifled in attack.

Hargreaves told TNT Sports: "I think they could probably do with another striker option. I think that showed today, Sesko didn’t start and Cunha played a little bit deeper. He’s a 10, and plays very effective off the left.

"But I do think with (Carlos) Baleba coming into the team, it is a good squad and it is a top four squad, I just think they were at their best last season counter attacking teams. Sports.content:
Crystal Palace star stretchered off in tears as injury nightmare returns on opening day

Crystal Palace's 2-0 defeat at Everton came with a further blow after defender Chadi Riad was stretchered off, having sustained a nasty-looking knee injury

View 2 Images Chadi Riad was stretchered off after being injured (Image: Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

Crystal Palace star Chadi Riad was in tears after sustaining what looked like a serious injury on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

‌



Riad appeared to twist his left knee while defending a cross from Vitaliy Mykolenko in the second half against Everton. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson immediately waved for medical treatment, with the Morocco international in obvious pain and distress.

‌



He pulled his shirt over his head and was in tears as he was stretchered off to warm applause at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Riad was replaced by Takehiro Tomiyasu in the 72nd minute of the 2-0 defeat.

‌



Palace wrote on X: "We're right behind you, Chadi." The 23-year-old's time at the Premier League club has been marred by injuries.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hints at new role for Bruno Fernandes as Man Utd hold future talks
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hints at new role for Bruno Fernandes as Man Utd hold future talks

Turkish giants Galatasaray were plotting a €50million (£43m) bid for Bruno Fernandes, but Manchester United have moved to open talks with him over a new contract

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has touched on Bruno Fernandes' future (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has hinted that he'll rotate Bruno Fernandes this season in a bid to get the best out of the Manchester United star. Fernandes, 31, enjoyed his best individual season to date last term, breaking the Premier League assist record with 21 while helping United qualify for the Champions League.

‌



But there is some doubt over the Red Devils captain's long-term future, having entered the final year of his contract at Old Trafford. Turkish giants Galatasaray had planned to test United's resolve by offering €50million (£43m) for his signature.

‌



Now, though, United are in talks with Fernandes and his representatives over a new deal. The Portuguese wants to stay and Carrick has pledged to 'look after him' ahead of what could be a gruelling campaign for his side, as they prepare to fight on all fronts unlike the 2025-26 season.

‌



"I've said quite a lot about Bruno, he's been a big part of the team and the club over recent times and had a huge impact, so he'll continue to do that,' Carrick stated ahead of United's abject 2-0 defeat away to Hull on Saturday.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"In terms of the games and how it comes, hopefully he stays fit and he's in good shape. But yeah, there's the element talking about the squad and the depth, and as we go through the season and the waves and the momentum and keeping the boys in good form, but keeping them fresh as well.

"So Bruno's part of that. He's a big player for us, he's obviously our captain, but there's still elements where we need to look after him."

Part of why Fernandes has been so successful since joining the Red Devils in January 2020 has been his immaculate fitness record. The midfielder has only missed five games through injury in that time for both club and country.

‌



But with the signings of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and soon Carlos Baleba, Carrick has more options in midfield. Mason Mount also enjoyed a promising pre-season before he suffered a small hamstring tear.

Should Manchester United give Bruno Fernandes a new contract? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes is out of contract in 2027 (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

‌



"I know we've got a good midfield," Carrick added. "We've brought in some really top players and really good characters, which is important.

"We're trying to improve the squad all the time. As it stands now, we've got some very good, top midfielders to choose from. So I think we've improved that.

"You need a solid foundation through the middle of the team. I think if you look at all the great teams over the years, the spine is really strong. We're conscious of that, and I think we've got a good spine of the team right now."

Sports.title: Dismal Man Utd sent brutal reality check after opening day defeat by Hull - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Dismal Man Utd sent brutal reality check after opening day defeat by Hull - 5 talking points

HULL CITY 2-0 MANCHESTER UNITED: Newly-promoted Tigers get their Premier League campaign off to a roaring start by outplaying and easily beating an abject United side

View 5 Images Michael Carrick had no answer to Hull City (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United kicked off their Premier League season with a woeful defeat by Hull City in Michael Carrick's first game as permanent manager. Having arrived on Humberside full of optimism, they left having put in one of the worst performances in recent memory.

‌



Hull took the lead when Semi Ajayi smashed in a loose ball from a corner in the 17th minute. It was 2-0 to the newly-promoted side in the 38th minute when Regan Slater's fantastic free-kick was nodded in by Nobel Mendy.

‌



United went in at the half-time break having seen 70 per cent of the ball but having truly tested Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis once with Bryan Mbeumo's effort at the back post.

‌



Carrick reacted by sending on Marcus Rashford for Patrick Dorgu at half-time but got zero reaction from his players, who remained sloppy in possession and lacking intensity out of it. Their first real chance came in the 78th minute, when Hull had substituted their two starting centre-backs, with Tzolakis saving from Mbeumo one-on-one.

In truth they didn't even huff and puff. United mustered next to nothing of note and were deservedly beaten by organised and determined opponents. Here are the talking points.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. Lammens powerless

United goalkeeper Lammens had already been forced into making three decent stops before Hull hit the front. The Belgian pushed away a header from Ollie McBurnie, tipped over Ryan Giles' shanked cross and kept out another from McBurnie just before Ajayi buried it.

Lammens has provided a solid and calming presence at the back since his arrival from Royal Antwerp 11 months ago and it was his defence who let him down in the early stages. Luke Shaw lost John Egan at the front post, Ayden Heaven lost McBurnie at the back post and Ajayi was completely unmarked to power home the rebound after Lammens' save came back off the post.

‌



View 5 Images Semi Ajayi opened the scoring for Hull (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

2. Direct and deadly

Hull's game plan was obvious right from the off. Get the ball wide and put it into the box to challenge United in the air. McBurnie is the perfect striker for this tactic; aggressive and awkward. But it was their centre-backs who did the damage from set pieces.

On both occasions the delivery was exceptional, flat and fast. But the lack of leadership and presence in the United defence was remarkable, with Harry Maguire's fabled 'slabhead' nowhere to be seen. Hull's aggression clearly unsettled United, yet it was their quality from dead balls which did the damage.

‌



View 5 Images Nobel Mendy put Hull 2-0 up with a header (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

3. United way off the pace

When you start a new season, the hope is that your players will be highly motivated and raring to go. There was only one side who that appeared to be the case for. United were slow to the ball, lost duel after duel and looked all at sea while defending.

Watching on, it was hard not to wonder whether any other top Premier League sides would still be happy with the statis in defence, with Shaw in his 13th season with the club and Maguire still first-choice at the start of another season.

‌



It was little better in central midfield, either, where new arrivals Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos failed to offer much protection without the ball, or push United forward on the ball. The tactical set-up frequently left players occupying the same positions in the centre of the pitch.

View 5 Images Manchester United's new-look midfield struggled (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

4. Tenacious Tigers

Not many people have given Hull a chance of staying in the Premier League this season after coming up via the play-offs. The Tigers conceded a whopping 66 goals in the Championship last season, but turned it on when it mattered in May.

‌



On this evidence, Sergej Jakirović has a plan for keeping them up. His five-man defence didn't look defensive, with wingbacks Giles and Lewie Coyle getting forward and putting crosses into the box. Mendy made the perfect start on debut, meaning that club-record signing Tzolakis barely had anything to do.

View 5 Images Konstantinos Tzolakis had a comfortable time in goal (Image: Getty Images)

5. Ponderous and toothless

United were supposed to come out after the half-time break on a mission. They were supposed to get Bruno Fernandes on the ball and turn it around through sheer willpower. But it was simply just more of the same lacklustre stuff.

Article continues below

Tielemans looked well off the pace. Heaven's performance was riddled with errors. Fernandes' trademark defence-splitting passes were nowhere to be seen. Matheus Cunha, dropping deep time and again, was completely bypassed. Rashford didn't return a hero. Mbeumo looked the most threatening, but really that is grasping at straws. It's back to the drawing board after this shambolic display.

Sports.title: 'I played against Gerrard, Lampard and Scholes – one was a tougher opponent'
Sports.content:
'I played against Gerrard, Lampard and Scholes – one was a tougher opponent'

Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard and Paul Scholes regularly locked horns during their illutrious careers

View 3 Images Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard and Paul Scholes were part of a long-running debate in the 2000s (Image: Getty Images)

A former Premier League star found Paul Scholes a tougher opponent than either Steven Gerrard or Frank Lampard. The trio are among the most celebrated players of their era and were key figures for England.

‌



Scholes often found himself the odd man out for his country, with Sven Goran Eriksson often shunting him out to the left flank to accommodate the other two, which led to his early retirement from the international scene in 2004 at the age of 29.

‌



That came amid a long-running debate over whether Gerrard or Lampard was the better player and whether they could play together. However, according to former Blackburn and Birmingham midfielder Barry Ferguson, Manchester United's Scholes was the hardest man to play against.

‌



He told William Hill's podcast, The Warm-Up with Chris Boyd and Chris Sutton: "Paul Scholes was the toughest opponent I faced in the Premier League.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"He could do everything with a football. I could say the likes of Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard, Roy Keane and Patrick Vieira because they were all world-class players, but I didn't like playing against Scholes."

‌



Paul Scholes handed six-month driving ban after being taken to court twice in two days READ MORE :

Frank Lampard's incredible net worth with celeb wife blows away all Premier League rivals READ MORE :

Explaining the difficulty of facing Scholes, the Scot added: "I never knew where he was or what he was going to do and he had a nasty side to him as well.

"But he really could do anything he wanted with a football, he was top class. The other players I mentioned were all top class, but there was just something about Scholes.

View 3 Images Scholes was constantly compared to Gerrard and Lampard (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"You couldn't pin him down, you didn’t know where he was, and he had a range of passing which was ridiculous. He was a top player."

Scholes, one of the most decorated players in Man United's history, is now a pundit and football director at League Two Salford City, where he is a former co-owner. Scholes hasn't dipped his toe into full-time management like Gerrard and Lampard.

View 3 Images Barry Ferguson played against all three (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Gerrard has had spells at Rangers, Aston Villa and Saudi side Al-Ettifaq. After stints at Derby County, Chelsea (twice) and Everton, Lampard led Coventry City to the Championship title last season.

New Zealand outscored hosts South Africa ‌five tries to one to win ​the first Test 33-16 at Ellis Park on ​Saturday and go one-up ‌in the four-match series.

The Boks led 13-12 at half-time, but New Zealand took over in the second half to close it out and end South Africa's unbeaten streak.

The All Blacks had ​been underdogs going into the first international of their eight-match tour ​but took full ⁠advantage of the ⁠home side's numerous handling errors and ill discipline ‌for a statement victory that ended a 12-match winning streak for ‌the Springboks and will rock the confidence of the world champions.

Sports.title: Bolt set to play Sunday league football for Manchester side
Sports.content:
Usain Bolt: From sprint stardom to Sunday league - athletics icon set for Wythenshawe Vets bow

Usain Bolt is registered to play for a Sunday league team in Manchester

Usain Bolt is registered to play for a Sunday league team in Manchester, with the Olympic champion set to make another foray into football.

The former sprint star, who still holds the world records for the 100m and 200m, has appeared on the squad list for Wythenshawe FC Veterans over-35s on the Football Association Full-Time website.

The team play in the Cheshire Veterans League, and feature a side made up of former top-level professionals.

Managed by former Manchester City and Republic of Ireland midfielder Stephen Ireland, the line-up also includes Danny Drinkwater, Antonio Valencia, Joleon Lescott, Emile Heskey, Marc Albrighton and Papiss Cisse.

Bolt, 40, is a major football fan, and has harboured an ambition to build a professional career in the sport since retiring following the World Championships in 2017.

Bolt still holds the world records for the 100m and 200m

His athletic career saw him win eight gold medals across three Olympics, and skyrocket to global fame.

The Jamaican became known for his trademark victory pose.

The star filed a patent application for the distinctive stance to market a range of products including sunglasses, jewellery, hats and sporting goods.

He briefly played for the Australian A-League team Central Coast Mariners.

The Manchester United supporter has also been a regular participant in Soccer Aid charity matches over the last decade.

He has also trained with other clubs across the world, most notably German heavyweights Borussia Dortmund.

Wythenshawe, yet to announce Bolt's signing, have been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Everton outclass wasteful Palace in Premier League opener
Sports.content:
Everton made a winning start to the new Premier League campaign by beating Crystal Palace 2-0 thanks to classy goals from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Thierno Barry.

David Moyes's side ruthlessly punished their visitors, under the new charge of Frenchman Pierre Sage, for a series of missed opportunities, scoring either side of the break to register their first opening-weekend win for five years.

The performance was symptomatic of a team maturing under the influence of wily Moyes. The Everton boss entrusted 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong with a midfield role alongside new signing Hayden Hackney. Armstrong was involved in the first goal and Hackney connected to a superb second.

The teenager's hustle turned the ball over for Dewsbury-Hall to jinx inside Chris Richards and pick out the far corner just before half-time. Shortly after the break, Hackney's quick thinking from a free-kick got Iliman Ndiaye away and he picked out Barry with a cutting cross.

Image: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall celebrates with Iliman Ndiaye after scoring Everton's opener

"Everton did a professional job. Armstrong and Hackney were very good," reflected Tim Sherwood on Soccer Saturday.

Palace, meanwhile, faded horribly after a promising opening. Their conversion issues appear to have been carried over from last season, with Jean-Philippe Mateta guilty of spurning a prime opportunity when the game was goalless, adding to the frustration of Eddie Nketiah's earlier miss. The former Arsenal forward drew a world-class save from Jordan Pickford but should have scored with a curling effort that was tipped onto the woodwork.

Palace's expected goals tally (2.04) was their highest in a Premier League game without scoring since December 2018.

Palace's openness suited Everton

Sky Sports' Tim Sherwood:

"I don't think there's any danger of Palace getting relegated or dragged into that sort of argument. They play a really attractive style of football but just sometimes you have to pick when to play open. They played right into the hands of Everton.

"Everton counter-attacked; they've got quality and pace on the counter and they've punished them.

"There's been some fantastic football played by Palace but they're on the wrong end of the result."

The key moments from Hill Dickinson Stadium

17: SAVE! Pickford denies Nketiah with a save-of-the-season contender, pushing his strike onto the frame of the goal.

38: POST! Nketiah picks out Mateta with a teasing low cross but the striker can only plant against the foot of the post.

43: GOAL! Dewsbury-Hall beats Dean Henderson with a sublime strike from a difficult angle.

53: GOAL! Barry rises highest to Ndiaye's clever cross and heads past Henderson.

68: SETBACK! Chadi Riad is stretchered off with a worrying knee injury.

Moyes praises midfield duo

Everton boss David Moyes:

"Both teams had periods in the game. We could easily have been a couple of goals down. It was a worldie save [from Pickford to deny Nketiah]. It could have gone the other way.

"Once we got the first goal, it settled us. That mattered. We had big moments, Kiernan's goal was important. We managed the game well after that and contained Palace really well."

On the midfield duo: "They done great, I'm really pleased. Harrison is earning his place in the team, he's got an opportunity here, where at other clubs he might not have. He's showed lots of good things.

"With Hayden, sometimes boys from the Championship need time, but he's done well. I have to give him praise for how quickly he's picked things up."

Sage criticises Palace's slow pace of play

Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage:

"The first half we play as we decided but the second half we let the opponent score the second goal. When we had the ball, we don't play with speed. When you don't play quick, the opponent is comfortable.

"We didn't create so much in the second half. We have to be quicker in our play to be more assertive to take decisions quickly.

"We don't deserve to win this game but we deserve to win the first half. We miss something today. It's about us, we have to take the lesson and be better for the next game."

Sports.title: Leicester booed off after nightmare defeat to Burton
Sports.content:
Burton Albion stunned Leicester City at the King Power Stadium, as the former Premier League champions were booed off after being beaten 2-1 by Gary Bowyer's side.

Matthew Dennis and Kgaogelo Chauke ensured Leicester's woeful start was punished before Russell Martin's men, who then saw Oliver Skipp receive a straight red card, finally showed some fight.

Only five minutes had passed when a move involving the excellent Charlie Webster ended with Kyran Lofthouse slipping the ball through to Dennis before he fired past Alex McCarthy. City fans were in uproar 20 minutes later after seeing Chauke react first when Lofthouse's shot was deflected into his path.

But when Skipp walked for a cynical foul on Curtis Tilt on the 29-minute mark, Wes Burn's first strike since joining from Ipswich - converting at the far post from Will Alves' cross - prevented the atmosphere from turning truly mutinous.

Harry Souttar headed over the bar and substitute Tommy Watson went close as City tried to mount a comeback.

Albion's defensive grit helped them overcome late pressure to claim a memorable victory.

Martin questions Leicester hunger after defeat

Leicester boss Russell Martin:

"One team wanted it during the opening 25 minutes and were hungry. We weren't, definitely not hungry enough.

"After that, we were but we were down to 10 men with a nothing-to-lose mentality. We were dominant for periods after that, which isn't easy when you're down to 10. But it's hard at that point.

"We have to have some really honest conversations. I take responsibility as a manager, so if I haven't prepared them psychologically well enough, we must look at that.

"But fundamentals are fundamentals, regardless of how you play. Those don't change.

"We can't play the way we want to play without those fundamentals. And they just weren't there to begin with.

"We've already watched the goals back as a group and highlighted bits that we don't want to be us. We have to make sure that is our worst 25 minutes of the season."
