Sports.title: Norris 'still believes' in title fightback after Dutch GP pole
Sports.content:
Lando Norris feels it's "nice to know there's a possibility" he could stay in the battle to retain his Formula 1 world championship, after taking pole position for the Dutch Grand Prix.

​​​​​​The McLaren driver produced a dominant race victory in the final race before the sport's summer break in Hungary and made it two successive pole positions by topping qualifying in Zandvoort on Saturday.

Norris' pole came after he had reduced his deficit to championship leader Kimi Antonelli to 90 points by finishing ahead of the Mercedes driver in the Sprint earlier on Saturday.

In qualifying, Norris edged out the other Mercedes of George Russell for pole, with Antonelli having to settle for third behind his team-mate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris claims lap that secured him Dutch Grand Prix pole position was not his 'finest lap'.

Norris said: "There's no point in thinking about it. Just focus on tomorrow. I honestly don't care what I'm doing next weekend or the weekend after.

"It's nice to know there's a possibility."

Antonelli leads Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton at the top of the standings by 53 points, with Saturday's Sprint winner Russell a further three points back. Norris, who's fifth in the standings, also trails Ferrari's Charles Leclerc by 11 points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix.

Norris appeared to be in a head-to-head battle with his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri for last year's title before Red Bull's Max Verstappen surged back into contention and eventually finished just two points behind the champion.

Verstappen's cause was aided by both McLarens being disqualified from the Las Vegas Grand Prix and a strategic error from the eventual constructors' champions at the Qatar Grand Prix, which Norris referenced as he plotted his own 2026 comeback.

"Of course, I'm hoping both Mercedes get a double DSQ in Vegas like we did and decide not to box in Qatar for a free pit stop," Norris said.

"So, as long as they make the same mistakes, it'll probably be just as easy, but every year is different.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment that Lando Norris claims victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix!

"For me, we're still trying to play catch up with certain things, but I'm getting everything out of it for now and that's all I can be pleased about.

"I'm happy. It's still a very long way to go. I'm optimistic. I still believe that it's possible and that's all I need for now."

Russell: Title mine to gain, not lose

Russell, who must leapfrog Norris on Sunday to complete a Sprint-Grand Prix double in Zandvoort, believes he is benefiting from his position in the championship having removed pressure.

The 28-year-old started the season as the clear title favourite but has been surprisingly outperformed by Antonelli, who doesn't turn 20 until two days after Sunday's race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch George Russell win the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint, as Lando Norris loses second place to Charles Leclerc.

Russell said: "After the break, I just feel way more relaxed. I don't feel I've got anything to lose. The pressure's off. I'm just going to go out, enjoy it.

"I don't even really feel in a fight. It's not mine to lose, it's mine to gain. That's the mentality I've got, and I feel it's going to help me. I'm just enjoying driving."

Despite his change in mindset, Russell shared his belief that the title race could swing very quickly over the 11 remaining rounds that follow Sunday's race.

"There's more points on offer from this point until the end of the season than we've had so far," Russell said.

"It changes so, so quick. We already saw it earlier in the season - at one point I was almost 70 points down, got within 25, went up to 60. It's ebbs and flows and it's far from over. Long way to go.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell predicts a 'close Dutch Grand Prix, which will 'swing slightly in our favour'

"I think the Ferraris are looking great. Lando's been on pole for the last two races as well, so you can't count anybody out.

"We've got these upgrades coming. We've got to hope that they work. It only takes one issue with an upgrade and it doesn't work as you expect, and before you know it, you're not fighting at the front week in, week out, and they can be big points missed."

Antonelli: Weekend has been a wake-up call

While Antonelli could quite easily end the weekend with a bigger title lead than he begun it with, the Italian is already describing it as a "wake-up call" for him.

Antonelli made an error in the first part of Sprint Qualifying on Friday that damaged his car and left him compromised for the rest of the session, which contributed to him only managing to take fifth on the grid, before he finished the 24-lap race in fourth.

The 19-year-old, who is driving just his second season in F1, was also frustrated with himself for making an error in on his final run in Saturday's full-length qualifying session.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli admitted his confidence was 'hurt a little' after a difficult start to weekend, but remains optimistic about starting P3 for the Dutch Grand Prix.

Antonelli said: "I don't feel any extra pressure, but it was a very good wake-up call this weekend, that you can never lower your guard.

"Because when you do that, I did a mistake yesterday and today I did a mistake in Q3.

"It's not that I'm driving more tense or anything, but it's just I feel this weekend is a good wake-up call and to just, again, put things in the right place at the right time and just deliver the result when it counts."

Sports.title: 'The car is better for the race' - Hamilton 'optimistic' of Ferrari turnaround
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes his Ferrari car is in a "better place" after changes going into Dutch Grand Prix qualifying and that the team can still be "optimistic" for Sunday's race despite starting on the third row.

​​​​​​Ferrari are Mercedes' nearest challengers in both world championship races but qualified three tenths of a second away from pole at Zandvoort, F1's first event back after its summer break.

Fifth-fastest Hamilton and sixth-fastest Charles Leclerc will start behind both Mercedes and McLaren cars for a race that Lando Norris starts on pole position.

But fifth on the grid represented a step forward for Hamilton compared to the earlier Sprint sessions when he had qualified and finished seventh.

"Much different session, much different car," said Hamilton, who pipped Leclerc to the head of the third row with his final lap of Q3, to Sky Sports F1 after main qualifying.

"In Practice, the car felt great and was consistent but there are always areas you feel you can improve so we made subtle changes to try and fix those improvements and it flipped the car on its head and it was horrible through Sprint Qualifying and the Sprint. I had no confidence in the balance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix.

"We made all these changes into Qualifying so I was learning a new car again, a new balance which I'm much happier with - trying to progress with it and learning with only like six laps was a challenge.

"Also all the Mercedes [powered cars] are ahead and we know we have a bit of a deficit on power so I think our race pace should be better and the car is better for the race."

Saturday's earlier Sprint race had appeared to prove that Ferrari's car was a competitive proposition around the twisty, undulating Zandvoort circuit.

Leclerc finished second, 1.3s behind winner George Russell, with his overtake on Norris with six laps to go the only change of position in the top 10 after the opening lap.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton had a nervous moment during Dutch GP qualifying where he found gravel just out of the first corner.

And despite the track not being especially friendly for overtaking, Hamilton is not ruling out the prospect of the SF-26 getting in the mix at the front again.

"I feel optimistic," he said.

"Fifth is not the greatest but it could be far worse, so I'm grateful to be there but of course I wish I was up further ahead.

"However, our race pace was good in the Sprint. Charles had good race pace and the car is in a better place

"Hopefully with the right strategy and right execution I think hopefully we can challenge the cars ahead."

What went wrong for Leclerc after Sprint promise?

Leclerc's overtake on Norris for second place with six laps to go in the Sprint had proved a relative surprise given he had been the only one of the front runners to run the 24-lap race on the soft tyres, a compound which is initially the fastest but on which performance falls away more quickly.

He had therefore been tipped to contend for pole but the Monegasque never ultimately appeared a contender in any of the three knockout sections.

"I don't think the conditions played a role," said Leclerc. "I think we changed the power strategies a bit too much throughout qualifying then in Q3 I had some weird things going on, so we lost a bit of performance there.

"At no time during qualifying [did I have] the potential of pole."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix Sprint race.

Dropped to sixth on Sunday's grid thanks to Hamilton's late improvement, Leclerc added on his race prospects: "Realistically it will be very difficult to overtake on track but we will do our best and see where we end up.

"Starting from sixth doesn't make our life easy, so it will be a tough race but the pace is there so I hope we can do something with strategy and offset ourselves to the others."

Team principal Frederic Vasseur, though, took heart from their Sprint performance and said the fact the race was likely to be a multi-stop affair could play in their favour.

"The race pace in the Sprint was very strong so we will try to come back," said the Frenchman.

"We had a good comparison between the two [tyre] compounds [in the Sprint] which is probably the best preparation we can have for the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc overtakes Lando Norris in a 'beautiful' move to take second place.

"It's very difficult to overtake. It will probably be two or three pit stops which mean everything is open."

He also said the latest round of SF-26 upgrades, which include a new floor which was thought to be added to the car after the weekend's sole practice session on Friday, were performing as expected.

"It's working as per the plan," added Vasseur. "From the beginning of the season, every time we brought something it's worked per the plan.

"It's a positive side of the development this year. We are bringing a lot of upgrades at each race, not big ones, so we are not expecting to [gain] five tenths per race. But it's working as expected."

Sports.title: Carrick defends dismal Man Utd loss: 'It was never going to be perfect'
Sports.content:
Man Utd boss Michael Carrick focused on the "good things" his side had done despite a dismal 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull City on the opening day of the new season.

United were outfought and outplayed by a Hull side widely tipped to return to the Sky Bet Championship this season at the MKM Stadium, with two goals from set pieces giving the Tigers a richly deserved victory and their first over United in more than half a century.

The loss punctured the optimism around Old Trafford at the start of Carrick's first full season in charge.

He had picked up more points than anyone else since returning to the club in January and had overseen the arrival of Andre Santos and Youri Tielemans - with Carlos Baleba likely to follow - before a shock defeat to a Hull side missing as many as eight first-team players brought things crashing back to earth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Hull and Manchester United.

Despite losing 63 per cent of their duels and two thirds of their headers in a first half where Hull scored both their goals, Carrick said: "We did some good things today and it will get lost. We have to find answers but because we lose one game, it doesn't mean everything needs dissecting."

He added to TNT Sport: "Some of it was OK, there's bits to improve on. It was never going to be perfect, but going behind and giving ourselves a lot to do makes it more difficult.

"It was a typical one of those games, with a newly-promoted team at home. You can't give them much, they've got a lot to hold on to.

"After that, we had moments and opportunities but we didn't have the spark to put the chances away or create any more. We're bitterly disappointed with the result, but we won't let it knock us."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan gives us his three things to take away from Manchester United's loss to Hull City on the opening day of the season.

Captain Bruno Fernandes struck a more critical tone of his team-mates and said he had seen it all before as United were punished for their lack of aggression and intensity.

"It was the same mistakes we made last season, every away game we give too much of the ball to the opponent," he told TNT Sport.

"In the first 20 minutes, their goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

"We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set-plays and not concede these type of goals.

"Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment. We knew before the game set-pieces would be a big part of their game."

Your views: Carrick already under pressure

Jay: "Carrick under pressure straight away. Eddie Howe anyone?"

Marek: "The job is too big for Carrick, he did a great job at the end of last season but Utd need a proven winner in charge."

JB75: "It was quite obvious we need a strong centre back, left back and striker to support when Sesko is not available. Cunha was playing so deep at times going into a midfield that was 5 deep with Hull. And the midfield just didn't seem to have the legs, not a convincing start."

Big Dave: "Same old United, no paces, lack of movement, and a total lack of effort, shocking performance, seems like nothing has changed at United."

Analysis: Hull's tactics worked but this was about fight, and United's lack of it

Sky Sports' Ron Walker:

"Hull nailed their set-up with a back five too physical for Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, and wing-backs in Lewie Coyle and Ryan Giles who served target man Oli McBurnie well.

"But this was about fight and spirit over anything on Sergej Jakirovic's tactics board. Winning almost two thirds of both their duels and headers before the break was just reward for the intensity, energy and belief they brought to the game - and United did not match it.

"It was inevitable that the Tigers would be fired up after riding the wave of promotion, but it felt as though Michael Carrick's side hadn't realised. They failed to do the basics right and were punished.

"A video of McBurnie dribbling around a static Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans will rightly do the rounds on social media tonight.

"People may point to a lack of quality in the Man Utd side but without the hunger and desire to do those basics, it would have made little difference."

Sports.title: Swansea & Sheff Utd play out dour draw
Sports.content:
Sheffield United put their latest financial worries to one side to earn a gritty draw against a toothless Swansea.

It was a second successive goalless scoreline for the Blades, who drew 0-0 at Birmingham last weekend.

Manager Chris Wilder and his team may have had their build-up distracted by the threat of a 12-point deduction for the club due to unpaid debts, but they looked focused and disciplined, if not very threatening.

They managed two shots on target, compared to a Sky Bet Championship low of zero last week, but that was one more than the Swans mustered.

The home side started with Adam Idah up front, sent on Zan Vipotnik, and ended up throwing on new signing Ross Stewart for his debut late on.

But all three failed to fire as Swansea were unable to make it successive wins at the start of the season following last week's victory at Stoke.

Despite the perfect conditions, neither side was able to display much quality in an error-strewn opening half hour.

Swansea applied most of the pressure and should have gone ahead when a floated corner from Josh Tymon in the 19th minute was allowed to bounce in the goalmouth, but none of his team-mates were able to take advantage.

Home winger Moussa Yeo then cut in from the left and was allowed two bites of the cherry to set up Elijah Just.

But the low grade stuff was summed up by the New Zealand World Cup star's total miskick from 12 yards out.

When the visitors did make a rare foray forward, midfielder Harrison Burrows was shown a yellow card for diving after what referee Tom Nield judged a fair tackle from Filip Lissah.

The Blades finally roused themselves in the late stages of the half and almost snatched the lead when Callum O'Hare's volley struck the underside of the bar.

Joe Rothwell's rebound effort was then charged down and Swansea managed to clear their lines.

Idah's strength opened up the Sheffield United defence early in the second half, but team-mate Joseph Opoku was unable to profit as his shot lacked power and direction.

The next opportunity spurned was down to the Blades' centre-back Mark McGuinness who sliced wide with a volley from a free-kick.

Swansea head coach Vitor Matos swapped Idah for last season's top scorer Vipotnik on the hour mark and followed that with a raft of other substitutions.

But the changes failed to lift the tempo for the home side and it was the Sheffield United striking pair of O'Hare and Patrick Bamford who looked the more threatening.

O'Hare cleverly got in behind Swansea's defence, but his cross was not anticipated by a teammate.

Swansea had a late surge but their finishing remained poor.

The managers

Swansea's Vitor Matos:

"I think last week we played better football, but each game has different kinds of problems.

"We knew this one would be much more in terms of duels, in terms of man-marking, so you need to have different tools for these kinds of games."

Sheffield United's Chris Wilder:

"I said to the players there would be a lot of eyes on us today to see how we react to what's happened in the week.

"Their job is to be professional footballers, get on with the job, and they've done that to great effect, in my opinion.

"It goes without saying how proud I am of my football club, the supporters and the team. There's a genuine connection there."

Sports.title: Brentford v Tottenham: Premier League – live
Sports.content:
2m ago 14.30 EDT Roberto De Zerbi goes over to clap the Spurs fans. He has the good grace to look sheepish. He doesn’t get much back, and one punter in a Spurs top stands, arms spread out, palms up, top lip kinked quizzically, the internationally recognised pose for What The Eff Was That?! But while this story can’t not be about Tottenham – they were abysmal, and everything’s gong to be viewed through the lens of their summer spending spree – it really should be mainly Brentford focused. The Bees were superb to a man, though one stood out, the debutant Mamadou Sangaré, who modestly claps the Brentford support before being shoved forward by Michael Kayode, who makes sure his new mate receives his flowers. What a cheer Sangaré’s given! And he’s worth it, having set up two goals and buzzed around a pitch that he quickly made his own. A new Premier League star is born. Share

10m ago 14.22 EDT FULL TIME: Brentford 3-0 Tottenham Hotspur Brentford beat Spurs at home for the first time since Bill Nicholson’s playing days. View image in fullscreen Not the start Roberto De Zerbi was hoping for. Spurs second best. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Share Updated at 14.25 EDT

11m ago 14.21 EDT 90 min +4: On Sky, Alan Smith names Mamadou Sangaré as his player of the match. There can be no complaints. What a debut. Share

12m ago 14.20 EDT 90 min +3: The resulting corner is punched clear by Kinsky, then sent sailing miles over the bar by Yarmoliuk. Share

13m ago 14.20 EDT 90 min +2: Lewis-Potter juggles his way down the left, past Bentancur with ease, before winning a corner off Robertson. Share

14m ago 14.18 EDT 90 min +1: Wilson scampers down the right and shoots from a tight angle. Van Hecke diverts the shot into the side netting. The resulting corner is headed harmlessly wide right by Schade. Share

15m ago 14.17 EDT 90 min: There will be four additional minutes. Share

17m ago 14.16 EDT 88 min: Wilson gets the better of Tonali down the right. That was too easy. He crosses for Schade, who attempts a cute backflick. Too cute. Too far out to be trying that. Spurs clear. Share

18m ago 14.14 EDT 87 min: Maddison slithers into the Brentford box from the left. It’s a positive run, and he’s within his rights to shoot from a tight angle, but he cuts back for Solanke instead, and his team-mate’s shot is blocked. Share

19m ago 14.13 EDT 86 min: Gray, who became Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain this afternoon, is replaced by Udogie. For the record, and for what it’s worth, the armband is passed on to Maddison. Share

20m ago 14.12 EDT 85 min: Damsgaard swings a corner in from the left. Kinsky gathers. Spurs will be desperate to hear the full-time whistle. Share

21m ago 14.12 EDT 84 min: Wilson comes on for Thiago. Share

21m ago 14.11 EDT 82 min: Tel has a whack from distance. It’s not good. Miles wide left. Meanwhile there’s more on the Dundonian stramash, courtesy of Stephen McCrossan: “The ‘mistaken identity’ booking in the Dundee derby was baffling. The Dundee player was apparently booked for standing on the ball. Hilarious.” Ha! Shades of Hearts winger Tommy Murray “having a seat” against Rangers back in the day. A story worth revisiting … The Joy of Six: showboating Read more Share

24m ago 14.08 EDT 80 min: This game is petering out, which is probably the best Spurs can hope for. The same can’t be said for events north of the border, as Simon McMahon reports: “A lot of effing and jeffing at Tannadice as Dundee score again. It could always be worse I suppose. I could be a Spurs fan.” Share

27m ago 14.06 EDT 78 min: Janelt is booked for a flagrant tug on Maddison. Share

28m ago 14.05 EDT 77 min: Schade makes good down the right and finds Thiago at the near post. The striker flicks wide under pressure from Senesi. Brentford in search of a fourth. Share

29m ago 14.04 EDT 76 min: … Anthony, on the edge of the D, slices harmlessly over. At which point the new boy Sangare is replaced, departing to a great ovation. A hero is born. He earns a big hug from his manager too. Kayode also departs, Hickey and Damsgaard entering. Share

30m ago 14.02 EDT 75 min: Brentford continue to look lively, Anthony worming his way down the right and earning a throw. Kayode flings it long. Kinsky punches under pressure, and the ball pings out for a corner. From which … Share

32m ago 14.01 EDT 73 min: Was that the first time the word “Jeff” has been used in three consecutive MBM entries? Not sure. Anyway, it’s four now. Share

33m ago 14.00 EDT 72 min: Ah, here go the Brentford fans with “You’re getting sacked in the morning”. Jeff Necessary (69 min) got there just in time. Share

34m ago 13.59 EDT 71 min: Sangare sashays into the Spurs box from the left and takes a whack. His shot is deflected, the sting removed. But he continues to impress on debut. Meanwhile in the dugout, De Zerbi holds his head in his hands, before ranting, half at his assistant, half to himself, at high speed and with some passion, presumably using words including Eff and Jeff. Share

36m ago 13.56 EDT 69 min: Anthony bustles down the right and crosses for Schade, whose header flies straight to Kinsky. “It’s too late for the season’s first ‘you’ll be sacked in the morning’,” begins Jeff Necessary. “Enzo Maresca got that at Cardiff last week. But De Zerbi may not be far behind.” Share

38m ago 13.55 EDT 68 min: Spurs respond by switching out Moore and Richarlison for Maddison and Solanke. Share

38m ago 13.54 EDT 67 min: Brentford make a double change, replacing Jensen and Ouattara with Yarmoliuk and Anthony. Share

40m ago 13.53 EDT 65 min: Schade chases after a long ball down the right and is clipped by Bentancur. The referee absurdly waves play on, which if nothing else means he doesn’t have a decision to make, because Spurs were very light at the back and Schade was preparing to romp into all sorts of space. Share

42m ago 13.50 EDT 63 min: … and from the resulting corner, Van Hecke falls over, claiming a penalty he’s never going to get. Goal kick. Share

43m ago 13.50 EDT 62 min: Lewis-Potter misjudges Fernandes’s diagonal pass to Moore on the right. A fresh-air swipe, and suddenly Moore is one on one with the keeper! But he shoots straight at Kelleher, who nevertheless does well to turn the ball around the post. Share

44m ago 13.48 EDT 60 min: Tonali slips a pass down the left to release Robertson, who can’t find Richarlison with his cutback. Brentford then collectively butcher a three-on-two counter. It’s an open game, and that probably doesn’t augur well for the visitors. Share

47m ago 13.46 EDT 58 min: Tonali scuffs a shot from 25 yards. Easy for Kelleher. The xG is currently 3.19 to Brentford, 0.27 to Spurs. Share

48m ago 13.45 EDT 57 min: Spurs go up the other end and win a corner down the left. It’s their first of the match. Tel swings it in, and the offside flag goes up. The penalty miss is pretty much all that’s gone right for Spurs so far. As for the Dundee derby … “It’s all kicking off at Tannadice,” reports Simon McMahon. “1-0 to Dundee, and some mistaken identity VAR nonsense just before half time. To be honest I’ve no idea what’s going on, but hey, what’s new?” Share

50m ago 13.43 EDT Thiago misses penalty 55 min: Thiago steps up, sends Kinsky the wrong way … then batters his penalty off the base of the left-hand post and away! A rare opportunity for Spurs to breathe out. View image in fullscreen Igor Thiago takes the penalty and hits the post. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Share Updated at 13.57 EDT

51m ago 13.41 EDT Penalty for Brentford! 53 min: Spurs are all over the show, and as a game of pinball breaks out in their box, Bentancur barges clumsily into the back of Schade, who goes over. The referee points immediately to the spot. That was an absurd lunge, and this won’t be overturned by VAR. View image in fullscreen Brentford's Kevin Schade is fouled and awarded a penalty. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Share Updated at 13.55 EDT

53m ago 13.40 EDT 52 min: Spurs try to summon a response, Robertson making good down the left and crossing low for Moore, who finds himself one on one with Kelleher. But he shoots straight at the keeper, who parries before claiming. Share

53m ago 13.39 EDT 51 min: This is some debut from Sangare, who now has two assists to his name. Share Updated at 13.40 EDT

55m ago 13.37 EDT 50 min: On the touchline, Roberto De Zerbi fixes his stare on an imaginary point exactly 1,000 yards in the distance. Share

1h ago 13.37 EDT GOAL! Brentford 3-0 Tottenham Hotspur (Kayode 48) … but it doesn’t matter, because from the resulting corner, hit long from the right, Collins heads down for Sangare, who pearls an instant shot goalwards. Kinsky parries, a decent save from a well-struck shot, but the ball drops for Kayode, who roofs the loose ball from a couple of yards! View image in fullscreen Michael Kayode scores. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian View image in fullscreen And celebrates with teammate Igor Thiago. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Share Updated at 13.47 EDT

1h ago 13.35 EDT 47 min: Sangare piles down the left and crosses dangerously. Janelt prepares to head home but Van Hecke heads clear. Kayode throws long, and Senesi grabs a fistful of Collins’ shirt. As the ball’s blocked out for a corner, VAR has a look, but no penalty. Senesi was taking a big risk there, considering the new rules. Share Updated at 13.38 EDT

1h ago 13.33 EDT Brentford get the second half underway. Spurs have made two changes, replacing Bergvall and Gallagher with Fernandes and Bentancur. Spurs now have five debutants on the pitch. Share

1h ago 13.21 EDT Half-time postbag: Spurs sorrow special. “Have to say Spurs look absolutely miles off it so far although Brentford have been excellent. If anything, this looks as bad as last season’s Spurs. At least there are 37 games left to improve” – Martin Gamage “Last season Spurs were lousy, and they will not be better this season, just like Manchester United. It is an utter disgrace, and also a reflection on society, that players like Tonali are bought for 100 million and yet so many people live in poverty in England” – Jeff Sax “Gotta admire Tottenham’s resilience; despite failing to get relegated two years on the bounce they finally look like a proper Championship team” – Dave Estherby “In the as-it-stands table, Spurs are currently 17th. The more things change…” – Kári Tulinius “Dear old Spurs. I’m sure we all wish them well, but perhaps if they’re to be humbled again this season, better it be kept out of sight? Sympathetic MBMers would, I think, be happier were you to devote the afternoon entirely to, say, Simon McMahon’s posts from the Dundee derby. Probably also Spurs supporters” – Charles Antaki (It’s goalless at Tannadice at the moment.) Share Updated at 13.22 EDT

Roberto De Zerbi disappears down the tunnel with a face on. View image in fullscreen Are Spurs ‘Livin’ on a prayer? Jon Bon Jovi in the house. Photograph: Jordan Pettitt/PA Share Updated at 13.20 EDT

Sports.title: Burnham’s boys enjoy visit from Palace as Everton ease to opening day win
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham was in the posh seats to see how his beloved Everton would fare without the key additions that even the prime minister has voiced an opinion. No right-back, no new centre-forward, no problem: Everton contained enough quality to overcome a wasteful Crystal Palace.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Iliman Ndiaye delivered a timely reminder that, despite the missing pieces in the squad, there is pedigree and Premier League knowhow available to David Moyes as he attempts to sustain a challenge for European qualification this season.

Dewsbury-Hall swept home an outstanding finish to give Everton the lead and sweep away any lingering resentment over how last season flatlined. Ndiaye supplied the superb cross that invited Thierno Barry to seal Everton’s first opening game win since 2021. It was a brutal introduction for the new Palace manager, Pierre Sage, who lost defender Chadi Riad to a potentially serious knee injury late on.

“I spoke to the prime minister on the phone,” Moyes said. “Andy Gray came down into the office [before the game] and his assistant Peter Reid phoned down.”

Reid was Burnham’s chaperone for the day – along with a phalanx of security – and put the prime minister on the phone during his call to Moyes. His good luck message was answered, thanks in part to Palace’s profligacy.

There were no radical changes in formation or personnel from Sage for his first Premier League outing. A lack of cutting edge was familiar from the Oliver Glasner era, too. The visitors created three clear opportunities before Everton took the lead and failed to take any. Misfortune played its part in two of the chances, with Jordan Pickford’s left post struck twice, but that did not diminish the torment for Sage and the travelling support. A sense of the inevitable from Everton increased with each one.

Palace denied reports that Ismaïla Sarr had refused to play because of a desire to join Galatasaray – the Senegal international was absent due to a groin injury, according to his manager – and the disruption had no effect on their start. Eddie Nketiah created an early opportunity for Jean-Philippe Mateta, but his strike partner volleyed over at the near post.

View image in fullscreen Moved from his usual seat into the directors’ box by prime pinisterial security logistics, Andy Burnham celebrated with the Everton legend, and his good friend, Peter Reid. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock

Chance number two came from a sublime pass by Adam Wharton, the midfielder who Sage has insisted is going nowhere despite interest from Manchester City. Wharton found Nketiah free inside the area with a perfectly weighted ball over Merlin Röhl, forced to deputise at right-back in the absence of a conclusion to Everton’s almost farcical search for Séamus Coleman’s successor.

Nketiah had time to pick his spot, but Pickford produced a superb save to tip the shot on to a post. Mateta struck the same post from another Nketiah cross and Everton took full advantage of their reprieves.

Everton grew into their opening game with the summer signings Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Röhl all impressing. Creativity was initially in short supply from the home side, despite George’s constant probing on the left, until Dewsbury-Hall and Ndiaye imposed themselves on proceedings.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Dewsbury-Hall’s impact was worth the wait. The midfielder burst into life with a mazy run that ended with an appeal for handball when his shot hit Chris Richards. Play continued through Daniel Muñoz, a possible Everton right-back target, who was dispossessed by the industrious Harrison Armstrong and left a void for Dewsbury-Hall to exploit. Receiving Armstrong’s pass, the 27-year-old swept an unstoppable, angled drive into Dean Henderson’s far corner to open the season in style for Everton.

View image in fullscreen Thierno Barry outjumped Chris Richards to head Everton into a two-goal lead just after half-time. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA

Muñoz should have made amends when stealing in ahead of George to meet an inviting delivery from Daichi Kamada. Palace’s end product did not match the buildup yet again, however, and the Colombian defender guided his header wide of the far post.

Everton found the comfort of a two-goal lead when Ndiaye delivered a peach of a cross from the right. Barry, on a self-confessed mission to improve after a difficult debut season in the Premier League, rose between Richards and Jaydee Canvot to head past Henderson at close range. The departure of the unfortunate Riad on a stretcher compounded Palace’s deflating afternoon.

Sports.title: Anton Stach snatches late Leeds winner to sour Glasner’s new dawn at Forest
Sports.content:
For Anton Stach, another sweet direct free-kick to add to the back catalogue, this one souring Oliver Glasner’s first match in charge of Nottingham Forest. Only Dominik Szoboszlai eclipsed Stach’s record of three direct free-kick goals in the Premier League last season, one of those coming against Glasner’s Crystal Palace.

Stach’s latest right-foot strike earned Leeds, fresh from a near-flawless pre-season and an expensive and exciting summer in the market, a divine opening-day victory with a couple of minutes of normal time remaining.

It has been a busy few weeks for the Germany midfielder. “He even released a burger a few days ago and I never expected him to do this,” said the Leeds manager, Daniel Farke, alluding to Stach launching a burger at a city-centre eatery to raise money for charity. “He’s a bit of a weird and crazy guy.

“I expected when he was over the free-kick that he could do something special. He has done it time and time again. He surprised me [with his free-kicks] last season [but now] I trust him with everything. Last season, I would have never thought about it.”

For Forest, a few minutes before kick-off, the curtain going up on another season, a new protagonist emerged from the tunnel. Glasner, Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months, surveyed the scene from his technical area. But the start of this new dawn did not go to plan, an underwhelming performance culminating with Stach sneaking in his whipped free-kick at Matz Sels’s near post. At least Forest can put things right quickly, Leeds visiting in a Carabao Cup rematch on Tuesday.

Leeds were imposing and always looked more threatening, rationing Forest to moments. In the first half, Harry Wilson had a debut goal disallowed when the assistant referee raised his flag for offside after the Welshman, whose arrival is evidence of Leeds’ ambition, latched on to Jayden Bogle’s pushed pass. In the second, Sels’ strong left hand prevented a header by the £34m signing Tarik Muharemovic, another debutant, flying into the top corner.

Glasner, who left marquee signing Ousmane Diomande on the bench and introduced Xaver Schlager late on, puffed his cheeks as every outfield Leeds player joined the celebrations. The away end, bathed in the evening sun, was jubilant. The Forest areas began to empty.

“It was pretty clear that I can’t come with my staff, lay our hands on the shoulders [of the players], and all of a sudden we play like Real Madrid in the 70s or whatever,” Glasner said. “It was an OK performance from both teams – a typical first Premier League game after a long break and this is also now not the time to bury our heads into the sand.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Anton Stach jumps for joy after his late winner for Leeds. Photograph: Bruce Rollinson/PA

These remain early days – Nuno Espírito Santo was in charge when Forest beat Brentford in their opening game last season – but they did little to enthuse the locals. Chris Wood arrived from the bench and sent a bobbling ball wide with a first-time shot from Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected pass. Schlager replaced James McAtee for his debut, but Leeds were buoyant at the final whistle.

Only Arsenal and Manchester United scored more set-piece goals than Leeds last season, but Farke dismissed the suggestion they are more important than previously. “There is not one team who won the World Cup without a set-piece goal,” said the German, stating ability from dead balls was a factor in their summer recruitment, Wilson a case in point.

“I remember Germany 12 years ago, a crap [quarter-final] game against France: Mats Hummels header, boom, goal,” he said. “I remember magic free-kick takers: Juninho, who got this crazy curve on the ball. It is always a major part of the game, not just nowadays. Anton is perhaps not as beautiful on the eye like Juninho’s free-kicks, but bloody effective, and I quite like it.”

Sports.title: Ajayi and Mendy give Hull dream start against misfiring Manchester United
Sports.content:
Ever since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement 13 years ago, Manchester United have been stuck in football’s equivalent of purgatory and a chastening experience in Hull suggests they could be there a while longer. Michael Carrick’s permanent appointment was supposed to hail a new era at Old Trafford but very little has changed based on this defeat.

United were sluggish from start to finish and rightly punished for failing to defend set pieces with any degree of competence. Centre-backs Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy earned Hull the prized scalp upon their return to the Premier League while United are left to ponder if the squad requires more invasive surgery before the transfer window closes.

This was Hull’s first win against United in the Premier League while they had not beaten their rivals in 52 years. There had been a nine-year wait for the Tigers to be back at this level and they proved themselves worthy, admittedly against a toothless United, who lost their opening fixture for the fourth time in the past seven seasons.

Even with relatively little time on the clock, it felt like a game that needed a flashpoint to ignite the season. Harry Maguire and Elliot Stroud clashed around the halfway line, with both feeling wronged by the other, but nothing was given. The perceived injustice provoked the home players and supporters, increasing the level of intensity from Hull, while United retreated into their shell.

Warnings came as Senne Lammens saved from Oli McBurnie and tipped over a vicious Ryan Giles cross. Giles, however, delivered a corner that United failed to defend properly at either post. It was whipped to the front and flicked to the back where McBurnie had space to shoot. Lammens stopped it on the line, only for Ajayi to smash home only a second league goal for the club.

View image in fullscreen Semi Ajayi fires past Senne Lammens to put Hull ahead. Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images

McBurnie was causing problems with his relentless running and physicality as Ayden Heaven was welcomed to the perils of Hull. United, on the other hand, missed the presence of a striker, with Matheus Cunha nominated for the role of a false No 9, which allowed him to roam far and wide, spending as much time away from Hull’s three centre-backs as possible.

United looked like a side playing their first game of pre-season against an opponent midway through the campaign. An avoidable free-kick given away by Youri Tielemans resulted in another set-piece United failed to deal with. Regan Slater’s delivery was dangerous and the lack of desire for anyone in white to attack the ball allowed Mendy to head a debut goal from close range. If this was supposed to be the start of a new United era, the reality was a return to the passive days of Ruben Amorim and his band of miserable men.

The Hull fans celebrated the half-time whistle with joy, while half the away end was empty, as souls searched for a way to soothe the pain on the concourse. It gave Carrick time to plot the radical change that was required but he only removed the cautioned Patrick Dorgu, sending on the returning Marcus Rashford.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Nobel Mendy (left) sparks wild celebrations for Hull in their first league win against Manchester United since 1974. Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images

Carrick brought calm after replacing Amorim but playing with this much tranquility was naive. Tactics and natural ability need to be blended with fight and desire, traits not on display from United, who would have hoped for a promising start, especially with Ipswich at home next.

Rashford was introduced to provide the previously absent spark and make the team less narrow and more expansive. He brought something akin to intent on the left wing, running at defenders who had walked through the first half but nothing was created as Konstantinos Tzolakis enjoyed a comfortable debut. It was a sign of how the day had gone for United when debutants Andrey Santos and Tielemans, signed for a combined total of £85m, were withdrawn with 23 minutes remaining after struggling to get a foothold in the game.

Hull, who had the fourth worst defensive record in the Championship last season, did not need to attack in the second half and were happy to keep United at arm’s length. The hosts deserved everything they received, through a mixture of quality delivery, aggression and organisation, three things United lacked. Football, bloody Hull.

Sports.title: Jack Clarke’s last-minute strike secures Ipswich winning return against Sunderland
Sports.content:
It would be fascinating to know which algorithms or eagle-eyed staff in Ipswich’s recruitment department spotted the potential in Emersonn to score the goals to keep them in the Premier League.

Thirteen games, no goals and a serious knee injury at the Brazilian side Athletico Paranaense; two league goals in 17 games at Turkish side Goztepe; then six in 28 at French side Toulouse. A modest return and not one that screams he would be ready to break down doors in the English top flight.

Ipswich have spent more than £150m this summer, determined not to make the same mistakes as the last time they came up. Emersonn became a club record signing – for £24m plus add-ons – beaten a month later by the arrival of the attacking midfielder Julio Enciso for £26m.

In a season of flux and uncertainty, the sparks of a compelling partnership between the pair here offered faint hope Ipswich can stay up against the odds, just as their opponents did last season. They are certainly mirroring Sunderland’s recruitment plan.

“It’s important to assess the gap between the Championship and the Premier League – it’s massive,” the Sunderland manager, Régis Le Bris, said. “They made a good start, which is important, but the consistency throughout the season is a big challenge.”

Enciso and Emersonn combined for the opening goal and regularly tried to find one another. Luke O’Nien, for reasons unbeknown to anyone but himself, had the ball under no pressure on the halfway line but passed straight to Enciso. Anyone watching the previous 23 minutes could see he was the last player you wanted to give the ball to with yards of open grass behind you. Enciso duly skipped past O’Nien, drove into Sunderland’s half, shimmied past Dan Ballard before squaring for Emersonn to scruffily tuck the ball away.

Angulo swept in a marvellous free kick via the crossbar, six minutes before the break, and almost an entire second half of Ipswich pressure looked to be petering out in a draw. But Jack Clarke came on in the 71st minute – replacing man of the match Enciso, who left to a standing ovation – and in the 90th minute he delicately finished into the bottom-right corner.

View image in fullscreen Emersonn takes the plaudits after scoring Ipswich’s first goal against Sunderland. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

“We’ve thrown Emersonn in,” the Ipswich manager, Gary O’Neil, said. “There are still some bits he has to tidy up on. He gave Ballard a tough time, fought him physically.”

There is indubitable flair and talent in the 22-year-old – the first Brazilian to play for Ipswich. Later, with the ball on the left, he evaded Thomas Meunier and Enzo Le Fée by slipping the ball between them, then found Enciso with a low cross, but the attacking midfielder caught the ball wrong.

Enciso has returned to Ipswich as though intent on making up for lost time. He has had nibbles at the Premier League before – first at Brighton, where he could not quite move beyond useful player-to-bring-on, then on loan here the last time Ipswich were in the Premier League, where he impressed as they went down.

He spent a year at Strasbourg under O’Neil, before following the coach back for another crack. “He’s a No 10 who can produce unbelievable quality, but not many 10s in the world are willing to work the way he works,” O’Neil said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I worked hard with him in Strasbourg around his defensive game. He was excellent stopping [Granit] Xhaka dictating. When he beats two players and there’s a shot on goal there’s no thought for himself, he passes to Emersonn. You won’t find many that can do all the sides like him.”

There will be times in retirement when O’Nien will wake up, drenched in sweat, from feverish dreams replaying over and over what Enciso did to him on this afternoon. After a bruising spell, when Enciso darted in to steal the ball from O’Nien’s feet, the defender took a yellow card to avoid being humiliated again.

If it wasn’t O’Nien, it was others. Enciso chopped past Xhaka – the midfielder shaking his head in frustration – then cut inside Nilson Angulo and crossed to the back post, where Emersonn was unable to direct his header on target.

Enciso has the vibe of a diminutive forward capable of producing a world-class performance once every four or five games. If he could find some consistency he could become one of the best players in the league.

Ipswich are back and there is something different about them this time.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino angers Concacaf nations by hijacking Caribbean Football Union meeting
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has angered many of the Concacaf nations, whose support he is seeking in his re-election campaign, by hijacking a meeting of the Caribbean Football Union (CFU) to announce Fifa-funded development projects for the region with millions of dollars that had been delayed for months.

Multiple sources attending the CFU meeting in the Dominican Republic said many of the Concacaf members were infuriated by Infantino’s behaviour, particularly as he had been asked to stay away by their president, Victor Montagliani.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Concacaf position echoes previous complaints about Fifa’s operations from the Jordan FA, whose president, Prince Ali bin al-Hussein, accused Infantino of bribery this month when he claimed they have not received prize money from last year’s Arab Cup due to the country’s failure to endorse the president.

As reported by the Guardian, Infantino appears to have seen the CFU meeting as an opportunity to lobby for election votes among Caribbean countries in the hope of causing a split among Concacaf, who have aligned with Uefa and the Asian Football Confederation in demanding his resignation after the World Cup sell-off debacle.

In a letter addressed to Infantino on Friday, Montagliani had asked the Fifa president “in the name of football to reconsider your attendance”, pointing out his presence would take the spotlight away from a regional under-14 tournament being held alongside the meeting.

Despite that entreaty, Infantino is understand to have turned up the resort of Punta Cana with a large Fifa entourage including the secretary general, Mattias Grafström, and Elkhan Mammadov, a staunch ally who is responsible for maintaining good relations with the 211 members in his role as director of member associations.

Before making funding pledges in the CFU meeting Infantino’s team are understood to have approached individual member associations lobbying for support. Mammadov has played a central role in attempts to keep them onside since the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal broke and his insistent approach has caused disquiet in some quarters.

One source said the official Fifa party had attempted to portray their governance crisis as a private dispute between Infantino and Montagliani. The Canadian businessman has not commented since news of the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise emerged, but has been widely touted in Europe as a possible contender to replace Infantino.

The pair met briefly and shook hands before the CFU meeting in an exchange captured by Infantino’s personal camera crew and later posted on his Instagram channel.

While Mexico, Grenada and St Kitts and Nevis have all broken with Concacaf and declared their support for Infantino, the majority of their 41 members are understood to back the alliance with Uefa advocates by Montagliani.

The Uefa/Concacaf pact extends beyond attempts to unseat Infantino, with the two confederations in talks about setting up a joint Nations League in 2028 that could develop further into a new global competition.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Nuno feels the heat after West Ham beaten by Charlton
Sports.content:
Charlton maintained their perfect start to the Championship season with a 2-1 victory at West Ham in a pulsating London derby to pile more pressure on the Hammers manager, Nuno Espírito Santo.

Lloyd Jones and Tyreece Campbell put Charlton 2-0 ahead before Joel Piroe, signed on loan from Leeds, marked his first appearance for the home side with a goal that set up a frantic finish. Taty Castellanos then missed a stoppage-time penalty for West Ham that would have salvaged a point.

Fer López bagged a double as Wolves secured their first victory of the season with a convincing 3-1 success over Preston at Deepdale. The Spaniard put Wanderers ahead with an eighth-minute rocket and substitute Adam Armstrong tucked home a 71st-minute second, just four minutes after stepping on to the pitch.

View image in fullscreen Fer López scores Wolves’s third of the match to kill off Preston. Photograph: Gary Oakley/PA

López put a cherry on top of the cake with a poacher’s finish in the 82nd minute as César Peixoto’s men flexed their muscles, but substitute Jordan Thompson bagged a 25-yard consolation in the first minute of stoppage time to give the home faithful something to cheer.

It was a much-needed victory for the relegated Premier League side but Preston are now without a win in their opening two Championship matches.

Blackburn stunned Middlesbrough with two goals in the space of six second-half minutes to earn a 2-1 victory at Ewood Park which continues their impressive start to the season. After conceding late against Wolves, the early signs pointed to more misery for Rovers as Kim Hellberg’s side smothered them early and were rewarded through Jeremy Sarmiento’s composed 12th-minute finish.

Rovers created enough in that first half to give their fans encouragement and pounced after the break through Andri Gudjohnsen’s 49th-minute header – his second goal in as many games – and Todd Cantwell’s diving header six minutes later to complete the turnaround.

Quick Guide League One roundup: Skipp off as Leicester woe continues Show Leicester’s poor start to the League One season continued with a 2-1 defeat by Burton at the King Power Stadium, where Oliver Skipp was sent off (pictured). Russell Martin’s side – held 1-1 at Notts County in their opening league game following relegation – were behind to an early goal from Matthew Dennis, with Kgaogelo Chauke adding another for the Brewers in the 25th minute. Skipp was then shown a straight red card for a late challenge by the Foxes’ midfielder on Curtis Tilt, before Wes Burns reduced the deficit ahead of the break. Despite Leicester dominating possession in the second half, they could not find an equaliser. Jack Wilshere was happy his Luton players were disappointed to only claim a point from their 2-2 draw with Notts County at Kenilworth Road. The hosts had led through Nahki Wells’ 42nd-minute penalty but then found themselves 2-1 down with just over an hour gone, Cal Roberts netting before the break and Ollie Cooper also on target. Callum Marshall came off the bench to earn a point and Wilshere said: “I’m happy they’re disappointed we didn’t take all three points, we want that. However, my message to them was we’re not going to win every single game. We want to and we prepare every game like we want to win, however this league is demanding." Oxford beat Stevenage 2-1 at the Sporta Arena to secure a first league win under Aaron Ramsey. Huddersfield also continued their unbeaten start with a 1-1 draw at MK Dons, which puts them second. Victor Adeboyejo’s late goal gave Bromley a 1-1 draw with Cambridge, in what was the Ravens’ first home match in the third tier. Wigan sit bottom without a point after a 2-0 home defeat by Leyton Orient. Doncaster and Barnsley registered their first points of the season but were still searching for wins after a goalless stalemate. AFC Wimbledon and Reading ground out a 0-0 stalemate at Plough Lane in a game of few chances. Wycombe drew 1-1 at home to Plymouth, while Blackpool won 2-1 at Stockport. Peterborough won 2-1 at home to Mansfield. PA Media Photograph: Plumb Images/Leicester City FC Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Divin Mubama scored a dramatic late goal on his home debut to help Southampton to a 3-1 victory over his former club Stoke. Almost a year ago, the Manchester City loan striker was sent off for Stoke at St Mary’s for diving.

Here, he was the hero as Saints dug deep to preserve an unbeaten home run which stretches back to January. Ryan Manning also scored a stoppage-time penalty after Svante Ingelsson was sent off for bringing down Samuel Edozie.

Cyle Larin bagged his third goal in as many games to give Tonda Eckert’s side an early lead but Stoke hit back through Ethan Galbraith and looked good value for a point until late on.

Wrexham were kept waiting for their first Championship win of the season as they drew 1-1 with Watford in front of Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac.

Both goals at the Racecourse Ground came in the opening quarter with Luca Kjerrumgaard’s header cancelled out by Danny Imray’s first Wrexham goal. It meant another draw for Wrexham after the Red Dragons were denied by a last-gasp Cardiff equaliser on Monday.

View image in fullscreen Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac watch Wrexham draw 1-1 with Watford. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock

Cardiff remain unbeaten two games into their return to the second tier after goals by Cian Ashford and Yousef Salech earned a 2-2 draw at Derby.

The Bluebirds were good value for their point, having twice taken the lead in front of a raucous Pride Park crowd of 28,926. But the Rams, unconvincing for large periods, capitalised on defensive mishaps to earn their first point of the new campaign through Carlton Morris and Bobby Clark.

Taïryk Arconte scored his first two goals for Millwall as they breezed past 10-man Norwich 3-0 to make it two wins from two this season. Having been tipped to challenge for the playoffs, Norwich have lost both of their opening games and had defender José Córdoba sent off in the second half at The Den.

Millwall were rewarded for their lively start in the 18th minute when Mark Sykes’ ball found Josh Coburn, whose shot was pushed out by Vladan Kovacevic for Arconte to tap in the rebound on his home debut. They deservedly went 2-0 ahead after 58 minutes when Zak Sturge’s ball into the box was headed back by Jake Cooper for Arconte to steer a volley into the bottom corner.

Córdoba was sent off for a second yellow card after bundling over Arconte as he charged towards the area.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Victory was sealed with six minutes remaining when a slick counterattack ended with Luke Cundle sliding in Millwall’s third.

View image in fullscreen Tairyk Arconte celebrates scoring Millwall’s second goal of the game against Norwich City. Photograph: George Tewkesbury/Shutterstock

Alex Neil, the Millwall manager, said: “I thought it was a complete performance from us, probably the most complete performance we’ve had in the nearly 20 months I’ve been here.”

Portsmouth claimed their first win of the season with a comprehensive 3-1 success at Lincoln. Portsmouth found themselves under the cosh early on but a seventh-minute goal from Ryan Kavuma-McQueen put them in the driving seat.

Adrian Segecic doubled the lead nine minutes later before Reeco Hackett-Fairchild pulled one back from the spot just past the half-hour mark. Substitute Ebrima Adams made the game safe with a superb strike after 69 minutes to leave Lincoln still searching for their first win back in the second tier for more than 60 years.

Demarai Gray rescued a point for Birmingham with a late penalty in a 2-2 draw at home to Bristol City. Scott Twine’s 33rd-minute effort gave the visitors the advantage before they conceded a 42nd-minute equaliser to Carlos Vicente. Dom Ballard converted Rio Cardines’ cross with a superb flick with his back to goal after 85 minutes to restore Bristol City’s lead but they could not hold on.

Quick Guide League Two roundup: Barnet and Crewe share 100% starts Show Barnet maintained their 100% with a 3-1 win at Shrewsbury, who are bottom after two defeats. Crewe also have six points after Josh March’s second-half goal secured a 1-0 victory over Northampton. Danny Cowley admitted Oldham’s red card changed the game after his Colchester side secured a last-gasp 2-1 win. Lewis Temple’s own goal in stoppage time handed United victory but Gus Scott-Morriss’s dismissal in the first half ultimately proved costly for Latics. Cowley said: “It’s always the best way to win [in stoppage time]. I’m not sure it’s good for the blood pressure but it was a great performance. I genuinely thought at XI v XI that we were the better team. Oldham are a really good team, but I really liked the way that we played. The sending-off naturally changed the game, so we made tactical tweaks. We were super young at the end, but we had enough energy and enthusiasm.” On the sending-off, Cowley added: “I’ll have to have another look. It looked high, and I did think that the ball was high as well.” Early goals earned Exeter a 2-0 win against Accrington Stanley. After a Devon derby defeat by Plymouth in the Carabao Cup and losing 1-0 at Grimsby last week, there was a bit of anxiety around St James Park, but captain Fitzwater settled any nerves inside two minutes with a terrific bicycle kick finish. Ten minutes later, it was 2-0 as a Gwion Edwards shot took a wicked deflection of Accrington skipper Seamus Conneely before ending up in the net. Rochdale’s first home game since promotion back to the EFL ended in a 2-1 defeat by Crawley, which was a second straight loss. York, though, are still unbeaten after coming from behind to draw 1-1 at Rotherham. Port Vale continued their winless start to the season with an entertaining 1-1 home draw with Tranmere. The centre-back Bobby Faulkner was forced to fill in as an emergency goalkeeper for Tranmere after Harrison Male was injured, before Tom Ince’s strike cancelled out George Byers’ first-half penalty to extend Rovers’ unbeaten start under Darrell Clarke. Bobby Kamwa scored against his former club as Bristol Rovers beat Newport 5-3 at the Memorial Stadium – where they had fallen behind after just 15 seconds. Swindon saw off their West Country rivals Cheltenham 2-1 at the County Ground, while Salford lost 1-0 at home to Chesterfield and are also still pointless. Fleetwood were held 0-0 at home by Gillingham, with Walsall v Grimsby also finishing goalless. PA Media Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

QPR’s Richard Kone missed several chances in a goalless draw with Bolton at Loftus Road. Kone, left out for last weekend’s win at Portsmouth, was restored to the Rangers side but missed four clear-cut opportunities during a first half largely dominated by the hosts.

Callum O’Hare came closest to netting a winner but Sheffield United had to be content with a goalless draw at Swansea City.

West Brom have said they are “devastated” after the death of former midfielder Quevin Castro, aged 25.

Castro, who made two senior appearances for the Baggies during a two-year spell at the Hawthorns, collapsed during a friendly between his current club, third-tier Portuguese side Real Sport Clube, and Estrela da Amadora on Saturday and later died in hospital.

West Brom said: “West Brom are devastated to learn of the untimely passing of Quevin Castro, aged just 25. Albion will pay tribute to Quevin on Sunday, with a period of applause in the 25th minute of the fixture against Burnley. James Morrison’s men will also wear black armbands.”

Sports.title: Andy Burnham says he wants to bring men’s World Cup back to UK in 2042
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham has said he wants to bring the men’s World Cup to the UK in 2042, returning the tournament to Britain for the first time in almost eight decades.

During informal discussions at No 10 North in Manchester on Friday, the prime minister told regional mayors he was keen for the tournament to be played in the British Isles.

The World Cup took place in England in 1966, when the home side beat West Germany 4-2 in the final after extra time – the only time the country has either hosted or won the contest.

Burnham, a keen football fan who has a season ticket at Everton, said earlier this month that it was “insane” only one World Cup had been held anywhere in the UK.

It is understood an application to stage the competition could also involve other home nations, none of which have hosted any World Cup games.

In recent years, joint bids between countries for major football tournaments have become more common. Alongside the Republic of Ireland, England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will host the men’s European championships in 2028.

Work has not yet begun on any official bid for the 2042 event but it is understood Downing Street would support the FA should it choose to pursue it.

Sources say Burnham has “broad aspirations” and “a general ambition” to bring more major footballing events to the UK.

England made a doomed bid to host the 2018 World Cup, which was awarded to Russia amid allegations of corruption.

In 2014, while serving in the shadow cabinet, Burnham said he was uncomfortable that the tournament was still allowed to take place in Russia after its annexation of Crimea.

Under Fifa regulations, no European country would be eligible to stage the World Cup until 2042.

In 2000, Fifa introduced rules that meant the tournament would be rotated around its six continental confederations. It led to South Africa hosting its first World Cup in 2010, but the strict system was scrapped in October 2007.

Countries are not allowed to bid to stage a World Cup if either of the previous two tournaments have taken place on the same continent.

The 2030 World Cup will be hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with some early matches taking place in South America to mark the tournament’s centenary. The first World Cup was played in Uruguay in 1930.

Fifa has also confirmed that the 2034 tournament will take place in Saudi Arabia. The location of the 2038 World Cup has not yet been announced, but under the rules, it is likely to be played in North America or Oceania, which includes Australia and New Zealand.

Burnham is also understood to have spoken about the possibility of hosting the Olympic and Paralympic Games in the north of England in the 2040s at Friday’s meeting.

UK Sport was commissioned to assess whether a bid would be viable earlier this year under the previous prime minister, Keir Starmer.

It is understood that the government is considering the possibility of a “multi-city bid” in an attempt to spread any economic benefit between several northern cities.

A government spokesperson said: “The UK is committed to delivering world-class major sporting events with pride, with the Tour de France and Tour de France Femmes Grands Départs 2027 and Uefa Euro 2028 secured, and active bids for the 2029 World Athletics Championships and 2035 Women’s World Cup.



“As the prime minister has made clear, we will continue to pursue sporting events that bring communities together, drive regional growth and create jobs across the country.”
