Sports.title: Quevin Castro dead at 25: Former West Brom footballer dies after collapsing during a friendly in Portugal as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A former West Bromwich footballer has died aged just 25.

Quevin Castro, who grew up in Thetford in Norfolk where he attended the local secondary school, collapsed during a friendly match with third-tier Portuguese side Real Sport Clube.

Desperate attempts were made to revive him with a defibrillator by a doctor with the top-flight team he was playing against, Estrela da Amadora, which is based in Amadora just north-west of Lisbon.

He was rushed to hospital but pronounced dead shortly after arrival.

The tragedy happened earlier today.

West Brom fan page westbrom.fc said this afternoon alongside a photo of Portuguese-born Quevin: 'Former West Bromwich Albion player Quevin Castro has passed away aged 25.

Former West Brom footballer Quevin Castro has died at the age of 25 after collapsing in a friendly

'Our thoughts and prayers go out to his friends and family during this extremely difficult time. RIP, Quevin.'

A supporter reacted by saying: 'RIP Quevin. What a shock. Condolences to the family.'

Another said: 'Wow, aged 25. Gone playing the sport he loved. Horrible news. May he rest in peace.'

Another added: 'That's devastating. Far too young. RIP.'

The central midfielder, whose full name was Quevin Moises Cachicote da Rocha de Castro, had turned 25 on August 16.

He moved back to his homeland from Isthmian League Premier Division club Eastbourne Borough.

He played non-league football for Mildenhall Town, Thetford Town, Norwich CBS, Leiston and Bury Town during his early career.

Castro had trial spells at Ipswich Town in 2019 and later in 2020, and also spent time on trial at Sutton United, Arsenal, Chelsea and West Bromwich Albion.

In the summer of 2021, Castro signed for West Brom on a two-year contract following his trial at the club.

Real Sport Clube paid tribute to Castro on social media following his tragic death

He made his debut for the club on August 25, 2021, starting in a 6-0 EFL Cup second round defeat to Arsenal.

He went on to make his only league appearance for West Brom on February 28, 2022, as a substitute in a 2-0 Championship defeat to Swansea City

On July 14, 2022, Castro joined League One side Burton Albion on a season-long loan.

Castro had his loan terminated by mutual consent on September 1 of that year and later joined National League club Notts County on loan.

He went on to play for a number of clubs including King's Lynn and Chippenham Town before signing for Eastbourne Borough in March this year.

Today's match was cancelled following the footballer's collapse.

The footballer collapsed in the tenth minute of the match.

Estrela da Amadora said in a statement on its website, referencing Quevin's current club by the name Real Massama as it is commonly known although its formal name is Real Sport Clube: 'Estrela da Amadora hereby expresses its profound sorrow at the passing of Quévin Castro, player of Real Massamá.

'In this moment of profound sadness, Estrela da Amadora extends its deepest condolences to the family and friends of Quévin Castro, as well as to the entire Real Massama organization.

'Our thoughts are with all those who were close to him.

'Rest in peace, Quevin.'

Real Sport Clube said alongside a black ribbon photo and Quevin's name underneath: 'It is with profound sadness and great sorrow that Real Sport Clube announces the passing of Quevin Castro, a player and beloved member of our sporting family.

'Quevin Castro was far more than a player, he was a member of our family, leaving a mark on all those who had the privilege of knowing him, both on and off the pitch.

'At this time of grief, Real Sport Clube extends its most sincere condolences to the family and all friends of Quevin Castro, expressing its full solidarity and unconditional support.

'May the memory of Quevin Castro live on in our hearts.

'Rest in peace.'

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba to undergo Man United medical TODAY as Crystal Palace slap down Jean-Philippe Mateta enquiry and Joao Pedro signs eight-year Chelsea extension: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Carlos Baleba to undergo Man United medical TODAY as Crystal Palace slap down Jean-Philippe Mateta enquiry and Joao Pedro signs eight-year Chelsea extension: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Napoli sign Chelsea star on loan

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has joined Napoli on a loan deal, with an option to buy.

The loan fee is worth £2.5million and could rise to £3.4m with add-ons. The option price is around £23m.

Chelsea could receive more than £26m from the deal if Badiashile moves permanently. They valued him at £30m in this window.

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has joined Napoli on a loan deal, with an option to buy

Napoli are also one of the clubs keen on Chelsea's Marc Guiu. He is weighing up options from Spain and Germany too.

Hull City are exploring a loan for Chelsea midfielder Dario Essugo who is also wanted at Strasbourg.

Palace knock back Mateta enquiry

Aston Villa have had an enquiry for Jean-Philippe Mateta knocked back by Crystal Palace.

Unai Emery's team are hunting a centre-forward with Al-Hilal pushing hard to sign Ollie Watkins.

Daily Mail Sport understands that Villa's interest in Mateta was firmly rejected by Palace before an offer could be made.

Villa are also strongly interested in signing Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea. Informal discussions are thought to have taken place between intermediaries, with a bid expected in the coming days.

Watkins has also been offered a new deal at Villa. It is unlikely the 30-year-old would be allowed to leave before a replacement has been secured.

Reports Tom Collomosse

Villa have had an enquiry for French forward Jean-Philippe Mateta knocked back by Palace

Wrexham eye up move for Millwall's Azeez

Wrexham are exploring a move for Millwall forward Femi Azeez.

The exciting 25-year-old also has interest from Brighton and Hull City.

The Robins are hoping the Nigeria international will be attracted by their ambitious project despite Millwall being rival promotion contenders.

Wrexham are also looking at Ipswich Town attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti.

The 25-year-old Albania international only joined in January from Bristol City for £3.5m and scored his first goal for the club against Wrexham.

The move would mean him giving up the opportunity of Premier League football now though Wrexham hope to be there in a year's time.

Meanwhile, Wrexham's move for free agent defender Axel Tuanzebe looks to be off.

The exciting 25-year-old also has interest from Brighton and Hull City

Brighton enquire about Hull target Hernandez

Brighton have asked about Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez.

The 23-year-old has been in the UK to talk to Hull City who have been trying to sign him but Brighton are exploring a move also.

Hull owner Acun Ilicali said: 'We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself.

'This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive. He is young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come. We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure.'

Brighton remain in talks with Liverpool over the sale of winger Yankuba Minteh.

Though the 22-year-old wants the move, the clubs are some distance apart on valuation with Brighton wanting over £70m to reflect market prices.

The 23-year-old has been in the UK to talk to Hull City who have been trying to sign him but Brighton are exploring a move also

Blues keep tabs on Conceicao amid interest in Neto

Juventus winger Francisco Conceicao is back on Chelsesa's radar in case they sell Pedro Neto.

Conceicao was bought from Porto for £36million and Juventus would want some profit on their outlay for the 23-year-old Portugal international.

Neto has interest from Al Hilal, Tottenham and Manchester City but Chelsea are asking £100m.

They also have an offer from Roma for Jamie Gittens but so far that's too low, as a loan with option.

Conceicao is quick, technically good and robust for his diminutive stature.

Juventus would look to utilise any money from Conceicao for targets such as Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee.

Juventus winger Conceicao is back on Chelsesa's radar in case they sell Pedro Neto, with Al Hilal, Tottenham and Manchester City all interested in Neto

Magpies reignite interest in Spurs' Gray

Newcastle United have rekindled interest in Tottenham's versatile midfielder Archie Gray.

The 20-year-old is still very much part of coach Roberto de Zerbi's plans as he can cover various positions though midfield is his preference. He has also captained the team during pre-season.

Newcastle are speaking to Manchester City about Nico Gonzalez but Gray is also someone they admire.

After losing so much quality they are exploring a number of options to strengthen their squad and add Premier League experience.

Since joining Spurs from Leeds for £40million, Gray has made 81 appearances, often filling in at centre-back and right-back as well as midfield.

Tottenham will need to consider sales to offset their substantial summer spending, though they would prefer to sell others. Gray is valued over £60m.

Since joining Spurs from Leeds for £40million, Gray has made 81 appearances, often filling in at centre-back and right-back as well as midfield and has captained the side during pre-season

Joao Pedro signs eight-year Blues contract

Joao Pedro has signed his new Chelsea contract until 2034.

Chelsea have been determined to keep the Brazil international after he emerged as a target for Barcelona early in the summer.

The Brazil international joined the Blues from Brighton in July 2025 and made an immediate impact, scoring in the Club World Cup semi-final and final as Chelsea were crowned world champions.

His form continued into his first full season at Stamford Bridge, with the forward scoring 20 goals in all competitions.

While the club are willing to listen to offers for Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson, the 24-year-old was named Chelsea's new No 9 last week.

Joao Pedro said: 'I am very happy to sign a new contract with Chelsea. I always dreamed of playing for a big club, and it means a lot to me to give my long-term commitment to this club.

'Everyone is very excited for this season. We know we can achieve a lot of things. We have a great team, we have a coach who wants to win and has won already.'

Joao Pedro, who has signed a fresh eight-year deal at Chelsea, said: 'I always dreamed of playing for a big club, it means a lot to me to give my long-term commitment to this club'

Baleba prepares for Man United medical

Carlos Baleba is due to undergo his medical today ahead of completing his £70million move from Brighton to Manchester United.

The 22-year-old is recovering from an ankle ligament injury but is expected to be fit towards the end of next month.

The deal was agreed early on Friday evening at £65m plus add-ons and a sell-on clause.

Newcastle target given the green light for move

Newcastle target Nico Gonzalez has been told by Enzo Maresca and Hugo Viana that he can leave Manchester City.

Gonzalez was ready to fight for his place but with City looking to sign two more midfielders they are realistic about his prospects of playing regularly.

Newcastle believe he is open to the move and is emerging as their priority on a shortlist of three targets.

Nico Gonzalez has been told that he can move from Man City amid interest from Newcastle

Newcastle have also registered interest in Christopher Nkunku of AC Milan, though RB Leipzig are more active on the situation as it stands.

Man City's talks for Ayyoub Bouaddi are continuing, though Lille have been pushing for optimum price on the 18-year-old.

Man City forward Omar Marmoush is still expected to complete his move to Tottenham.

Villa circle free agent Germany star

Aston Villa have opened talks with free agent Germany international Leon Goretzka.

The former Bayern Munich midfielder is viewed as a high quality and experienced alternative to Joao Palhinha who is joining Benfica.

Goretzka, 31, has had interest from Atletico Madrid and Tottenham in recent months but Villa hope to progress in the coming days.

They have also made a check call on Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee who has the offer of a potential loan with obligation from Juventus.

Leon Goretza has begun talks with Aston Villa with the club seeking progress in coming days

Liverpool fledgling books Levente loan deal

Liverpool defensive prospect Ifeanyi Ndukwe is joining Levante on loan.

The 18-year-old does not qualify for a work permit in England as yet, so is having to be loaned out to play competitive football.

The Austrian youth international has excelled during Liverpool's pre-season and the club have high hopes for his future.

First team football in a top league such as LaLiga is viewed as an integral next step.

He has travelled to Valencia to complete terms. Ndukwe also had interest from clubs in Portugal, France and Germany.

Sports.title: Everton claim 2-0 win over Crystal Palace, Premier League new boys Ipswich stun Sunderland and Leeds leave it late against Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Everton claim 2-0 win over Crystal Palace, Premier League new boys Ipswich stun Sunderland and Leeds leave it late against Nottingham Forest

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Andy Burnham grew up watching an Everton legend called Kevin Sheedy conjure up goals with a left foot that appeared to be sprinkled with magic dust. So the Prime Minister would have appreciated more than most the strike by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall that put his favourite team on the path to victory.

The Merseysiders had been second best in a first half packed with chances when Dewsbury-Hall took aim just inside the angle of Crystal Palace's penalty area. The crispness of the connection with his left boot was pure Sheedy.

The ball exploded past Palace keeper Dean Henderson in a blur - and David Moyes' team didn't look back.

Burnham was ensconced next to his wife Frankie and boyhood hero Peter Reid in the best seats in the house. He resisted the temptation to wear a replica shirt, but his royal blue suit gave the game away.

He was on his feet again when a close-range header by Thierno Barry early in the second half persuaded Palace that this wasn't going to be their day.

'I spoke to the Prime Minister on the phone before the game when Andy Gray came into my office,' said Everton manager David Moyes. 'He was with his assistant, Peter Reid!

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall was on target as Everton claimed all three points against Crystal Palace

'I think it's the first time in five years since we've won on the opening day. Kiernan's goal was very good - but we also needed our goalkeeper. After we scored the second goal we probably should have gone on to score one or two more.'

New Palace manager Pierre Sage has inherited a seasoned squad that had won the Europa Conference League just 89 days earlier. For the first 41 minutes, the game appeared to be theirs for the taking, with Adam Wharton running the show.

But missed chances - and the intervention of inspired Everton keeper Jordan Pickford - took their toll.

Jean-Philippe Mateta fired an early opening over and Daniel Munoz was denied by Pickford before the Everton keeper excelled himself to tip Eddie Nketiah's close-range effort against the post after Wharton had illustrated why Manchester City have told the London club to name their price with a delicious lofted pass.

When Mateta then beat Pickford with a side-footed shot from Nketiah's cross, only to see the ball rebound back off the same post, it seemed inevitable there would be a reckoning.

'Sometimes in football, you don't score when you deserve to score - and you pay the bill,' lamented Sage. 'You have to convert your chances.'

Everton had also created chances during an opening half that was so end-to-end it would have driven both Sage and Everton manager David Moyes to distraction, with Iliman Ndiaye first thumping a shot straight at Henderson when given a clear sight of goal from 12 yards and later dragging another decent opportunity wide.

Moyes had spent the build-up to the game suggesting chief executive Angus Kinnear had been mistaken to suggest that Everton's failure to qualify for Europe last season represented failure.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham celebrates alongside Everton legend Peter Reid in the stands

His team were transformed by Dewsbury-Hall's opening goal, which came about thanks to the tenacity of homegrown teenager Harrison Armstrong.

When Merlin Rohl's quick free kick on the right flank in the 53rd minute caught Palace napping, the outstanding Ndiaye punished them with a cross that took Henderson out of the equation and Barry couldn't miss from inside the six-yard box.

Ndiaye forced Henderson into another save before Tyrique George blazed a chance over as the visitors could barely raise a riposte.

Palace missed the injured Ismaila Sarr, with Sage confirming that the Senegalese forward's absence wasn't down to interest from Galatasaray. 'Sarr will be training on Monday,' said Sage. 'He has a contract and he has won many trophies with us.'

BY SIMON MULLOCK

Ipswich 2-1 Sunderland

Jack Clarke scored a dramatic late winner to get newly-promoted Ipswich off to the perfect start on their Premier League return against Sunderland.

Former Black Cats winger Clarke came off the bench to raise the roof off Portman Road with a 90th-minute strike to hand Gary O'Neil the dream start to life as Tractor Boys boss.

Ipswich only won one home game all season during their last Premier League campaign two years ago but have already matched that this term with a memorable victory on the opening weekend.

Perhaps inspired by their opening day opponents, who finished seventh in the top flight last year, O'Neil handed out six full debuts after spending £150 million so far this summer in an attempt to bridge the gap.

'I thought we played pretty well,' the Ipswich boss said. 'I thought we deserved to win on the balance of it. New signings and players that have been here a while, all pulling together.

'The players know that they can compete at the level. We were competitive today in all phases. I'm 100 per cent confident that they will give everything in every game and we will find a way to be competitive.

'The most confident that I've been in a group that I know what I'm going to see, and I know that they're going to give everything.'

Powerful striker Brian Brobbey was the first to threaten, but Ipswich left-back Leif Davis was on hand to snuff out the danger with an important late block after Trai Hume's forward pass.

Jack Clarke scored a dramatic late winner to get newly-promoted Ipswich off to the perfect start

Club record signing Emersonn had the hosts' first sight of goal soon after, using his status as a target man to good effect as his header was almost fumbled by Robin Roefs.

Ipswich's big moment came after 24 minutes when Emersonn lifted the roof off Portman Road, scoring the game's opening goal after fine work from Julio Enciso on his own second Town debut.

Enciso, who only joined from Strasbourg on Monday, pounced on a loose pass and burst past both Luke O'Nien and Dan Ballard after winning possession inside his own half.

From there, the Paraguay international unselfishly laid off for the onrushing Emersonn to finish into the empty net on his maiden Ipswich appearance.

Dutch goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen was forced into a strong stop to deny compatriot Brobbey's powerful header on goal as the visitors sought an immediate response.

They got it shortly before half-time when a wonderful free-kick from Nilson Angulo found the net moments after Enciso had fired over at the other end.

From 25 yards out, Angulo curled into the top corner via the underside of the crossbar. Even the long arms of 6ft 9in keeper Scherpen, the Premier League's tallest ever player, could not keep it out.

'Welcome back to the Premier League, someone smashes one into the top corner from 25 yards and it's back to square one,' O'Neil said afterwards.

Enciso worked some magic shortly after half-time and almost scored a stunner, with his inventive hook round the corner just evading the far post with Roefs stranded.

Almost immediately at the other end, Brobbey came close to giving Sunderland the lead when pouncing on an Ipswich error, but Marcelino Nunez was well-placed to block.

The energetic Enciso was showing his class and created another chance soon after, but Daizen Maeda was unable to meet Emersonn's headed cutback around the penalty spot.

As Ipswich began to tire, O'Neil threw on last season's top scorer Clarke in an attempt to swing momentum back in their favour, a decision that paid its dividends.

Sasa Lukic, another of Town's experienced summer arrivals, pounced on Omar Alderete's loose pass and allowed Clarke to do the rest on the edge of the box.

The Tractor Boys' super sub curled into the far corner beyond Roefs to lift the noise levels and hand Ipswich the best possible start to their latest top flight campaign.

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris rued: 'At the minute, we are not clinical enough to create chances and score goals. They enjoyed using those opportunities.

'We were in control when we made those mistakes. We'll learn from that experience. It was the problem of the afternoon and we didn't solve it.

'When you make mistakes, you get punished. It's not new. We want to get better and we'll bounce back.'

BY KALLUM BRISSET

Nottingham Forest 0-1 Leeds

So much for Nottingham Forest's bright new dawn under Oliver Glasner. If the Austrian is to have the same transformative effect as he did at Crystal Palace, he will need to find much more than this. He will need some more players for a start.

Forest didn't deserve to lose this dreadful opening-day affair at the City Ground, but they certainly didn't do anywhere near enough to win it. Neither, in all honesty, did Leeds. The fairest of all outcomes would have been for both teams to shake hands, go home with a point apiece, and agree to forget the previous turgid two hours ever happened.

Maybe it was the early-season rust. Glasner described it as a 'typical first Premier League game'. Maybe it was two rusty teams playing the same three-at-the-back system finding themselves at an impasse.

This is only the first match, of course, but either way these two clubs who spent most of last season fighting against relegation showed little to suggest they won't have to scrap again. We can only hope their League Cup clash here again on Tuesday is more exciting.

Another set-piece season?

It was fitting, in the end, that this contest should be decided at the death by a set-piece as Anton Stach curled a free-kick from the edge of the penalty area past a flapping, bewildered Matz Sels. All of the best chances came from dead balls, whether it be corners or long throws, with so little of anything resembling quality emerging from open play.

Anton Stach curled a free-kick from the edge of the penalty area to earn Leeds three points at Nottingham Forest

Leeds, and Stach, are becoming masters of them. Glasner told his players that whoever won the set piece battle would win the match. It was such a huge part of the Premier League last season, the early signs are that it could be again.

'We are talking so much about set-pieces being so important nowadays,' said Leeds boss Daniel Farke. 'Even in my day, set pieces were important. Remember magic free-kick taker Juninho, curling the ball. If you want to be successful, if you want to win the title one day, you have to be good at set pieces. Anton is maybe not as beautiful on the eye as Juninho's free kicks but effective!'

Forest struggle to fill Anderson void

No new signings started for Forest and it showed. There was always going to be an Elliot Anderson-shaped hole in Nottingham Forest's midfield following his £116million move to Manchester City, the question was how Glasner would fill it.

Instead of combative new signing Xaver Schlager, Glasner went for precision and artistry of James McAtee. The midfielder struggled in his first season at Forest after his £30m move from Manchester City but there's hope that under Glasner, he can thrive playing in the same quarter-back role as Adam Wharton did for him at Palace.

As tackles and fouls flew around, McAtee at least tried to bring some decorum. There was a neat little backheel flick to Morgan Gibbs-White that drew a rare oooh of excitement and it was his cross into the box that found the head of Nikola Milenkovic, whose effort struck the post.

Yet it was just moments. It was not enough for Forest to dominate the midfield. It was not enough to completely fill the void left behind by Anderson. Not yet, at least. He was replaced after the hour.

Gibbs-White kept dropping deep to link play and fizz diagonal balls into the channels instead of being in the heart of it all further up the field. Even he was over-hitting them.

Glasner became the seventh Forest manager in a row to lose his first Premier League match but insists this will be a long process. It took him a while to get the Eagles soaring.

'There is no button to press,' he said. 'It is getting confidence what we are doing. It is a process. Me and my staff can't come in, put our hands on their shoulders and all of a sudden we play like Real Madrid in the 70s.'

All smiles for Trafford

As the final whistle blew, Leeds' defenders took it in turn to embrace James Trafford. The Leeds keeper was grinning from ear to ear. He needed that. Like McAtee, Trafford is someone trying to settle into life away from Manchester City after his summer move and this was the ideal start.

He didn't have the busiest afternoon, he made one strong diving save to push away Igor Jesus's header, but was neat and tidy and commanded his area. 'He has this natural aura of confidence and calmness around him,' said Farke. 'It's just what we want. He played a decisive part.'

His fellow new signing Harry Wilson, a fine bit of business on a free transfer from Fulham, showed flashes of what he will offer in the forward line, getting on to the end of a cross to poke home what looked like the opener only for his goal to be ruled out for offside.

Is Delap the answer?

Glasner confirmed after the game that Forest are after 'two more players, two different positions and we are trying hard to get these deals done'. One of them is expected to be a striker.

Jesus had a good pre-season but showed here that he doesn't quite have the ruthless killer instinct of an elite striker. Chris Wood has shown that but he's 35 in December. He made a difference when he came on but dragged a good chance wide.

Forest are interested in Liam Delap, and tried to sign him last season. He fits the same profile as Wood but is younger. Chelsea want £50m but you expect Forest could get him for nearer £40m.

BY JAMES SHARPE

Sports.title: Lando Norris on the march again as he claims pole for Dutch Grand Prix - as George Russell boosted on return from summer break
Sports.content:
Lando Norris on the march again as he claims pole for Dutch Grand Prix - as George Russell boosted on return from summer break

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lando Norris wears No1 on his back and on his car, but it has not seemed that way as often as he would have liked during his title defence.

Yet it is from that position he will start the Dutch Grand Prix, just as he did in Budapest three weeks ago, when he won. All of which are signs that his McLaren team might be on a march after upgrades that are confounding a lack of early-season form.

This time, as spits and spots of rain hit the resort of Zandvoort, a 30-minute rail ride from Amsterdam, the world champion secured his excellent pole one-tenth of a second ahead of compatriot George Russell.

It was, however, a seriously encouraging day for Russell on Formula One’s resumption after the summer break and a number of bumps for him and his lofty expectations of title glory.

He, unlike Norris – who is 90 points off the top of the standings – is still contending towards the front of the world championship reckoning. And his hopes were first rejuvenated earlier in the afternoon when he won the sprint race from pole position in a procession he dominated clinically.

Points in the sprint are meagre, though. So, by finishing ahead of his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who came fourth, Russell only narrowed his deficit to him from 59 points to 56. Big deal, you might say. But it was a major psychological leap when he most needed it.

Lando Norris will start the Dutch Grand Prix on pole with signs McLaren are now on the march

George Russell earned a boost by qualifying ahead of his team-mate Kimi Antonelli

And that was before he qualified a place above Antonelli, the Italian wonderkid who is in serious danger of upsetting what was meant to be Russell’s season of fulfilment.

Clearly relieved post-qualifying, Russell said: ‘The truth is Kimi has been doing an amazing job. We have different driving styles. It is working well for him and these tyres.

‘I’m trying to implement something similar into my driving style. It is like changing your golf swing. You will probably take half a step back first before making improvements.

‘The break allowed me to put my learning to the back of my mind, not fixating on what I want to achieve with the car, but still knowing what I need to do and driving more freely.

‘In tennis, the racquet is basically the same. The lines are always the same distance apart. This isn’t the way it is in Formula One, so I am pleased with how I have managed to adjust to this year’s regulations.

‘I feel very confident going into the race.’

Antonelli registered Russell’s green shoots of revival, however tentative they might be for now. ‘It was a very good wake-up call today,’ admitted the 19-year-old. ‘You can never lower your guard.’

Norris, who had been downbeat after the sprint, in which he finished third, said: ‘A good turnaround from earlier today, where I felt we struggled. Credit to the team, they did a good job.

‘We had to try something because what we had before wasn’t going to be enough. We made some small changes. Enough to give me more confidence. And on a track like Zandvoort you need confidence. You want to attack a lot and I felt I could do that more, so it paid off.

Lewis Hamilton qualified fifth for Ferrari, a place behind Norris’s team-mate Oscar Piastri. He never quite seemed in the frame for pole.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes rips into his Man United team-mates for making 'the same mistakes' - as Alan Shearer claims Michael Carrick's men 'didn't look fit' in shock opening day defeat at Hull
Sports.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes called on his team-mates to 'be more aggressive' and stop making the 'same mistakes as we did last season' after they were battered and bruised in a 2-0 defeat to Hull City. United ran out their new £85million midfield pairing of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans and had all of their stars available, except for Amad, Mason Mount and Matthijs de Ligt. But many of United's mistakes were painfully familiar and captain Fernandes is tired of seeing them over and over again away from home. 'Same mistakes as we did last season every away game,' Fernandes bemoaned afterwards. 'We give too much of the ball to them. In the first 20 minutes the goalkeeper had more touches on the ball… too much time. 'We need to press a little bit more, be more aggressive, and set-plays - we need to work on it, to be more aggressive and try not to concede these types of goals. Bruno Fernandes has warned Man United must stop making the 'same mistakes as last season' after the Red Devils fell to a 2-0 defeat to newly promoted Hull City in their opening match Hull scored twice from set pieces in the first half to make a dream return to the Premier League BBC pundit Alan Shearer expressed concerns that Man United 'didn't look fit' during the defeat

Your browser does not support iframes.

'We knew before the game that [set-pieces] would be a big part of their game.' Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic explained afterwards that the switch to a back five was done after spotting gaps behind Manchester United's full-backs and it worked to great effect. That switch, which caught United out, only added to Fernandes' frustrations. 'They played a full pre-season with a back four,' Fernandes added. 'They went against us with a back five, also to have some height, also for these moments [at set-pieces] because they could get a chance from it and defend well from our set-pieces. The most frustrating thing is that we lost the game.' BBC pundit Alan Shearer expressed concerns over Manchester United's physical conditioning following the defeat, with the England and Newcastle legend suggesting the Red Devils 'did not look fit' in the season opener. 'I haven't seen Manchester United in pre-season,' Shearer said on on BBC Radio 5 Live. 'I saw them in this game and they didn't look fit, they didn't look ready to play 90 minutes of intense, high pressure, high energy football. 'There was only one team that looked fit there and it wasn't Manchester United.' United's passiveness played into Hull City's hands and the eventual outcome was a dream come true for captain Lewie Coyle. 'Before we went to bed last night we couldn't have dreamt it any better,' Coyle said. 'It'll be a shock to people, I'm not saying it's how I thought it would go, but this team's got something special in terms of character, resilience, and we know what we're doing. 'We know we're going to get chances on the break. You're against a fantastic side and we know that's the minimum it's going to take. 'So, so proud of the boys for what we achieved last year. We're not just here to make the numbers up - we're here to stay in this division. What an incredible start for the boys.'

Sports.title: Hull 2-0 Man United: Michael Carrick could not have seen this opening-day humiliation coming even in his worst nightmares - any title talk on this evidence is a joke, writes CHRIS WHEELER
Sports.content:
Well, Michael Carrick did say it was ridiculous to suggest Manchester United had been given an easy start to the season away at Hull.

Even in his worst nightmares, though, Carrick couldn't have foreseen this: an opening-day humiliation at the hands of a team that sneaked into the Premier League via the Championship play-offs in May, and have been prepped for their return to the top-flight with a summer spend of just £70million on 12 players – the same as it is costing United to sign Carlos Baleba from Brighton.

What a day this was for Hull City; their players and their fans, head coach Sergej Jakirovic and charismatic owner Acun Ilicali.

They will talk for a long time here of a first-ever Premier League win over United, and the two set-piece goals created by Regan Slater for Semi Ajayi and new record signing Nobel Mendy.

But what of United? All of a sudden, Carrick might have felt he was back at Turf Moor in August 2009 when a first away game of the season ended in an embarrassing defeat at Burnley and he missed a penalty. There were shades too of United's 4-0 defeat at Brentford four years ago.

This was every bit as bad. After a summer of guarded optimism over the signing of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, the new midfield failed to launch. Both players were replaced midway through the second half on their Premier League debuts with United two goals down, having been eclipsed by Matt Crooks and Slater, a mere £50,000 signing from Sheffield United in 2022.

Calling Manchester United title contenders sounds like a joke based on this performance

This was a serious setback for a side who were sloppy, ponderous, and vulnerable

Instead, it was the business that United haven't done that becomes the main talking point. The new striker that hasn't arrived. The missing defensive cover for Luke Shaw. Baleba, the third midfield signing, coming in too late to start the season.

Considering Carrick only lost two of his 17 games after taking over in January, this was a serious setback. He talked in the week about touting United as title contenders being 'a jump'. On this evidence, it's a joke.

To further put this result in perspective, eight of Hull's line-up from the Championship Play-off final win over Middlesbrough in May started their first Premier League game for nine years with many – notably Joe Cole – already tipping them for relegation.

The other three players came from the raft of new signings, including Mendy and Greece goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis who was as unflappable as his manager. Not that United gave him much to worry about.

'He played under huge stress and pressure at Olympiakos, so for him this was like a cup of tea,' smiled Jakirovic, sipping from an imaginary mug.

The Hull boss outfoxed Carrick by switching to a back-five, primarily he said to counter Shaw playing higher up the pitch and thwart United's attempt to flood the midfield. It worked.

He also found a way past a United defence that has been strong at defending set-pieces under Carrick, after detecting a flaw in the system.

'It's a secret,' Jakirovic grinned again. 'We tried something on Friday. My assistants saw this. We had some plans there to try to punish them, how they stand at a wide free kick.'

Semi Ajayi gave the hosts the lead after a kerfuffle in the box in the 17th minute

Nobel Mendy made matters worse for United when he added Hull's second after 38 minutes

The first goal actually came from a corner in the 17th minute after Bryan Mbeumo's indecision in midfield gifted possession to Hull and ended with Senne Lammens tipping over from Ryan Giles.

Slater crossed from the left and John Egan flicked on. Oli McBurnie got in a shot from a tight angle which Lammens saved on the line and turned against the post, but the ball ran loose for Ajayi who was left unmarked to score.

The second goal in the 38th minute came from a free kick whipped in by Slater that was inviting a close-range finish, and Mendy provided it as he stole in front of Shaw to power a header past Lammens.

The MKM Stadium was in rapture, United in disarray.

They were passive and ponderous on the ball and vulnerable without it, particularly when Hull fed their wing-backs in wide areas. There was little to suggest that the new midfield partnership of Tielemans and Santos is clicking into gear. Hull muscled United off the ball too often, epitomised by McBurnie's battle with Ayden Heaven.

Carrick had been forced into a change of plan by a minor injury to Amad Diallo in training, moving Mbeumo back to the right flank after playing him through the middle in pre-season.

That wasn't much of an excuse against a Hull side with eight injuries of their own, and Mbeumo had United's best two efforts well saved by Tzolakis.

Marcus Rashford came off the bench wearing the number nine shirt but was unable to change the match

Hull City owner Acun Ilicali felt vindicated after standing up for his side despite their doubters

Matheus Cunha played at centre-forward but lacked any punch. Patrick Dorgu was the worst of a bad bunch and was replaced at half-time by Marcus Rashford, playing his first competitive game for United since December 2024 in the No.9 shirt.

Benjamin Sesko, Kobbie Mainoo and Shea Lacey followed off the bench in the second half, but United never looked like avoiding a first league defeat to Hull since 1974.

Carrick was keen to stress that it's only one game, but the pressure will be on if his team lose to other Premier League newcomers, Ipswich Town, at Old Trafford next weekend.

The Hull fans who mocked pundit Cole for writing off their season took delight in the matchday announcer informing the United supporters with barely concealed relish that two trains back to Manchester had been cancelled.

'You're going home in a taxi,' they taunted their rivals, although most of them had disappeared by the final whistle.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick admits Man United 'have got to find answers' after being blown away by Hull - but insists 'it doesn't mean everything's wrong'
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is refusing to hit the panic button after his Manchester United side were bullied en route to a 2-0 defeat by Hull City.

The newly-promoted side, who ran out eight of those who started the play-off final at Wembley, have been widely tipped to be relegated straight back to the Championship.

But Sergej Jakirovic's side blew a passive Manchester United side away and goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy were enough to secure a deserved three points for the Premier League newcomers.

Asked afterwards if Hull City had found a flaw in his system, with both goals emanating from set-pieces, Carrick was firm in his response.

'We haven't lost many games in six, seven months,' the United boss said.

'So again, I get it, we've lost today and I understand there's questions to be asked, but it doesn't mean everything's wrong because we've lost a game.

Michael Carrick is refusing to hit the panic button after his Manchester United side were bullied by newly-promoted Hull

Sergej Jakirovic's side blew a passive Manchester United side away with two first half goals

Join the discussion Should Manchester United overhaul their approach after being outplayed by a newly promoted team?

'We've done a lot of good things and we did some good things today, but it gets lost, and I understand it'll get lost, but it doesn't get lost from our point of view.

'There's definitely issues playing against different systems, so we have got to find the answers for that. But just because we lose one game it doesn't mean that everything needs to be dissected and it's wrong from our point of view.'

Carrick is rarely ruffled win, lose, or draw, but behind his calm demeanour here was a coach hurting at seeing his side totally outplayed.

'I'm talking to you quite calm, but I'm not exactly calm inside and enjoying the day, you know?

'So there's a big difference. I played here for a long time. You don't get to play here for a long time without just going day by day, the results, the ups and downs, but you just carry on as normal. It's 100% not that; trust me, it's not that.

'It just doesn't mean that we all have to shout and scream and come out and create some chaos just because of it.

'Inside we're hurting. The boys know we need to get better, but the calmness doesn't mean that there's no emotion in it, for sure.'

For Hull City boss Jakirovic, he is happy to keep proving critics wrong and believes a performance such as this one will help convince transfer targets to make the move between now and the deadline on September 1.

Sports.title: Rossa Ryan's piece of advice inspires Sky Bet Ebor win by Alan King-trained Daiquiri Bay
Sports.content:
Rossa Ryan's piece of advice inspires Sky Bet Ebor win by Alan King-trained Daiquiri Bay

The 10-1 chance held on in an exciting finish to the £500,000 feature race on Saturday, crossing the line front of the Wathnan Racing-owned pair Hopewell Rock and Opportunity

View 2 Images Jockey Rossa Ryan after riding Daiquiri Bay to victory in the Sky Bet Ebor (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

Rossa Ryan was praised for inspiring the Sky Bet Ebor success by talented stayer Daiquiri Bay on the final day of York's racing festival.

‌



The rider pipped the Wathnan Racing-owned pair Hopewell Rock and Opportunity by a head and a neck aboard the 10-1 chance, trained Alan King.

‌



Ryan rode Daiquiri Bay to win the Copper Horse Stakes at Royal Ascot earlier in the season, when the chestnut gelding lowered the track record.

‌



Not seen on a racecourse for two months, a 67-day break was no problem for the upwardly mobile handicapper, who travelled nicely through the field and found enough to hold on in a close finish.

"Full marks to Rossa, we sat down after Ascot and he said put him away and freshen him up," said King, delighted to go two places better than Salsalino's third when favourite in 2003.

Jockey Juan Hernandez rushes to Nunthorpe victory then dashes by helicopter to Heathrow READ MORE :

Race meeting abandoned after two jockeys sent to hospital following heavy falls READ MORE :

"He had a hard race and broke the track record. We haven't missed a beat in the last three weeks. He's a tough horse and it was a great ride. I'm blown away."

‌



Ryan, disappointed to be pipped in the Yorkshire Oaks on the unlucky-in-running Sparan Nua on Wednesday, also had to settle for second in yesterday's Nunthorpe partnering Starlust, who was no match for US raider Bacio.

But while he was out of luck in the Grade One contests, it changed in the highly valuable handicap which rounds off the four-day racing week on the Knavesmire.

View 2 Images The top three dash for the line (Image: Getty Images)

‌



And Ryan was only freed up to compete at the prestigious meeting after a 28-day race-riding ban was reduced to ten on appeal, the original punishment handed out for easing Thunder Home prematurely at Sandown on July 23.

The panel did not accept that the young thoroughbred would inevitably have won had the rider pushed out continuously.

"The man's a genius," said Ryan about King, who has collected numerous top prizes on the Flat and over jumps.

Article continues below

"We’ve had a year where, luckily, we’ve been able to plan him out. After Ascot I thought I'd leave Daiquiri Bay and come straight here. Alan agreed and he had him spot on."

Ebor gambles on Willie Mullins' number one Love Me Tender (7-2 favourite) and another Irish raider Emit (4-1) from Joseph O'Brien's stable, went astray.

Ascending (28-1) filled fourth as the field of 22 horses passed the post, with Beylerbeyi (20-1) in fifth for the boosted each-way places with some bookmakers.

Sports.content:
US Open make huge Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz announcement

With the US Open now on the horizon, a huge decision involving Carlos Alcaraz and Serena Williams has since been revealed

Serena Williams will partner up with Carlos Alcaraz in the mixed doubles of the US Open. Alcaraz had recently confirmed he would be at Flushing Meadows, having recovered from a persistent wrist injury.

‌



Not only will he be back in singles action, he will also play alongside Williams in what promises to be a blockbuster partnership. Alcaraz has not competed since April, but he will be fit enough to complete a duo which boasts a combined 46 Grand Slam titles.

Sports.title: Arsenal in 'frequent contact' with Julian Alvarez as tensions grow at Atletico Madrid
Sports.content:
Arsenal in 'frequent contact' with Julian Alvarez as tensions grow at Atletico Madrid

Arsenal are still in the running alongside Barcelona to sign Julian Alvarez in the summer transfer window, with the Atletico Madrid striker increasingly unhappy and unsettled

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez is unhappy at Atletico Madrid (Image: Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta have been in 'frequent contact' with Julian Alvarez and haven't given up hope of signing the unsettled Atletico Madrid striker.

‌



The Gunners are determined to add a world-class forward to their squad before the summer transfer window closes. Alvarez has been focused on leaving Atletico Madrid for Barcelona, but hasn't ruled out a return to the Premier League.

‌



Things have got increasingly messy between Atleti and their star forward - and it could play into Arsenal's hands. Barca saw their €100million (£86m) bid rejected earlier this summer, with Atleti then reporting their La Liga rivals for allegedly tapping up the Argentina international.

‌



Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone wants to keep the 26-year-old, but tensions behind the scenes could trigger a transfer. Atleti chief executive Miguel Ángel Gil Marín said on Friday that Alvarez "has not had the best advisors" this summer after saying he wanted to "fulfil his dream" of joining Barca.

Gil Marín's words prompted a not-so-subtle response from Alvarez's agent Fernando Hidalgo, who wrote on social media: "Never ask a liar why he lied. To explain himself, he would have to lie again."

‌



According to ESPN, Barcelona have given up on signing Alvarez, with Atleti refusing to engage in negotiations. They have turned their attention to his Argentina team-mate Lautaro Martinez, of Inter Milan.

AS reports that Alvarez doesn't understand his club's approach to the transfer saga and remains determined to leave before the window closes on September 1. He would still prefer to join Barcelona, but is conscious of not closing the door on Arsenal either.

View 2 Images Arsenal are still interested in a move for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez (Image: (AP Photo/Manu Fernandez))

‌



Arteta and Berta have been keeping in touch with Alvarez, who is said to appreciate their interest. A move to Arsenal is considered to be 'a welcome emergency solution' for Alvarez, even if he doesn't want to uproot his family from Madrid.

He is continuing to train for Atleti, but is expected to receive a frosty reception from the supporters when they host Villarreal on Sunday. Simeone has tried to cool the situation ahead of what should be his first appearance since the World Cup.

"There's no uncertainty. Miguel Ángel [Gil Marín] spoke clearly," he said. "For me he's a really important player to achieve our objectives. We'll be with him, we'll look after him on the sporting side, because he's our player... He'll be in the squad tomorrow."

Article continues below

"Atlético Madrid, like every big club, is built on great players, and Julián is one of them, as well as being a great professional," Gil Marín told EFE on Friday. "We have to compete with our values, with homegrown players and the best players we can bring in from outside.

"We are going to help Julián and continue to look after him, so he can reach his full potential... We must understand that Julián hasn't had the best advisors around him in recent months."

Sports.title: Hull City fans call out TNT Sports pundit during coverage of shock Man Utd win
Sports.content:
Hull City fans call out TNT Sports pundit during coverage of shock Man Utd win

Joe Cole confessed he would be stunned if Hull City avoided relegation and their fans were happy to remind him of that during their win over Manchester United

View 2 Images Hull City fans lapped up their surprise win over Man Utd

Hull City fans called out Joe Cole in the first half of their win over Manchester United as the Premier League new boys got their season off to the dream start.

‌



The Tigers won promotion to the top flight via the play-offs last season having finished sixth and have been tipped by many - including Cole - to finish bottom of the table. Hull haven't been in the Premier League since 2017 and were tipped for the drop last year.

‌



They exceeded expectations, but few expected them to cause such an upset on the opening weekend as they downed the Red Devils, scoring twice in the first half to knock off Michael Carrick's side, who have been tipped to potential finish as high as second.

‌



When discussing Hull's year the TNT Sports pundit said on The Dressing Room podcast that he would be "stunned if they stayed up" - and once they led by two goals the MKM Stadium crowd were keen to remind him.

After Nobel Mendy scored their second goal, heading home from a set piece, the home fans sang: "Are you watching, Joe Cole?" The chant was heard again as the full-time whistle neared.

‌



Hull were more than good value for their three points with United very much kept at bay. The Tigers owner Acun Ilicali admits his team have already been written off, which served as a point of frustration last season, and knows that much the same is happening 12 months on.

He said on TNT Sports: "I was fed up last season, [people tipping us for] relegation - but not like this year. This year, everybody's making predictions. If nobody thinks we will achieve something, I like it like this."

Hull are the favourites for relegation, but their statement win on Saturday afternoon gives them the ideal start. Their most recent spell in the top flight only lasted one year as they went straight back down.

Tigers defender Semi Ajayi, who scored the opener at the MKM Stadium, insists they are not bothered about the doubters. "We're not focused on outside noise," he said. "We back ourselves to do well and hopefully we will have a really positive season."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino clashes with reporter with bald jibe as FIFA boss told to stay away
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino clashes with reporter with bald jibe as FIFA boss told to stay away

Gianni Infantino has spent the last two months under intense scrutiny and it appears the beleaguered FIFA president has developed his own style of media management

View Image Gianni Infantino lashed out at a reporter (Image: Sky)

FIFA president Gianni Infantino mocked a Sky reporter's baldness as he wriggled away from questions about his position. He is still being held to account for his disgraceful plan to essentially sell stocks in the World Cup and other FIFA affiliated competitions.

‌



He has been clinging onto power in desperate fashion despite the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), the Confederation of North, Central America and the Caribbean (CONCACAF), and UEFA all withdrawing their support for him. In addition the football associations of Scotland, Albania, Canada, Croatia, Denmark, England, Finland, Germany, Greece, Guyana, Jordan, Netherlands, New Zealand, Northern Ireland, Norway, Republic of Ireland, Romania, Serbia, Sierra Leone, Sweden and Wales have also expressed their opposition against him.

‌



In and amongst the pressure, Infantino was approached by Sky News journalist James Matthews who wished to ask him questions about his future. Instead of answering, he attempted to bully the reporter.

‌



Matthews asked him if he had betrayed football before requesting an explanation for why he has not resigned from his position. Infantino then snapped back by mocking Matthews' hair.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Infantino, who is also very bald himself, said: "You have a nice haircut, thank you so much. See you at the hairdressers."

‌



Matthews found Infantino in the Dominican Republic, which is a contentious point in itself. It's understood he is there to watch the Caribbean Football Union under-14s tournament.

While local politicians were quick to greet him, the Swiss football bureaucrat was told to stay away from the competition by the head of CONCACAF Victor Montagliano, who is also a vice-president on the FIFA council.

He penned a letter which begin with "As you may be aware, your proposed attendance has garnered significant media attention" before adding his presence would "unfortunately significantly take away from the technical nature of the CFU youth competition."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

It also added: "As such, I respectfully ask you in the name of football to reconsider your attendance as it will unfortunately undermine the technical nature of this important youth development activity."

The Dominican Republic Minister of Sports and Recreation Kelvin Cruz felt differently about Infantino's presence in the country. He said: "We deeply appreciate your visit to the Dominican Republic.

‌



"Without doubt that your presence in our country puts us on the international football radar and opens us great prospects for growth and development of Dominican football."

Infantino is hoping to be elected for a third term, but will likely have plenty of opposition from other governing bodies.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
