World.title: Telecom Minister denies direct starlink deal, confirms EarthLink role
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Minister of Communications Mustafa Jabbar Sanad clarified on Saturday, August 22, 2026, that the Ministry has not signed a direct operational contract with U.S. satellite internet provider Starlink, affirming that domestic telecommunications provider EarthLink remains the state’s primary operational partner under existing service frameworks.

Speaking during a panel session at the 8th Baghdad Dialogue Conference, organized by the Iraqi Institute for Dialogue, Sanad stated that the Ministry seeks to harness market competition to upgrade the country’s digital infrastructure. He noted that while EarthLink and other entities currently provide connectivity, Starlink is slated to transition into a direct partnership role within two years.

Regulatory Oversight and Security Compliance

Participating in the same session, Baligh Abu Kalal, Head of the Communications and Media Commission (CMC), detailed the regulatory and security framework governing satellite internet deployment in Iraq:

Unregulated Terminals: An estimated 40,000 unauthorized Starlink devices were active across Iraq prior to formal regulatory engagement.

National Security Annex: Iraq established a comprehensive security regulatory appendix, making Starlink the first international satellite provider to formally subject its technical operations to Iraqi legal jurisdiction and national security specifications.

Global Precedent: Abu Kalal highlighted that Starlink services operate legally across more than 160 countries worldwide under comparable regulatory frameworks.

Formal Licensing Background: The clarification follows the CMC’s July announcement in the United States—held at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce—confirming the finalization of Starlink’s regulatory license to operate legally within the Iraqi market.

The regulatory track for Starlink reflects Baghdad’s strategy to expand advanced satellite broadband into remote, underserved, and enterprise sectors without undermining existing fiber-optic investments or state regulatory oversight.

By integrating direct licensing with legal compliance protocols, Iraqi authorities aim to regularize existing gray-market hardware, enforce data sovereignty standards, and foster competition across the telecommunications landscape.

World.title: Iran grants exceptional passage for Iraqi oil tankers via Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Following repeated formal requests submitted by the Iraqi government through multiple diplomatic and security channels, Tehran has granted exceptional transit permits for several Iraqi oil tankers, allowing them to navigate through the Strait of Hormuz amid severe maritime insecurity caused by ongoing regional conflict.

According to a report published on Saturday, August 22, 2026, by Iran’s official state news agency, IRNA, securing safe maritime passage for Iraqi crude shipments formed a core agenda item during the recent high-level visit of Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf to Baghdad.

Key Developments & Maritime Details

Exceptional Passage Clearances: Iranian maritime and military authorities approved special security permits facilitating the safe navigation of designated Iraqi crude oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz.

Persistent Diplomatic Requests: Baghdad engaged Tehran repeatedly across bilateral channels to secure formal guarantees for Iraqi energy exports traversing the vital chokepoint.

Severe Maritime Friction: Clearances were authorized despite heightened military alerts, stringent navigational restrictions, and active security threats surrounding the strategic waterway.

Bilateral Coordination: The agreement follows strategic talks in Baghdad between Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and senior Iraqi executive and security officials regarding regional stability, border coordination, and energy security.

The Strait of Hormuz remains the single most critical export conduit for southern Iraqi crude originating from the offshore terminals of Basra.

With regional maritime hostilities threatening international shipping lanes and driving up maritime insurance premiums, securing coordinated transit permits helps Baghdad maintain baseline crude export volumes and fulfill international supply commitments while pipeline diversification initiatives remain underway.

World.title: Former envoys urge joint French, UK action on Palestinian territories
World.content:
Paris – Dozens of former senior French and UK diplomats on Saturday urged their governments to work together to uphold international law in the Palestinian territories, accusing Israel of seeking to “destroy” any prospect of a viable Palestinian state.

The 102 signatories of the letter published in Le Monde included former British ambassadors to the UN Jeremy Greenstock and Emyr Jones Parry as well the former directors for the Middle East at the French foreign ministry Yves Aubin de la Messuziere and Denis Bauchard.

They said the involvement of France and the UK was essential given the historic roles of the two powers in the Middle East and the fact that both permanent members of the UN Security Council, in 2025 recognised a Palestinian state.

“Our two nations believe that those responsible for war crimes and crimes against humanity must be held to account. Only then can our governments rebut the accusation of double standards. That is why they must act together to uphold international law in Palestine,” said the letter.

It accused Israel of seeking “to destroy any prospect of an independent Palestinian state, showing contempt for the law, the rulings of the International Court of Justice and countless UN Security Council resolutions.”

Israel launched a military campaign on the Palestinian territory of Gaza following the October 7, 2023 attack by militant group Hamas against Israel.

Violence in the West Bank, occupied by Israel since 1967, has surged since the Gaza war began, sparking international concern over the conduct of Israeli troops and settlers.

France and Britain this week joined other countries in releasing a statement condeming the Israeli government’s release of new tenders for construction in the occupied West Bank.

The letter said house demolitions and “rampant settler violence — with the connivance of the Israeli army and police” in annexed east Jerusalem and the West Bank amounted to “ethnic cleansing”

“The world no longer sees Israel as a genuine democracy — there is nothing democratic about depriving others of their rights and land,” said the letter.

World.title: Integrity Commission audit uncovers 16K deceased on Iraq pension rolls
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Federal Integrity Commission announced on Friday, August 21, 2026, the launch of a comprehensive cross-matching audit of the National Pension Board’s records following formal approval by Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi.

The nationwide audit uncovered major administrative irregularities and public fund waste, including 16,384 deceased individuals whose pension disbursements were never terminated, alongside 40,000 biometric Qi-Cards issued on obsolete, unverified records.

Key Audit Metrics & Identified Violations

Unstopped Deceased Records:16,384 deceased individuals were verified across Ministry of Health and National Center for Digital Transformation registries as still receiving active monthly pension disbursements with no legal beneficiaries attached.

Outdated Qi-Card Accounts: Roughly 40,000 biometric Qi-Cards were identified as having been issued based on legacy, un-updated databases without duplicate-number prevention checks.

Nineveh Counter-Terror File Review: An inter-agency committee formed by Diwani order is reviewing 102,867 pensioner records for martyrs and victims of terrorism in Nineveh Governorate, uncovering unentitled payments issued without requisite cross-referencing with Martyrs Foundation archives.

Anbar Fraud Suspensions: Approximately 19,321 pension records have been suspended in Anbar Governorate alone due to forged documentation and database discrepancies.

Unprocessed 2022 Suspension Orders: Significant volumes of unstopped records have persisted since 2022 due to the National Pension Board’s failure to cross-reference stop-payment orders issued by the Martyrs Foundation.

The Integrity Commission’s report—submitted to the Prime Minister’s Office, the Ministry of Finance, and the National Pension Board—highlighted widespread systemic flaws, deliberate data tampering, and complicity among branch managers in liberated governorates:

World.title: PM Al Zaidi outlines $100B fund, 10M bpd oil goal and housing plan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi delivered a comprehensive policy address during a panel session at the 8th Baghdad Dialogue Conference, organized by the Iraqi Institute for Dialogue on Friday, August 21, 2026.

Al-Zaidi laid out the executive branch’s multi-year development roadmap, assuring public sector salary security, launching structural financial and housing initiatives, and outlining plans to scale crude oil production capacity while enforcing state monopoly over arms and modernizing national infrastructure.

Key Policy Pillars & Strategic Directives

1. Energy Expansion, Pipeline Redundancy & OPEC Targets

Export Diversification: Baghdad is actively accelerating alternative crude export routes through the Turkish port of Ceyhan, alongside active development for pipeline corridors via Baniyas (Syria) and Aqaba (Jordan).

Long-Term Export Goal: Iraq is formally requesting an increased OPEC quota reflecting its population size and proven reserves, targeting export capacity of 8 to 10 million barrels per day (bpd) within six years.

Domestic Fuel Savings: Downstream consumption and fuel management reforms are projected to yield 17.8 trillion IQD ($13.6B) in annual fiscal savings.

Power Grid & Renewables: The upcoming federal budget will prioritize electricity generation, transmission, and smart distribution, alongside large-scale utility solar deployments.

2. $100B Iraq Development Fund & Private Sector Transition

Capitalization Architecture: The Iraq Development Fund will be capitalized at $100 billion, financed through Central Bank equity, public stock offerings (IPOs), and co-investments from regional and international development finance institutions (DFIs).

Tax & Customs Modernization: Instituted pre-clearance import taxation linked directly to official wire transfers (refundable if imports do not clear), coupled with targeted customs duty reductions to encourage formal trade compliance.

Workforce Shift: Establishing regulatory mechanisms and incentives to shift labor migration from state-dependent employment toward the private sector.

3. State Arms Monopoly & Security Guarantees

Consensus on Arms Integration: Al-Zaidi confirmed unified political consensus across parliamentary blocs to consolidate all weapons under state authority, establishing operational mechanisms for weapons handover.

Investment Safeguards: Emphasized that unregulated weapons outside state command directly repel foreign capital, reiterating that Baghdad will prevent any escalation or military confrontations on Iraqi soil.

4. One Million Residential Plots & Agricultural Programs

Three-Year Housing Delivery: Finalizing the launch of the “One Million Residential Plots” initiative, providing modern, master-planned housing lands to non-homeowners, with the final beneficiaries receiving land in under three years through the National Investment Commission (NIC).

Agricultural Enterprise Grants: Allocating designated agricultural parcels paired with structured development loans specifically for agricultural engineers and veterinary professionals.

5. Governance, Procurement Reform & Leadership Pledge

Ex-Ante Anti-Corruption Audits: Shifting procurement oversight from lagging post-audits to pre-contract price verification and benchmark auditing to eliminate inflated tender pricing.

One-Term Commitment: Al-Zaidi reaffirmed his formal pledge not to seek a second term as prime minister, stating that the cabinet’s structural reforms are designed for institutional longevity under subsequent administrations.

Regional Diplomacy: Positioning Iraq permanently as a diplomatic bridge for regional negotiations and conflict de-escalation rather than an arena for regional proxy friction.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s address at the Baghdad Dialogue provides a structural counter-strategy to ongoing fiscal pressures, connecting non-oil revenue reform directly with capital mobilization.

By capitalizing a $100 billion sovereign vehicle, pre-auditing public tenders, and diversifying crude export corridors, the administration aims to transition Iraq from short-term fiscal containment toward large-scale infrastructure self-sufficiency and private-market expansion.

World.title: Trump tariffs heap up as Canada tries to curb US reliance
World.content:
Montreal – US President Donald Trump’s 50-percent tariffs on certain Canadian goods which took effect Saturday delivered another blow to bilateral trade, renewing focus on Ottawa’s efforts to reduce dependence on its southern neighbor.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s strategy involves a search for new markets, a focus on domestic trade and the launch of major projects.

– Inter-connected markets –

The two economies are heavily inter-connected, with roughly 70 percent of all Canadian exports heading to the United States.

Previous Trump levies on autos, steel, aluminum and lumber have hit Canada hard, forcing job losses and stunting growth.

Canada has even entered a technical recession this year after two consecutive quarters of economic contraction.

The latest 50-percent tariffs came into force after days of negotiations failed to produce an agreement.

They impact some $20 billion worth of goods, or 5.5 percent of Canadian exports to the United States, targeting products ranging from hockey sticks to cement.

Carney said Friday that Canada would match the US tariffs “dollar for dollar to protect our workers and businesses.”

– Breaching the shield –

The exports affected by the US tariffs include products that were previously protected under the North American trade pact, the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA).

At first glance, “that’s frightening,” said Richard Ouellet, a professor of international economic law at Quebec’s Laval University.

“Until now, the USMCA acted as kind of a shield. The Americans are opening a breach,” he told AFP.

Trump declined to renew the USMCA on July 1, making it subject to annual reviews.

While Trump ditching USMCA exemptions could forecast more extreme measures to come, Canada’s largest bank, RBC, predicted the first package of 50-percent tariffs won’t “significantly change broader Canadian growth.”

“That’s because the new tariffs, while significant, will still impact a small segment of total trade,” RBC said last month, adding that around 80 percent of Canadian goods would still enter the United States tariff-free.

– ‘Diversification’ –

Since taking office in March 2025, Carney has focused on diversifying economic partnerships to reduce Canada’s reliance on the US market.

“Canada has what the world wants,” Carney said in a statement following the breakdown of negotiations with Washington.

“We will not allow any nation to determine our future,” he said.

The prime minister has headed to China, India and Saudi Arabia and made several stops in Europe seeking deals to expand Canada’s economic relationships overseas.

In January, he signed a preliminary agreement with China, providing for the import of electric vehicles to Canada.

Relations with Europe have also been strengthened. In July, Canada selected the German firm TKMS to build its new fleet of submarines.

Last month, Canada’s central bank said the economy was “showing signs of improving,” noting that some businesses were adjusting to US protectionism, including by finding new customers abroad.

A report from Canada’s international trade minister also said that in 2025 the value of exports to non-US markets jumped by 11 percent, hitting 33 percent at one point — the highest level in more than four decades.

– Domestic revitalization –

Another factor that could help cushion the impact of Trump’s tariffs is a renewed focus on domestic trade.

One of Carney’s first major initiatives as prime minister was federal legislation to reduce interprovincial trade barriers.

Provinces have shown reluctance to lift their own restrictions, but Ouellet said that overall “the Canadian market has been reinvigorated and there is more domestic trade.”

Carney has also tried to jumpstart domestic economic activity through his Major Projects Office, set up to reduce bureaucratic delays and grant quicker approval for select large-scale infrastructure initiatives.

Carney has promised port expansion in Montreal and Vancouver and new mines to exploit critical minerals, as well as backing plans for an oil pipeline from Alberta to the Pacific.

Overall, Ottawa has unveiled plans to spend CAN$115 billion ($83 billion) on infrastructure and an unprecedented CAN$82 billion on defense over the coming years.

World.title: US, Canada fail to reach trade pact to avert Trump tariffs
World.content:
Washington – Hefty US tariffs on some Canadian products took effect on Saturday after days of negotiations that went down to the wire failed to produce an agreement.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney vowed that his country will match the US tariffs “dollar for dollar to protect our workers and businesses,” as officials said late Friday that Washington and Ottawa had not managed to strike a deal.

The lack of a final agreement means that new 50-percent duties impacting some $20 billion worth of goods, or 5.5 percent of Canadian exports to the United States, came into force.

Impacted products range from hockey sticks to cement.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Friday that “tonight, Canada declined to finalize the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week.”

That came despite Washington’s offers for tariff reductions in sectors like steel and aluminum, he added in a statement.

A senior US official said there are no further scheduled meetings for now.

The surprise announcement came after Trump said that the United States “should be able to have a deal with Canada,” citing his “good relationship” with Carney.

After hours of trade talks on Friday, however, Canada’s top negotiator Dominic LeBlanc told reporters that officials still “have more work to do.”

LeBlanc and Greer also met for around three hours on Thursday.

Greer said that the Trump administration put on the table “significant tariff reductions on steel, aluminum, autos and lumber” in exchange for concessions from Canada.

He said that Canada was also maintaining its “prolonged retaliation” against the United States, including prohibitions on certain American goods and services.

Canada’s regional leaders said previously that the United States was particularly irritated by one retaliatory measure: the removal of US alcohol and wine from liquor stores.

But Carney added in a separate statement that “last-minute changes in the US proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal.”

While Washington and Ottawa made “important progress” in recent weeks, Carney said, this “has not been enough to meet our objectives for Canadians.”

The senior US official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said Canada had sought additional concessions that the United States was unable to provide.

But they added that talks were candid and not acrimonious.

– ‘Significant pressure’ –

Ryan Majerus, a former US commerce official, told AFP that “if Canada has agreed to also impose retaliatory tariffs, that will make deescalating this a lot harder.”

“But I think both sides will face significant pressure in the coming days to find an off-ramp,” added Majerus, a trade lawyer with King & Spalding.

Christopher Padilla, another former US official who is now with Brunswick Group, told AFP there has been “a lot of hope among businesses on both sides” for a deal to “turn the page on what has been a very difficult eighteen months in the US-Canada relationship.”

The White House had alleged “discriminatory treatment” by Canada against US alcohol, automobile and dairy products in introducing the duties.

They were originally set to take effect on Wednesday, before Trump issued a last-minute delay of three days, citing major progress in talks.

Canadian negotiators had been camped out in Washington this week to firm up a deal that aimed to address various flash points.

Canada has been seeking relief from Trump’s tariffs on autos, steel and aluminum, which have battered the country’s economy, forced job losses and strained what was once an iron-clad trade relationship.

Carney has repeatedly told Canadians that relations with the United States have been forever changed, regardless of what happens with an individual trade deal.

He says the country must diversify and reduce its reliance on the United States, which currently accounts for roughly 70 percent of Canadian exports.

Beyond the latest tariffs, the United States and Canada still have to agree on revisions to the North American free trade agreement, USMCA, which Trump declined to renew in its current form.

World.title: Brazil’s Lula urges tariffs resolution in call with Trump
World.content:
Brasília – Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva urged US counterpart Donald Trump in a phone call Friday to resolve their countries’ trade dispute, saying US tariffs were imposed on “baseless” grounds.

Washington imposed two new sets of tariffs on the Latin American giant in July, a move that has become a key campaign issue ahead of Brazil’s presidential election in October.

Lula — seeking a fourth and final term — told Trump that the tariffs “negatively affect both Brazil and the United States,” according to a statement from his office.

“To remain at the negotiating table is the best option for both countries,” he said.

Relations between Trump and the leftist Lula have blown hot and cold in recent months, but diplomatic tensions have flared as the election approaches.

Trump has backed several victorious right-wing candidates in recent Latin American elections. He is an ally of Brazil’s jailed far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, whose son Flavio is Lula’s main election rival.

The Brazilian presidency statement said the conversation between Trump and Lula lasted an hour and 20 minutes and “took place in a friendly and cordial tone.”

During a campaign event in the southeastern state of Minas Gerais, Lula said Trump asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to contact his Brazilian counterpart Marcio Elias Rosa “and they already scheduled a meeting.”

He added that Trump acknowledged during their call that the tariffs on Brazil are “based on a lie.”

Lula, who like Trump is 80, has made national sovereignty a key theme of his campaign.

In an interview last week, he warned Trump: “Don’t meddle in Brazil’s affairs, especially regarding the election. If you do meddle, you’ll lose.”

“I said, ‘Hey Trump, if you want to fight organized crime, let’s fight organized crime,'” Lula told the crowd in Minas Gerais. “We want to work together. What we don’t want is interference in Brazil.”

– ‘Daily terror’-

The two leaders have often appeared to get on well one-on-one, with Trump last year hailing an “excellent chemistry” with Lula.

The US last year dropped punitive tariffs it imposed over the trial against Jair Bolsonaro, which Trump labelled a “witch hunt,” after diplomatic efforts by Lula’s government.

However, Lula then suffered a blow after a May visit to the White House by Flavio Bolsonaro.

Two days later, the US designated Brazil’s two largest drug cartels as terrorist organizations — which Flavio has said was a personal request.

“These criminal groups inflict daily terror on the most vulnerable populations, but they are not the same as terrorist organizations,” Lula told Trump.

Security is the main concern of Brazilians heading into this year’s elections, polls have shown.

Flavio Bolsonaro is pushing for a tough-on-crime model like that of El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele, whose sweeping crackdown on gangs and mass detentions have drawn controversy.

– Deforestation and PIX –

The United States imposed a 25-percent tariff on a range of Brazilian goods over policies it argued harm US commerce — such as deforestation and a free electronic payments system known as PIX.

Brazilian data shows deforestation in the Amazon fell last year to its lowest point since 2016.

Brazil was also impacted under a separate global tariff regime against US trading partners accused of using forced labor.

Lula has repeatedly said he believes it was US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and not Trump who was behind the tariffs against Brazil.

“Trump is the best of the lot, and the one who talks most seriously with me,” he said last week.

World.title: Karnataka man arrested after Instagram trail unveils links to ‘Pakistani gangsters’
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A 25-year-old AC mechanic was arrested in Karnataka on charges of a terrorist act after police allegedly found he was in contact with Pakistan-based gangsters through social media, officials said on Friday.

The accused, identified as Syed Abubakar, a resident of Islampur, was arrested by Doddaballapur Town police after a tip-off led them to examine his mobile phone and alleged online activities.

Police said Abubakar was using an Instagram account named "sayedabudakar 313" and had allegedly liked reels featuring Pakistan-based gangsters posted by an account identified as "Hammadmemon 333".

According to the FIR, Abubakar had also uploaded videos of gangsters as Instagram status updates and shared his identity card with the "Hammadmemon 333" account.

Several photographs of pistols were also allegedly found on his phone.

The case came to light after a police constable attached to Doddaballapur Town police station received information on August 20 that Abubakar was allegedly involved in suspicious dealings with people from Pakistan.

The FIR alleged that Abubakar could potentially attempt to instigate youths against India and engage in activities detrimental to the sovereignty of the country.

World.title: Ex-IAF vice-chief Kapoor says India’s 4.5-gen Tejas may not have relevance in 2030s, country must partner with global consortiums like FCAS or GCAP for 6th-gen programme
World.content:
Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future

NEW DELHI: Less than two months after retirement as the IAF's vice chief, Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force, saying, âwhy must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the otherâ.In an interview to NDTV, the IAF veteran said, âWhy must we be hamstrung because someone somewhere has not been able to keep their promises?âThe delivery of the indigenous LCA Tejas Mk1A jets by HAL to the IAF has faced multi-year delays, primarily caused by late supplies of F404-IN20 engines by American GE company, complex mission software validation, and stringent operational requirements set by the IAF.When asked if advanced Tejas Mk-2 may be operationally relevant when it starts entering service in big numbers in mid 2030s at a time when China is already raising its fleet of its 5th-generation fighter jet, the former vice-chief said, âNo, operationally, definitely no.âWith China on its way to deploying 500 5th-generation J-20 fighters by 2030, India is still struggling to get the delivery of the first squadron by 4.5-generation Tejas Mk1A. Though the IAF had placed orders for a total of 180 Tejas Mk1A fighter jets long ago, HAL hopes to deliver the first 18-25 Tejas Mk1A only by March 2027.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future when he said, âYou can have a certain number of those 5th generation and 6th generation fighters, but given the size of the country, you won't be able to deploy them everywhere.So those gaps which continue to remain to be filled will have to be filled by this class of aircraft.â âI want Tejas Mk-2 to come, I want Indiaâs 5th-gen AMCA to come. But they must come at a much faster speed,â he said.When asked about Russiaâs 5th-gen fighter jet Su-57, the former vice-chief said when the Russian fighter is compared to western jets like American F-35, western jets have an edge over the Su-57 as they have better avionics and stealth.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) suggested that India should partner with an European consortium working on state-of-the-art sixth generation platforms. âThere are other things that are happening â why not join FCAS (Future Combat Air System is the European programme for 6th generation jet under development by French Dassault Aviation, Airbus and Indra Sistemas) Why not GCAP (Global Combat Air Programme is a multinational initiative led by Italy, Japan, and UK to jointly develop a sixth-generation jet).ââ'You are probably going with a consortium which has got a good record of delivery, of development. Why go through this Gen 4, Gen 4.5 steps when you know the next best thing is already being thought of and why not just join up there?,â the IAF veteran said.

World.title: World in churn, and India’s foreign policy needs to adapt to it
World.content:
Disclaimer : Views expressed above are the author's own.

There is a growing sense that something is seriously amiss in Indiaâs foreign policy. Yet, foreign policy debate is still tiptoeing around the big questions.There were three foundational assumptions that underlay Indian choices at the turn of this century. First, no great power in history had acquired such preponderance over its rivals as the US had by 2000. US primacy also meant there was no way to avoid hitching a ride with the US.Second, to make the arrangement mutually attractive, a common antagonist, China, was projected to help overcome decades of dissonance and suspicion that had divided Indians and Americans. The new discourse played on Indian ego and US greed. Washington would lift Delhi in the international pecking order, while India would generate business and arms sales for America. If everything unfolded as planned, India would become a prized Western sentinel in Asia, cementing US hegemony for the 21st century.Third, although the world economy had broadened by the early 2000s, the US was firmly at the helm in connecting the Global South to the G-7. Interdependence was a euphemism for a US-led geoeconomic order that would dominate innovation, supply chains and international trade.All three assumptions have been shattered in recent years. One, the US has not just lost its primacy, it has lost its ability to control major geopolitical events. Every roll of the dice in recent years to arrest its decline â the trade standoff with China, NATOâs confrontation with Russia, the clash against Iran â has produced a blowback that has further weakened it.Historically, the balance of power has always been ultimately revealed through major war. The present phase is no exception. The Ukraine and Iran wars have not just depleted NATO arsenals, they have exposed the doctrinal fragility of Western military power.Two, China has raced so far ahead that the rhetoric from two decades ago of an Indian âcatch-upâ and âthe 21st century rivalryâ appears absurd to any sober observer. The Chinese lead is not merely in aggregate economic terms but in the underlying policy institutions, human capital and technologies.And, most crucially of all, the commanding heights of the world economy are inexorably shifting towards the east. From manufacturing and high technologies to energy and natural resources, consumer demand, and financial capital, the greater Eurasian continent and its periphery have all the core requirements of sustaining a dynamic geoeconomic order without dependence on the Atlantic West. At no point in recent centuries was such a Eurasian-centred globalisation possible.But even as world events have upended the Indian foreign policy consensus, a network of gatekeepers is stubbornly impervious to change. The defenders of the failed policy erect a straw man to frighten policymakers from a thoughtful reassessment. China, they say, must remain the raison dâÃªtre of Indian policy planning even as US predatory actions seek to eviscerate the last vestiges of Indiaâs strategic independence and authority in the subcontinent. Much has changed between 2005 â when the US pledged to help make India a âmajor power in the 21st centuryâ â and 2026, when a US diplomat publicly warned that India would never be permitted to acquire the sinews of a great power. Pentagon official Elbridge Colby even had the cheek to imply that US strategic interests vis-Ã -vis China would not be held hostage to disputes within Asia.Must India be the only rigid actor amidst all these churnings and machinations around it? The search for a workable modus vivendi with China must acquire a bipartisan policy priority, not as an afterthought to merely prevent conflict in the Himalayas but as a means to diversify a dangerous dependence on the West. India needs to permanently discard the proxy role that it assumed during the unipolar moment and recover its regional power identity that allows for differences as well as shared responsibilities with China. The world is becoming multipolar. And such a future demands responsible Eurasian powers to safeguard world order and stability. It is in Indiaâs vital interests to play such a role.Indiaâs foreign policy debate canât be stuck on an old framework, one that prides itself on managing the distance between Delhi and the great powers. There is no geopolitical room or surplus strength in any great powerâs tent to underwrite Indiaâs social, economic and security challenges. The Cold War is over. The post-Cold War era is over too. The transformation in world politics demands a new intellectual framework where sovereignty, regional interdependence, new geoeconomic networks of trade and investment, international public goods and order-building are placed at the front and centre of Indiaâs foreign policy.To change course, Indian leaders need to look at the day after tomorrow.

World.title: 'You don't belong to anyone else, but yourself': Rahul Gandhi's  message to young women
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday described Indiaâs 70 crore women as the countryâs âbiggest assetâ, saying they are more forward-looking than men and have a crucial role in shaping the nationâs future.

He also invoked the idea of women's autonomy and said that a woman should have the exclusive ownership of her own life.

Speaking at the fourth event of 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' at the AISSMS College Ground in Pune, Maharashtra, he invoked a verse from the Manusmriti and contrasted it with his call for the empowerment and autonomy of women.

Rejecting the idea of women being liable to other men, he asserted that a woman's exclusive ownership belongs to herself.

While acknowledging that the relationships in a womanâs life are important, he stressed that they do not determine her identity or ownership.

Speaking on the central theme of the evening, âbreak the cageâ, Rahul Gandhi called on the audience to recognise the individuality that sets each person apart and to resist the pressures that seek to confine them to predetermined identities or expectations. He said the most important message he wanted people to take away from the evening was a simple but powerful one: âEvery single one of you is unique in this universe.





â

Elaborating on the idea, Rahul Gandhi stressed that individuality is not merely about being different from others, but about recognising oneâs own worth and identity. âYou are unique. You are special. You are an individual,â he told the audience. He emphasised that every person has a distinct way of looking at the world, a different set of aspirations and the ability to imagine a life beyond the boundaries imposed on them.

Rahul further connected this sense of individuality to the freedom to dream and choose oneâs own path. âAnd you have your own dream, your own vision for your life,â he said. The emphasis, he suggested, was not simply on having dreams, but on having the freedom to define those dreams for oneself rather than allowing society, circumstances or established notions of what one âshouldâ be to determine them.

Through the theme of âbreak the cageâ, the LoP framed personal freedom as the ability to step outside these limitations and acknowledge that no individual should be reduced to a role, label or identity prescribed by others.

His message was that recognising oneâs uniqueness is the first step towards claiming the freedom to shape oneâs own future, pursue oneâs aspirations and live according to oneâs own vision of life.

Rahul Gandhi attacks Manusmriti

Rahul Gandhi launched a sharp attack on the Manusmriti over its treatment of women, criticising the textâs prescription that women should remain under the authority of male relatives throughout their lives. He contrasted the idea with his call for womenâs autonomy, arguing that a womanâs identity and freedom should not be defined by her relationship with her father, husband or sons.

Quoting from the Manusmriti, Rahul Gandhi said, âI (would) like to quote here the Manusmriti, which says clearly that in childhood a female must be subject to her father, in youth she belongs to her husband and, when her lord is dead, she belongs to her sons. A woman must never be independent.â

Calling the words unacceptable, Rahul Gandhi added, âThese words are a shame. These words should not have been spoken.â He said the country should instead recognise women as individuals with their own aspirations and agency, describing Indiaâs 70 crore women as its âbiggest strengthâ because of their â70 crore unique journeys, unique imagination, unique dreamsâ.

His remarks framed the debate around womenâs independence as a broader question of individual freedom, with Rahul arguing that women should have the right to define their own identities and determine the course of their lives rather than be treated as belonging to male relatives.

Event follows political storm, clashes

The event follows a political storm and clashes between student organisations. The programme was preceded by a midnight clash between the NSUI and ABVP at the COEP Technological University hostel.

It happened after ABVP claimed that female students were being forced to attend the event. Meanwhile, Congress leaders countered the claims, saying two female students, who had earlier expressed their support for the event, were threatened and confined inside the hostel.

BJP has also accused Congress of paying influencers and manufacturing crowds for the event. Meanwhile, Congress has alleged that the ruling establishment was attempting to disrupt Rahul Gandhiâs student outreach.

NSUI-ABVP clash erupts at COEP hostel

Tensions escalated on Friday night when NSUI and ABVP members clashed at the COEP hostel campus ahead of the LoPâs interaction. Police resorted to a lathi charge to control the situation, while several injured activists were taken to Sancheti Hospital.

According to police sources cited in the material, the Shivajinagar Police registered cases against 50 to 60 people, including six named NSUI and Youth Congress activists, following a complaint by an ABVP member.

The confrontation reportedly centred on student participation in LoP Rahul Gandhiâs programme. NSUI activists said they were responding to distress calls from female students, while ABVP alleged that Congress-linked workers were forcibly encouraging hostellers to register for the event.

Congress alleges female students were intimidated

Congress leaders accused ABVP workers of entering the girlsâ hostel and intimidating students who had expressed support for the event.

Congress spokesperson Atul Londhe alleged that a female student was cornered and forced to apologise on camera. NSUI state president Sagar Salunke claimed that students had called the organisation for help and alleged that CCTV cameras had been switched off before NSUI members arrived.

Salunke also alleged that students, including orphaned students, had been pressured to record videos praising the college administration.

The case registered by police followed a complaint from 21-year-old student Malhar Nilesh Patil, who alleged that a studentâs video statement had been recorded under pressure at the hostel.

Pawan Khera alleges conspiracy to disrupt event

Congress leader Pawan Khera alleged that there had been a conspiracy to disrupt LoP's Pune programme, claiming that the response among young people had rattled those in power.

Khera linked the controversy to the issues female students were expected to raise with Rahul, including alleged diversion of scholarship funds.

He accused ABVP workers of intimidating students and said the incident reflected an attempt to keep women away from public decision-making.

He also invoked Puneâs history as the city where Savitribai Phule pioneered womenâs education, arguing that the theme of the event was particularly relevant to the city.

BJP calls event âPaise Ki Goonjâ

The BJP launched a separate attack on the programme, accusing the Congress of paying influencers to mobilise attendance and promote Rahul Gandhiâs event on social media.

BJP Maharashtra spokesperson Navnath Ban alleged that influencers were being offered Rs 30,000 to Rs 35,000 each, along with travel expenses, and claimed that the overall expenditure could reach Rs 9 crore to Rs 10 crore if around 3,000 people were paid.

Ban dubbed the programme âPaise Ki Goonjâ instead of âChhatron Ki Goonjâ and demanded an investigation into the source of the alleged funds. BJP leader Keshav Upadhyay separately accused Rahul Gandhi of using student issues as a political platform.

Congress hits back, says BJP ârattledâ by youth response

The Congress rejected the BJPâs allegations and accused it of trying to create obstacles to LoP Rahul Gandhiâs programme because of his growing support among young people.

Maharashtra Congress spokesperson Sachin Sawant claimed that the BJP was particularly apprehensive about Rahul's appeal among Gen Z and alleged that authorities and ABVP members had attempted to disrupt the programme.

NCP (SP) leader Mahesh Tapase also criticised the BJP, saying there was no reason to oppose a programme focused on issues affecting students and young people.

What is âChhatron Ki Goonjâ about?

Rahulâs Pune interaction with female students is centred on student and youth concerns, with issues such as paper leaks, unemployment and the education system expected to feature in the programme.

The Congress has sought to position the initiative as a platform for students to directly raise their concerns, while the BJP has characterised it as a political campaign by the Leader of the Opposition. The Pune event, therefore, has begun against the backdrop of an escalating political battle over who controls the narrative around student and youth concerns.

World.title: 'Deal with China confidently': Jaishankar on India strategy; lays out 3Cs, 4Ds global outlook
World.content:
NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Saturday offered a candid assessment of a rapidly changing global landscape, warning that growing geopolitical and economic tensions are creating new challenges for countries and businesses.

He also stressed that India must remain engaged with the world's major economies while strengthening its own industrial and economic capabilities.

Speaking at the Economic Times World Leaders Forum 2026, Jaishankar said the emerging global environment required countries to reduce vulnerabilities, broaden their economic options and prepare for disruptions rather than rely on assumptions of stability.

He framed his assessment around three defining features of the present world order: competition, conflict and the growing use of economic and strategic leverage.

To navigate these pressures, he proposed a four-part approach centred on reducing risks, diversifying partnerships and sources, addressing market distortions and maintaining a margin of safety.

On China, Jaishankar said India should continue doing business with Beijing while developing the domestic strength needed to compete with it. He said greater self-reliance, industrialisation and manufacturing capacity would allow India to engage China more confidently rather than disengage from it.





"We have to do business with the entire world. That includes China too. But it is important we deal with them confidently."

Jaishankar said India-China relations had gone through a difficult period between 2020 and 2024 because of the border situation, but both countries had an interest in maintaining stable ties. He also said India needed to make up for decades of shortcomings in building its manufacturing and industrial base.

"So I think a stronger, more self-reliant India, a more industrialised India, a more manufacturing India will be able to actually compete with China as it will with other major countries of the world."

Jaishankar's 3Cs view of the world

"It's not a very comforting answer I'm going to give," Jaishankar said while describing how he sees the world today.

He said the world had become increasingly competitive, with countries and policymakers pursuing their interests to a point where competition could turn into conflict.

"I think what we've seen particularly in the last year or so, but I would really describe it as a growing trend. It looks increasingly competitive," he said, adding that countries and policymakers were pushing their interests "to a point where you actually have conflicts."

He pointed to the Russia-Ukraine conflict and the conflict in West Asia as major examples, noting that one had entered its fifth year while there was still no clear "light at the end of the tunnel" for the other.

Jaishankar said competition was no longer confined to traditional geopolitical rivalry, with economic and strategic tools increasingly being "weaponised".

"This is a world increasingly characterised by choke points," he said, explaining that such a choke point emerges when "a country or a set of countries have established dominance" in a particular field and are prepared to use that dominance to exert pressure.

According to Jaishankar, such leverage can "inflict pain" on others, while countries exercising it may believe they are sufficiently insulated from the consequences.

The 4Ds response

Jaishankar then outlined what he described as a response to these challenges.

"If I declare the problems in terms of Cs, maybe I move an alphabet beyond," he said, presenting derisking as his first and "biggest mantra".

"Derisking will be my biggest mantra," Jaishankar said, stressing that the principle applied not only to businesses but also to politics and strategy.

His second D was diversification.

"The more partners, the more sources that you have, clearly extending that you derisk," he said, arguing that countries and businesses should avoid excessive dependence on a small number of partners or sources.

The third was dealing with distortions. Jaishankar pointed to disruptions in energy, fertiliser and shipping markets linked to conflicts and the emergence of choke points.

For his final point, he urged businesses and policymakers to move beyond the traditional principle of "Trust and Verify".

"Today I say 'Distrust and Diversify'," he said, arguing that planning should take into account the possibility that "things may not go right".

He also warned against excessive reliance on just-in-time supply chains and the assumption that the lowest cost should always determine economic decisions.

"Don't let your supply chain really be just in time anymore; don't assume that your lowest cost will be the determinant," he said, stressing the importance of building a "margin of safety".

India-China ties need stability

Turning to China, Jaishankar said India's engagement with Beijing should ultimately help modernise the Indian economy and strengthen domestic capabilities, even as trade and other economic interactions continue.

"But for us, the interaction is the purpose of it is finally to modernise our economy and to develop our capabilities, but even as we do so, obviously there will be trade, there will be other economic interactions with them."

He said India and China had experienced a particularly difficult phase between 2020 and 2024.

"I think we went through a particularly bad patch between the summer of 2020 and the autumn of 2024, and that was primarily an outcome of the situation in the border"

However, he said both countries remained major economies and markets for each other, and that greater cooperation could be possible if relations remained stable and moved in a more cooperative direction.

At the same time, Jaishankar said India had to address the weaknesses created by decades of inadequate industrialisation.

"We stand our ground as we have stood in the border. We develop our strengths, which unfortunately, as I said, from the 1960s for half a century, we did not do."

"We have to make up for the shortcomings and you know the the mistakes of the past, and and that is really what we are hoping to do."

Jaishankar said building a stronger manufacturing base would be central to India's ability to compete with China and other major economies.

India has raised Chinese visa concerns

Jaishankar also acknowledged concerns among Indian businesses over difficulties obtaining Chinese business visas, saying the government had taken up the issue.

"So, in seeing those stories about business visa issues, which our businessmen have been facing, yes, we have seen it, and I want to say, I mean, for those of you who may have an interest or who may have been affected, we have taken it up as well."

At the political and strategic level, he said both India and China had an interest in maintaining stable relations.

"I would also say, at a political level, at a strategic level, they, you know, it's both of us have an interest in maintaining a certain, you know, I would say stable relationship here."

Jaishankar cautions against US-China 'G2' narrative

Jaishankar also urged caution over the idea of a US-China "G2", saying the relationship between Washington and Beijing remained fundamentally competitive despite areas of cooperation.

"I think people use that term. I would advise you to treat it with some caution, because the fact is, if you look at the US-China relationship, I think at its heart it's a fundamentally competitive relationship."

He said the two countries could still cooperate in some areas and remain largely indifferent to each other in others.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"But as is often the case, it can also be collaborative in certain matters. It can be indifferent in certain sectors."

He added that the US and China would not necessarily compete on every issue, in every geography or at every point in time.

"So it is not that they will compete on every issue and every geography and every time flight."

Jaishankar concluded that the uncertainty confronting governments and businesses represented a broader shift in the global environment.

"I think this is the reality of the world. It applies to national policymakers; it applies to enterprise decisions," Jaishankar said, concluding: "I think it is a realistic picture."

World.title: ‘Modi Chalisa’ controversy: Press Club of India pesident says event violated venue rules
World.content:
Press Club of India president speaks out on 'Modi chalisa' row. Photo credit: PTI

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: Press Club of India president Sangeeta Barooah Pisharoty on Saturday said the journalistsâ body neither organised nor endorsed the âModi Chalisaâ event at its premises, calling it âa victim of a breach of trustâ.Sharing a video statement on X, Pisharoty said the Press Club regularly rents out its premises and has a standard operating procedure (SOP) governing such events.âBy now several of you may have noticed a photograph or a video clip featuring certain individuals reciting what they call the Modi Chalisa at the Press Club of India. At the outset, I want to reiterate clearly that that event was neither organized by the Press Club of India nor it endorsed it. A clear no,â she said.The clarification came after photographs and videos from Thursdayâs event were widely circulated online, showing a cutout of Prime Minister Narendra Modi being depicted in a god-like manner as a devotional poem described as the âModi Chalisaâ was recited. The Press Club had issued a clarification the same day, stating that it had not organised the event and that club authorities stopped it after the terms of the venue booking were violated.Pisharoty said the clubâs rules require every event to be recommended by a member, who must also be present during the programme.âIn this case, the trust placed by the club on the recommending member was breached,â she said, adding that the member was not present during the event, which was itself a violation of club rules.She said the hall had been booked for a press conference, but the organisers instead lit a live fire indoors.âInstead a live fire was lit indoors inside the hall which was a huge violation of the terms under which our venue is rented out,â Pisharoty said, adding that the secretary general has also issued show-cause notices to those concerned and initiated a review of the SOPs, she said.The organiser, Rajan Singh, vice-president of the Bihar State Transgender Welfare Board, told PTI that he planned to construct a temple for Modi in Bihar.âFor the first time ever, Prime Minister Narendra Modi ensured that the transgender community gets its rights... If we want to construct a temple for him, what is wrong with it?â Singh said.He said the proposed temple for âLord Shri Narendra Modi jiâ would cost Rs 112 crore and be built on five acres of land in Bihar.Pisharoty, meanwhile, said the Press Club would continue to focus on media freedom and open discussion.âThe Press Club of India has always stood for the rights and freedoms of journalists,â she said, adding that the Managing Committee was committed to âpreserving and carrying forward that legacyâ.

World.title: One is not born, but becomes: India's drag story, from myth to modern stage
World.content:
India has a rich but complex history of men performing femininityâone that modern drag queens are reclaiming with agency, drawing from both Indian tradition and global queer culture

The history of 'drag' in India

Contemporary drag

Drag queen: Lush Monsoon

Drag queen: Noor Sins

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The most heavily quoted feminist scholar, Simone de Beauvoir, launched entire fields of feminist theory by writing - one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.To be a woman, to be feminine was never purely biological, it was also societal. You are shaped into a woman, piece by piece, experience by experience.In her rejection of the arbitrariness one would often attach to what femininity means, she made space for who some would argue is very much a queer icon and a scholar.Almost half a century later, RuPaul said: weâre all born naked, and the rest is drag.It's a strange thing, watching a philosopher and a reality show host arrive at the same conclusion from opposite directions, that gender was never the given, natural thing it pretends to be, just the costume everyone's already wearing. De Beauvoir got there through existentialism. RuPaul got there through sequins. Both arrived to the conclusion that the performance was the point all along.A common practice to define drag would be to trace its historic roots in the Indian subcontinent. Women were kept out of public spaces, be it India or the West. So when women roles had to be filled in theatrical production men would dress us as them and take up that role in the public eye.India has its own unique lineage to give to this art form, be it through mythology or folk dance and other cultural performances. In the Natyashastra, men played goddesses, heroines, demonesses, styled into femininity through gesture, costume, and the trained emotionDance forms like Kathakali, Jatra and Yakshagana still carry that inheritance. These traditions though have never termed themselves as drag and only trace lineage through reductive definitions of drag being men becoming women convincingly enough to make an audience believe it.India's mythology also builds gender transformation directly into the stories being told. In the Mahabharata's Virata Parva, Arjuna spends a year of exile disguised as Brihannala, a court dancer and music teacher, cursed by the nymph Urvashi to live without his manhood after refusing her. Shikhandi was also born a woman, raised as a warrior, and eventually granted manhood by a Yaksha to fulfil a vow of vengeance against Bhishma.None of this stayed confined to myth and stage. In Ahmedabad, on the eighth night of Navratri, men of the Barot community drape themselves in saris and jewellery to dance garba. In Kottankulangara, Kerala, thousands of men dress as women each year for Chamayavilakku, offering prayers to the goddess Durga at a temple local legend says was born from a bleeding stone, with no women present at the founding moment, boys dressed as women to complete the ritual.Outside temple and epic, there is the tradition of Launda Naach, male dancers performing in women's dress at weddings, in the North Indian belt. It's argued to be India's oldest living form of vernacular drag but it shows no interest in being called "drag".Indiaâs modern drag is a celebration of the feminine inside a being, a lot of what we try to say it draws its lineage from was never a celebration. In some instances it was perversion and in most it was erasure of women from public spaces.A man performing femininity is not automatically a drag queen.The historical circumstances matter. Who was performing? Why were they performing? Who was watching? Who was excluded from the performance? And, crucially, who controlled what that performance meant?For Lush Monsoon, who was among the early generation of contemporary drag performers in Delhi, the relationship between these histories and modern drag is complicated by the question of agency.To her the art forms are exploitative, even if they are often posed as a celebration of queer history. She points to the gaze surrounding these traditions, and to the people who historically inhabit this gaze.âI always see them as an extension of that you are afraid of the feminine, so you are more okay with the masculine projecting as a feminine, and you putting their desire on that.âThe issue, she says, is not only about the audience.A lot of the participants are queer. They are queer people from marginalised sections of society or spaces where the language of queer is not defined yet somehow exploited.A younger drag queen too, who has been in this space for around one year, held the same belief. They said that India has a culture of gender intermixing, something we can draw out as a rich queer heritage but modern drag is not a direct extension of this.âThe reason that I got attracted to this form of drag, because I saw a certain amount of agency in it.âThe point is not to deny Indiaâs rich queer history but to make space for its even more vibrant present.As of today, there are only a handful of venues and spaces for drag performers. Most of the queens interviewed said Indian drag still doesn't carry the same stature as its Western counterpart, which makes it hard to find venues, build audiences, and turn performance into a sustainable career.Venues like KittySu and the Lalit chain of hotels pioneered the space, and it's now getting a push from queer collectives like the GaySi family and smaller creators trying to build safer rooms for queens and their audiences.Yet, reaching a wider audience in the digital era will take a digital push. Every queen interviewed named the same first encounter with drag as an art form: RuPaul's Drag Race. The show cemented its place in queer history, but there's a need for an Indian platform that celebrates queerness and the art form on its own terms, instead of reducing it to comedy.Older drag queens have long faced the accusation of importing a Western culture that maligns Indian heritage. But that heritage has always had space for queer stories. It was colonialism that maligned it, criminalising hijra communities and policing gender through an imported Victorian morality, codified in 1861 as Section 377, a law that stayed on the books for 157 years until the Supreme Court struck it down in 2018.Getting there took decades of work the current generation didn't have to do from scratch. Earlier drag queens fought not just for legal recognition but for the art form itself â pulling it apart from the crass, punchline version of drag Indian television has long been comfortable with.Noor Sins, a younger queen, put it simply: that fight mattered because it meant queens her age could grow up with contemporary, Indian, queer icons to look up to, not borrowed ones.It is perhaps here that the history of Indian drag and what Indian drag is becomes more interesting. In some sense drag always existed but for a lot of contemporary queens what did not exist was the ability to see themselves in the person performing it.The queens performing on stage are taking a form that has so often been used to make femininity into spectacle and making spectacle something they control. They are borrowing from the West without necessarily belonging to it, and drawing from Indian history without pretending that every man who ever wore a sari was a drag queen.The world is changing, the queens coming up now get to inherit something their predecessors had to build: a language, a community, spaces to perform, and most importantly, people who look like them already standing on a stage. But the stage has to become bigger, and the language more universal.De Beauvoir never wrote about drag. But she wrote the sentence that explains why it matters: one is not born, but becomes. For the queens performing in India today, that becoming is not simply about becoming a woman through makeup and dresses. It is about becoming visible to themselves, and then to one another, in a form that did not always give them someone to see.

World.title: Hyderabad police step up security for Milad-un-Nabi procession
World.content:
Hyderabad police are stepping up security arrangements for the Milad-un-Nabi procession scheduled to be held on August 26, with the main procession to be monitored through drones and CCTV cameras, Hyderabad City Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar said on Saturday.

The Commissioner held a coordination meeting with representatives of the Markaz-e-Milad Juloos Committee at the Telangana Integrated Command and Control Centre (TGICCC) in Banjara Hills and urged them to ensure the procession is conducted peacefully and concludes within the stipulated timeframe.

The Commissioner said the procession should begin at the scheduled time and stressed that DJs and sound systems causing excessive noise pollution would not be permitted in accordance with the Supreme Court and government regulations. He also warned that minors driving vehicles, triple-riding on motorcycles and rash driving using modified silencers would not be tolerated.

No bike rallies would be permitted before the scheduled date, he said.

With the monsoon continuing, Mr. Sajjanar asked organisers to take precautions while putting up electrical decorations and ensure flags do not come into contact with power lines. Volunteers at food distribution points were also asked to coordinate with the police to prevent traffic congestion.

During a video conference with police officials earlier, the Commissioner directed field-level personnel to work in coordination to ensure the celebrations pass off peacefully. Security measures are being strengthened in sensitive areas, while police will maintain surveillance over the procession through drones and CCTV cameras.

He said police would also keep a close watch on provocative or hateful content posted on social media and known troublemakers. Stickers are being issued in advance for vehicles participating in the procession, while a dedicated coordination WhatsApp group and helpline have been set up for emergency communication.

Additional CP (Law and Order, South Range) Tafseer Iqbal, Joint CP (Traffic) Joel Davis, DCP (Traffic-3) Rahul Hegde, DCP (Charminar) Khare Kiran Prabhakar, DCP (Rajendranagar) Srinivas, DCP (Shamshabad) Rajesh and DCP (Golconda) Raghavender Reddy attended the meeting along with representatives of the Markaz-e-Milad Juloos Committee.

World.title: Minister Bindhu Krishna promises top priority for children’s welfare
World.content:
Addressing children’s issues will be the top priority of the government, Minister for Women and Child Development Bindhu Krishna said here on Saturday. She was inaugurating the Onam celebration organised by the Department of Women and Child Development for children at Anchalummoodu Children’s Home.

Encouraging the residents to face life’s challenges with courage and confidence, the Minister assured the children that they can bring any problem directly to her attention. She added that all necessary facilities will be provided to nurture their talents, urging them to excel not only in their studies but also in extra-curricular areas such as reading, writing, painting, music, and dance.

The Minister also promised immediate intervention to resolve any deficiencies or inconveniences in the various children’s homes if brought to her notice, noting that children could also write to her directly. District Panchayat President R. Latha Devi, District Collector Annie Jula Thomas, Sub-Judge Rekha Laurel, and State Commission for Protection of Child Rights acting chairperson Sicily Joseph also spoke at the event.

World.title: Metal scrap godown gutted in Tirupattur
World.content:
A private metal scrap godown at Perumalpettai near Vaniyambadi town in Tirupattur was gutted on Saturday after a fire broke out in the facility and goods worth ₹8 lakh got destroyed.

Police said that it was around 9 a.m. when residents noticed thick smoke billowing out of the godown, which was run by K. Padmanaban, 49, a resident of Vaniyambadi. Immediately, they tried to douse the fire but the flames engulfed the entire godown.

Based on an alert, fire fighters from Vaniyambadi town rushed to the spot. But before the firemen could reach there, fire spread across the entire godown. After a few hours of hard labour, fire fighters doused the flames.

However, the entire facility got completely gutted. A case was registered by Vaniyambadi Town police. Police said that an electrical short circuit could be the reason for the accident. A probe is under way.

World.title: Telangana energy sector to complement govt. plans to achieve $3 trillion economy: Dy. CM
World.content:
HYDERABAD

The State government is strengthening the energy sector in line with its goal of transforming Telangana into a $3 trillion economy by 2047, Deputy Chief Minister M. Bhatti Vikramarka has said.

He stated that Telangana had emerged as one of the best destinations for investments and the government was committed to provide infrastructure required by the industrial sector without any shortage of power or water. He invited industries and investors from across the country to invest in Telangana in the manufacturing and services sectors.

Speaking after inaugurating Power Exhibition–2026 organised by the Southern Power Distribution Company of Telangana Ltd (TGSPDCL) here on Saturday, he said long-term plans were being formulated to anticipate future energy requirements and enhance power generation and supply capacities through thermal, solar, hydel, pumped storage and battery storage among other avenues.

The exhibition was organised to create awareness among the public, particularly students, about the achievements of the Energy Department, the reforms being introduced and the use of modern technology. He appreciated the services being rendered by employees of the power utilities stating that though their work would not always be visible, their contribution was extremely important to the development of the State, he said.

Despite a significant increase in power demand the government had been able to ensure uninterrupted power supply without difficulties, the Deputy Chief Minister said. He stated that consumer problems were being resolved quickly through the 1912 toll-free service and “Power Ambulances”.

Special Chief Secretary (Energy) Naveen Mittal, Chairman and Managing Director of TGSPDCL Jitesh V. Patil, CMDs K. Varun Reddy (TGNPDCL), D. Krishna Bhaskar (TG-Transco), other Directors and senior officials of the Southern Discom participated.

World.title: Panama-flagged cargo ship sinks in Bay of Bengal, rescue operations on
World.content:
A Panama-flagged cargo ship sank in the Bay of Bengal on Saturday (August 22, 2026), about 240 nautical miles from the Paradip coast in Odisha, officials said.

The ship, with 24 crew members on board, was heading towards Singapore carrying iron ore from Odisha, they said.

The Indian Coast Guard and Indian Navy have launched a rescue operation, they added, "We are not sure how many of the crew members have been rescued," a senior IPS officer told PTI, adding that most of the crew members were Chinese.

Other vessels in the vicinity have been alerted to assist in the rescue effort, he said.

"The ship left the Odisha coast on Friday [August 22, 2026]," the officer said.

World.title: TVK MLA booked in trespass, assault case in Puducherry
World.content:
A case has been registered against legislator belonging to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam, A. K. Sai J. Saravanan Kumar, and his associates, in connection with alleged trespass and assault of security staff of a multinational company in Puducherry.

According to the police, the legislator and his supporters barged into the premises of Whirlpool company and manhandled the security staff. The TVK MLA has been accused of threatening the company staff, the police said.

The case was registered based on a complaint filed by a senior staff of the company. The legislator has been booked under section189(2), 329(3), 296(b), 115(2), 351(2) r/w 190 of BNS, police said.

World.title: Samajwadi Party plans youth manifesto for U.P. poll; party won’t break alliances
World.content:
Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday said his party would not break alliances, asserting that its fight was against the Bharatiya Janata Party, which he accused of pursuing policies benefiting big business groups.

Addressing presspersons at the party headquarters in Lucknow, Mr. Yadav said the SP had always honoured its commitments. “The Samajwadi Party never breaks alliances. When we agree to move forward with others, we stand by them,” he said.

He said the party’s objective is to form a government committed to social justice, based on socialist ideology and solidarity with the ‘PDA’ — ‘pichhda’ (backward classes), Dalits and ‘alpsankhyak’ (minorities).

His remarks came a day after Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the SP’s definition of ‘PDA’ was constantly changing, referring to the party’s outreach to Brahmins.

Mr. Yadav also accused the State government of deliberately weakening primary education and shutting schools attended by children from disadvantaged communities.

He said an SP government would revive the model schools project initiated during its previous tenure and strengthen school infrastructure and midday meal kitchens.

Youth manifesto

The SP plans to release a separate youth manifesto for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly election, focusing on education, employability, skill development and digital learning.

Alok Ranjan, former Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary and a SP member, told The Hindu that the blueprint would propose model schools and colleges in districts, upgrading government inter-colleges, filling vacant sanctioned posts and introducing a time-bound recruitment calendar for teachers.

“It will also overhaul school and university education, with a focus on employability in changing times, besides establishing skill-development institutions and promoting digital learning,” Mr. Ranjan said.

The manifesto is also likely to propose an allowance for unemployed youth. Mr. Ranjan said the plan was “rooted in the SP’s socialist ideology”.

Mayawati seeks apology

Meanwhile, a political row erupted over Mr. Yadav’s recent remark that the SP had “turned 25 paise into a rupee” but was later abandoned by its alliance partners, an apparent reference to the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD).

Bahujan Samaj Party national president Mayawati on Saturday demanded an apology from Mr. Yadav to the RLD and the Jat community, saying the remark was “indecent” and “shameful” and had insulted the family of former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh.

RLD chief Jayant Chaudhary also criticised Mr. Yadav, saying the SP chief could have named him rather than making a reference to the Jat community. “Such behaviour only leads to downfall,” he stated in a post on X.

The remarks followed criticism by SP State president Shyam Lal Pal of an unnamed ally for abandoning the party despite its support. Mr. Yadav’s comment alluded to Mr. Chaudhary’s 2022 remark that he was not a “chavanni” who could be easily flipped.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: MSME products from Puducherry to be identified under PONFAIT brand name
World.content:
The Pondicherry Industrial Promotion Development and Investment Corporation Limited in association with Entrepreneurship Development Institute of India (EDII) has launched PONFAIT, a new brand identity for products and enterprises from Puducherry under the Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP) Scheme.

The brand name PONFAIT and its logo were released at a function held in Puducherry by the Lieutenant Governor K. Kailashnathan and Chief Minister N. Rangasamy. The launch forms part of the ‘Made in Puducherry,’ initiative, which seeks to recognise, promote and celebrate the valuable contributions of MSMEs across Puducherry, a release here said.

The launch of PONFAIT marks the beginning of a collective branding initiative aimed at bringing the diverse products, services, and enterprises of Puducherry under a recognisable identity. The initiative seeks to strengthen the visibility of local MSMEs, promote their products and create greater market opportunities, the release said.

The ‘Made in Puducherry’ initiative encompasses a wide range of sectors, including coastal tourism and allied sectors, fisheries and marine industry, pharmaceuticals and medical sector, textile and apparel, handicrafts and handlooms, manufacturing and small industries, woodcrafts, traditional food products manufacturing, masonry art and sculptures, the release said.

The launch event held near Gandhi Thidal was attended by Industries Minister Malladi Krishna Rao, Raj Bhavan MLA Vignesh Kannan, Chief Secretary Sharat Chauhan, Secretary to Government, Industries, Vikranth Raja and Director General of EDII Sunil Shukla, the release said.

World.title: Govt blames PTI for 'violating' SC order, says family committed contempt by issuing statements
World.content:
The government on Saturday blamed the PTI for “violating” a Supreme Court (SC) order by issuing statements and speaking to the media following former prime minister Imran Khan’s medical check-up at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) on Friday.

“PML-N believes that health issues should not be used for political gain,” Information Minister Attaullah Tarar told the media.

He added that, whether in opposition or in government, the PML-N’s stance had always remained the same: politics and health issues should not be linked.

The minister also accused Imran of issuing statements and releasing videos about the health of PML-N leaders when they were incarcerated and he was prime minister.

Tarar added that since the SC order regarding Imran’s health was issued, “our government has not mocked him or made any controversial statements”.

Recounting events of the past few days, Tarar said that after the SC order was issued, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar had explained the government’s position on it in detail.

“The viewpoint was that whatever will happen, it will be according to the law,” Tarar said.

He added that the government’s review petition “respectfully questioned whether the facility was available to every prisoner”. Secondly, he said, the petition questioned whether the law and Constitution allowed Imran to be examined at a private hospital.

Tarar then elaborated on the implementation of the SC’s order.

“The next question is whether the order was implemented. The answer is yes. Was the check-up conducted? Yes. Was it done transparently? Yes. Was his sister present? Yes. Were doctors from Shifa [Hospital] present? Yes. All the obligations were fulfilled.”

Tarar also addressed the communication of these developments to the media and the general public. He said that shortly after the government filed its review petition, the law minister had explained its grounds in detail.

He added that after Imran’s check-up was completed at Pims, he himself posted an update on X.

Tarar said he was “surprised” by the PTI’s subsequent statements and actions. “PTI is miles away from the light of knowledge,” he said, adding that the party would not have filed a contempt petition had it been aware of the situation.

“A baseless contempt petition has been filed.”

The facts were shared with the public immediately, he said, adding that the government had maintained transparency throughout.

“Contempt has definitely happened,” he said, adding that the SC had directed that no political motives should be involved in the medical check-up. However, Tarar said, people gathered outside Shifa Hospital, created social media content and removed barriers.

“Wasn’t it the PTI that did this? Didn’t they violate the court order?”

He added that the PTI had also issued statements and spoken at press conferences.

“If somebody is in contempt, it is Imran Khan’s sister and his party.
